jobs.title: Senior Data Engineer (Databricks)
jobs.excerpt: At Livefront, we help companies design and build world-class digital products that command attention and inspire joy.
jobs.description:
At Livefront, we help companies design and build world-class digital products that command attention and inspire joy. We’ve helped household names like CVS, Samsung, General Mills, and Optum create experiences that have reached millions of people, and startups like HomeSpotter and Credly build entirely new businesses that challenge their industries’ status quo.
We're looking for an outstanding Senior Databricks Data Engineer to join our growing data practice — someone who builds the data and AI foundations that digital products and intelligent experiences run on. This is a senior-level position with the opportunity to work remotely inPeru.

Who you are

You are a Databricks-focused Data Engineer who understands that great data platforms are only as valuable as the products, AI workflows, and experiences they enable. You bring deep, production-grade expertise across the Databricks platform and know how to connect platform capabilities to real business outcomes.

You thrive in ambiguity and can quickly assess a client's data landscape to recommend and implement the right solutions. You understand that in consulting, your Databricks depth is most valuable when it connects platform capabilities to the products and experiences clients actually use — and you're as comfortable in a product design conversation as you are building a DLT pipeline.

You excel at translating complex data challenges into clear technical requirements and can confidently navigate conversations with everyone from data scientists to executives. Your engineering principles are mature and grounded in real-world experience across various industries and scales.

You have an interest in and a curiosity about data platforms and the latest advances in data technology.

What you will be doing

  • Design and build production data pipelines using Lakeflow Declarative Pipelines, Autoloader, and Structured Streaming, with end-to-end ownership of ingestion, transformation, data quality expectations, and CI/CD deployment via Declarative Automation Bundles.
  • Architect and implement Lakehouse solutions on Databricks — medallion architecture, Delta Lake, Unity Catalog — tailored to the client's analytics, AI, and application needs.
  • Build and maintain Databricks transformation layers — DLT pipelines, PySpark notebooks, and dbt — with data quality constraints and SLAs baked in.
  • Design and maintain the data and AI foundations — Unity Catalog, Feature Store, MLflow, and Model Serving — that power production ML, agent workflows, and AI-enabled digital products.
  • Collaborate with product and backend engineers to design data models, APIs, and application data contracts — ensuring the platform serves the product, not just the warehouse.
  • Consult with clients to understand their data challenges, develop data strategies, and implement sustainable solutions.
  • Adapt your approach based on project needs — sometimes leading data architecture discussions with clients, other times supporting internal teams with specialized data expertise.
  • Work within multi-cloud environments — primarily AWS and Azure — anchoring data platform recommendations around Databricks where it fits the client's architecture and goals.
  • Champion data governance through Unity Catalog — access control, lineage, data quality policies, and compliance — as a first-class part of every engagement, not an afterthought.
  • Design data-to-application architectures — including Lakebase-backed services and Databricks Apps — that connect governed data to AI workflows, digital products, and user-facing experiences.
  • Help build Livefront's Databricks practice — contributing to accelerators, internal enablement, certification goals, and Databricks partner go-to-market materials alongside delivery work.

Why you should apply

  • You want to work with passionate and talented people who are always looking for ways to make things better.
  • You desire a work environment where respect, mutual trust, and egoless collaboration are paramount.
  • You want colleagues who take their work seriously but not themselves, and who know how to let loose and have a good time.
  • You like being part of a team with a reputation for excellence that gives back to the community by educating, mentoring, and sponsoring.
  • You want to work on products and accounts that have outsized impact and reach.
  • You believe in sweating the details, giving a damn about quality, and taking pride in going the extra mile.
  • You want to help build a data practice specialization from the ground up — shaping how we go to market with Databricks, what we build as accelerators, and what it means to do this kind of work at a digital product company.

What you bring to the table

  • 5-8+ years of data engineering experience with at least 4 years in production Databricks environments, preferably in a consulting or client delivery context.
  • Solid working knowledge of AWS and Azure cloud services relevant to Databricks deployments — storage, networking, IAM, and compute — with GCP familiarity a plus.
  • Deep, production-grade Databricks expertise: Lakeflow Declarative Pipelines, Autoloader, Structured Streaming, Lakeflow Jobs, Unity Catalog (including fine-grained access control and lineage) — demonstrated through shipped production workloads, not prototypes.
  • Proven experience designing Lakehouse architectures — medallion patterns, Delta Lake table design, partitioning, Z-ordering, and query optimization — at production scale.
  • Hands-on experience with data pipeline testing, observability, and CI/CD for data — including unit testing, data quality frameworks, and version-controlled deployments via Git and Declarative Automation Bundles.
  • Strong proficiency in SQL and Python, with the ability to write clean, performant, and maintainable code.
  • Understanding of data modeling, schema design, and query optimization.
  • Excellent communication skills with the ability to explain complex data concepts to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Strong problem-solving skills with the ability to navigate ambiguous requirements and deliver pragmatic solutions.
  • Above-average discipline and personal organization skills.
  • Obvious comfort with critique and peer review in the context of an iterative development process.
  • A demonstrated hunger for personal and professional growth.
  • A self-evident love and care for the craft of data engineering.

Bonus points if you…

  • Have worked with real-time streaming technologies (Kafka, Kinesis, etc.).
  • Have hands-on experience with alternative cloud data platforms — useful context for migrations and competitive assessments, though Databricks is our primary platform focus.
  • Have experience in healthcare or fintech domains.
  • Have hands-on experience with MLOps or LLMOps on Databricks — MLflow experiment tracking, model registry, Model Serving endpoints, or Vector Search for RAG pipelines.
  • Have experience with Java, Go, or Scala.
  • Have strong illustration skills for technical diagramming and data architecture documentation.
  • Speak, write, and/or educate publicly about data engineering topics.
  • Have contributed to open-source data projects.
  • Hold or are actively pursuing a Databricks certification (Data Engineer Associate or Professional, or Apache Spark Developer) — we treat these as meaningful signals of platform depth, and they directly support our Databricks partner growth goals.
  • Have experience with Databricks Apps, or Lakebase — early familiarity with where the Databricks platform is heading is a strong differentiator.

What to expect

When applying, please include a short note about yourself, a summary of your work experience, and a link to any public profiles you actively maintain (e.g., GitHub, LinkedIn, etc).
Our hiring process moves quickly and consists of several stages for candidates who capture our attention with their initial submission, sometimes including but not limited to a short preliminary phone interview, a series of video interviews, and a short take-home exercise, which you'll have up to a week to complete.

Additional information

We go out of our way to evaluate all employees and job applicants equally based on merit, competence, and qualifications. We encourage candidates from all backgrounds to apply and consider all qualified applicants. Don't worry, every application will be reviewed by a human.

jobs.title: Senior Director, Partner Data
jobs.excerpt: Risepoint is an education technology company that helps regional universities launch and grow online programs for modern learners.
jobs.description:
Risepoint is an education technology company that helps regional universities launch and grow online programs for modern learners. Risepoint supports more than 100 universities and colleges across five countries, with programs concentrated in high-demand fields including nursing, healthcare, teaching, business, technology, and public service. Our suite of products and services supports the full student journey and each university’s long-term goals. Together, we increase access to affordable education that delivers a strong return on investment for learners and meets employer and community needs. Learn more at risepoint.com.


The Impact You Will Make

Risepoint's Partner Data organization is the operational backbone connecting more than 100 university partners to accurate, timely student and program data. We are seeking a Senior Director, Partner Data Integrations & Operations to lead this organization through its next stage: Reshaping two dedicated teams - Partner Data Operations and Partner Data Enablement, so day-to-day case resolution and forward-looking partner enablement each run to a higher standard.

In this role, you will lead a team who resolve partner data issues, run the recurring processes that keep partner systems in sync, and deliver new partner launches and relaunches. You will transform the team into a Partner Data Integrations & Operations team that runs disciplined, well-governed case management and monitoring, and a Partner Enablement Data team that gets ahead of partner needs - owning onboarding, relaunches, and acting as the systems subject matter expert for partner data integrations. Across both teams, you will instill a product mindset - ensuring day-to-day issue resolution and partner enablement work continually surface and drive broader improvements to Risepoint's partner data products and integrations, not just close individual cases.

The ideal candidate pairs technical fluency in SIS systems and integrations with hands-on operations leadership, ideally built in ed-tech, higher education, or another partner-based, data-intensive environment. This person can read a data flow as comfortably as they can run a case-management queue, and can operate with real autonomy while keeping cross-functional partners - Enterprise Data, Partner Support, Student Success Center, and CRM - aligned.

How You Will Bring Our Mission to Life

What You Will Do

  • Build the operating model, leadership capability, and standards for the Partner Data Operations team - defining how partner data cases are triaged and resolved, and how monitoring and reconciliation work keeps partner systems accurate and reliable
  • Set clear service-level standards and escalation rules for the Partner Data Integrations & Operations team, collaborating with Enterprise Data, Partner Support, SSC, and CRM, replacing today's informal, case-by-case routing.
  • Drive automation and process redesign to cut repeat, low-judgment case volume and free the team for higher-value work.
  • Instill and enforce a product mindset across the organization, ensuring that case resolution and monitoring work routinely surfaces patterns and root causes that translate into broader improvements to partner data systems and integrations, not just one-off fixes.
  • Stand up Data Integration Engineering to work directly with partner SIS systems (Slate, Banner, Workday, and others), producing a repeatable integration playbook per system rather than one-off, person-dependent builds.
  • Serve as the strategic advisor partner-facing technical lead for new partner onboarding, engaging directly with partner IT and SIS teams from day one to scope integrations, unblock technical issues, and set the relationship up as a strong technical partnership rather than a handoff
  • Grow the Partner Enablement Data team into the go-to subject matter expert on partner systems, data, and workflows, bringing that expertise, and a product mindset, into every partner engagement so the team can advise Partner Management and partners directly on how Risepoint's products should integrate for a successful partnership.
  • Champion the architectural fixes that tooling can't replace to shape the cross-functional roadmap and priorities for partner data architecture, aligning Partner, Data, Product, and Technology leaders around enterprise-wide solutions, turning structural gaps into system enhancements and architectural improvements that go beyond what validation and tooling alone can fix.
  • Own the partner data strategy - setting priorities, investment choices, and trade-offs across the Partner Data Integrations & Operations and Partner Enablement Data teams, including owning validation and monitoring tooling (such as an Agentic AI validation tool) and standardizing file formats, data mapping, and integrations across a partner portfolio that today runs on multiple legacy systems with no single standard.
  • Lead, hire, and develop Partner Data Integrations & Operations organization across two teams; report on case trends, launch progress, and team performance to senior leadership, and own the KPI scorecard for partner data operations.
  • Operate autonomously with minimal oversight, proactively identifying issues and driving solutions, and influence decisions across the organization using data-driven reasoning, storytelling, and a strong executive presence.

What Success Looks Like

  • Partner data cases are resolved quickly and consistently against clear service-level targets, improving the partner and student experience.
  • New partner launches and relaunches run on a repeatable playbook and go live on time, without depending on any one person.
  • A capable Partner Enablement Data team is established and recognized as the systems expert for partner data integrations.
  • Partner data is treated as a strategic differentiator, not just a support function, opportunities such as richer application-form and retention data are identified and pursued to improve partner business outcomes, beyond fixing what's broken.
  • New partners experience includes integrations & operations team as a direct, hands-on partner during onboarding, not just a backend resource.

How Impact Will be Measured

  • Case volume, resolution time, and incident rate for partner data issues trend down, with clear SLAs defined and met.
  • New partner launches and relaunches hit target go-live dates at a high rate, using a documented, repeatable process.
  • Manual, repeat case volume drops through automation, and partner satisfaction with data support improves
  • Product and system improvement ideas surfaced from case and partner-enablement work are tracked, prioritized, and shipped, with a measurable reduction in partner-specific workarounds as upstream product gaps close.

What You’ll Bring to the Team

Experience That Matters Most

  • 8+ years leading data operations, technical support, or partner/customer success teams, including at least 3 years managing managers or multiple teams. (Must have)
  • Technical fluency with data systems (snowflake, databricks) and integrations (file feeds, SFTP, APIs) and CRM platforms such as Salesforce, comfortable going deep with engineering and data teams. (Must have)
  • Experience in ed-tech, higher education, or another partner-based, data-intensive industry. (Must have)
  • Experience with SIS systems such as Slate, Banner, Workday, and others (Must have)
  • Comfort as the client-facing point of contact on technical onboarding conversations, not just an internal operator.
  • A track record of building or restructuring an operations team, setting up intake, case management, and service-level standards. (Must have)

Experience That’s Great to Have

  • Background in partner onboarding, implementation, or customer launch and migration management.
  • Familiarity with Agile or Jira-based work management (epics, sprints, backlog prioritization).
  • Prior experience partnering with Enterprise Data or engineering teams on system enhancements and data-quality initiatives.
  • Experience partnering with Product teams to translate operational or partner pain points into product requirements, with comfort operating with a product mindset in an operations seat.

Risepoint is an equal-opportunity employer and supports a diverse and inclusive workforce.

Visual Designer

College Board – AP & I

Location: This is a remote role. Candidates who live near CB offices have the option of being fully remote or hybrid (Tuesday and Wednesday in office). All CB employees are required to occasionally travel to meet in person for business purposes.

Role Type: This is a full-time position


About the Team

The Advanced Placement team supports College Board in serving more than seven million students a year as they prepare for a successful transition to college through programs and services in college readiness and college success — speciﬁcally through the Advanced Placement (AP) Program. With more than 40 courses in a variety of subject areas, we are committed to promoting innovation, equity, and excellence for generations of students.


The AP Design team is a small in-house team focused on delivering high-impact, brand-aligned creative solutions. Partnering closely with internal stakeholders, we translate business goals into functional user-centered design across print and digital channels. Our team combines strategic thinking with hands-on execution to ensure consistency, quality, and efficiency at every stage of the creative process.

About the Opportunity

As a Visual Designer, you have a love for design and an attention to detail in everything you touch. You’re interested in learning more about the craft of design, trying new things, and are open to working on any type of project. We’re looking for someone who can work independently, communicate regularly with autonomy over their projects, and support our design goals. You are comfortable creating and editing design files across many channels – print, digital, presentations, email, marketing, and video. You seek finesse in all projects, taking pride in your work ethic and delivery of excellent creative assets. If you are adaptable, service-oriented, and dedicated to being an advocate for our audiences through great design, then we want to work with you.



In this role, you will:

Conceptualize and Design (80%)

  • Develop and deliver consistent and high-quality design solutions for organizational campaigns and initiatives that are aligned to brand standards – this may include print, digital, email, products, and event graphics.
  • Work on an array of PowerPoint presentations for a variety of internal stakeholders.
  • Implement established best practices in marketing, including information design, social media, and other emerging strategies.
  • Manage all phases of an assignment from concept through completion, including design development and digital file preparation.
  • Maintain and organize design files, templates, and shared assets to support team efficiency.
  • Ensure accessibility standards are incorporated across all materials.
  • Support vendor coordination and production processes, including print specifications and quality control reviews.
  • Contribute to workflow improvements that help refine internal creative processes to increase output quality.

Communicate, Collaborate, and Adapt (20%)

  • Communicate with all team members to ensure timely delivery of design artifacts.
  • Work effectively with cross-functional teams, while navigating and adjusting to shifting priorities.
  • Build trust and strong working relationships with internal stakeholders.
  • Clearly articulate design ideas and rationale, present work confidently to stakeholders, and actively listen and incorporate feedback

About You

  • A portfolio of your work included in your application.
  • A BFA in graphic design, along with a minimum of 4–6 years of hands-on experience in design and production.
  • An understanding of visual design systems, hierarchy, typography, aesthetics, illustration, iconography, photography, data visualization, interaction, and composition.
  • An appetite for problem solving, while thriving in fast-paced environments.
  • Sharp design sensibilities and keen attention to detail, with experience crafting custom design specifications.
  • Openness to take on any project, no matter size or medium, with the ability to jump from one project to another, based on priorities and workload.
  • Affinity for problem solving and being a team player.
  • High understanding of industry standard design tools, such as Adobe Creative Suite and Figma.
  • Deep knowledge of Microsoft Office products, including advanced-level skills using PowerPoint, designing templates, master slides, and more. Experience working with Adobe After Effects, in animated media, or motion graphics a bonus, but not required.
  • The ability to travel 3–6 times a year to College Board offices or on behalf of College Board business.

All roles at College Board require:

  • A passion for expanding educational and career opportunities and mission-driven work
  • Curiosity and enthusiasm for emerging technologies, with a willingness to experiment with and adopt new AI-driven solutions and comfort with learning and applying new digital tools independently and proactively.
  • Clear and concise communication skills, written and verbal
  • A learner's mindset and a commitment to growth: welcoming diverse perspectives, giving and receiving timely, respectful feedback, and continuously improving through iterative learning and user input.
  • A drive for impact and excellence: solving complex problems, making data-informed decisions, prioritizing what matters most, and continuously improving through learning, user input, and external benchmarking.
  • A collaborative and empathetic approach: working across differences, fostering trust, and contributing to a culture of shared success
  • Authorization to work in the United States


About Our Process

  • Application review will begin immediately and will continue until the position is filled. This role is expected to accept applications for a minimum of 5 business days.
  • While the hiring process may vary, it generally includes: resume and application submission, recruiter phone/video screen, hiring manager interview, performance exercise such as live coding, a panel interview, a conversation with leadership and reference checks.

What We Offer

At College Board, we offer more than a paycheck- we provide a meaningful career, a supportive team, and a comprehensive package designed to help you thrive. We’re a self-sustaining nonprofit that believes in fair and competitive compensation grounded in your qualifications, experience, impact, and the market.


A Thoughtful Approach to Compensation

  • The hiring range for this role is $64,000-$100,000
  • Your exact salary will depend on your location, experience, and how your background compares to others in similar roles at the College Board.
  • We aim to make our best offer upfront, rooted in fairness, transparency, and market data.
  • We adjust salaries by location to ensure fairness, no matter where you live.

You’ll have open, transparent conversations about compensation, benefits, and what it’s like to work at College Board throughout your hiring process. Check out our careers page for more.

Responsible for leading the enterprise strategy, development, and delivery of data, analytics, artificial intelligence, and intelligent automation solutions that drive measurable business outcomes. Enterprise Data & AI Strategy: Develop and execute enterprise data, analytics, and AI strategies aligned with business objectives, regulatory requirements, and technology priorities. Data Engineering & Data Products: Lead enterprise data engineering, modern cloud data platforms, data architecture, and reusable data products. Drive scalable, secure, and integrated data solutions that support business operations, analytics, digital capabilities, and AI adoption.

Data Governance & Quality: Establish enterprise data governance frameworks, standards, and accountability for data quality, security, privacy, metadata, lineage, and master data management. Partner with business and risk leaders to ensure regulatory compliance and trusted enterprise data.

Artificial Intelligence & Intelligent Automation: Partner with application teams on the development, implementation, and adoption of enterprise AI, machine learning, generative AI, and intelligent automation solutions. Education

Experience

jobs.description:
We are seeking a highly organised, proactive, and detail-oriented Personal Assistant to provide comprehensive administrative support, including diary and email management, billing, invoicing, and basic financial administration.

The successful candidate will be responsible for managing day-to-day administrative tasks, coordinating schedules, handling correspondence, preparing invoices, maintaining financial records, and supporting the smooth and efficient operation of the business.

The ideal candidate will have excellent organisational and communication skills, strong attention to detail, and the ability to manage multiple priorities while maintaining confidentiality and professionalism.

Key Responsibilities

1. Diary and Email Management

  • Manage calendars, appointments, meetings, and schedules.
  • Coordinate meetings, prepare agendas where required, and ensure appointments are scheduled efficiently.
  • Monitor and manage incoming emails, prioritise correspondence, and draft or respond to routine communications.
  • Follow up on outstanding emails, action items, and pending requests.
  • Arrange travel, accommodation, and other logistical requirements when necessary.
  • Maintain an organised schedule and proactively identify and resolve scheduling conflicts.

2. Billing and Invoicing

  • Prepare, issue, and distribute invoices accurately and within agreed timelines.
  • Verify billing information, rates, quantities, and supporting documentation before issuing invoices.
  • Maintain accurate billing records and update invoice trackers or financial spreadsheets.
  • Monitor outstanding invoices and assist with payment follow-ups.
  • Liaise with clients, suppliers, and internal teams regarding billing queries and discrepancies.
  • Assist with preparing statements, expense summaries, and other billing-related reports.
  • Ensure invoices and supporting documents are properly filed and readily accessible.

3. Basic Financial Administration

  • Maintain and update financial records, spreadsheets, and administrative databases.
  • Record and track business expenses, receipts, payments, and reimbursements.
  • Assist with accounts payable and accounts receivable administration.
  • Reconcile invoices, receipts, and payment records against available documentation.
  • Assist in monitoring expenses and maintaining basic budget trackers.
  • Prepare routine financial summaries and reports for management review.
  • Support the preparation and organisation of documents required for bookkeeping and accounting.
  • Liaise with accountants, bookkeepers, or finance teams to resolve routine administrative queries.
  • Handle financial information confidentially and ensure records are maintained accurately.

4. General Administrative Support

  • Provide day-to-day administrative assistance to management and other team members.
  • Prepare, format, and maintain documents, reports, presentations, and correspondence.
  • Maintain organised electronic filing systems and document records.
  • Manage office supplies, administrative requests, and other operational tasks as required.
  • Coordinate communications with clients, suppliers, and other stakeholders.
  • Assist with data entry, record keeping, and updating internal systems.
  • Track deadlines, follow up on outstanding tasks, and ensure administrative activities are completed on time.
  • Undertake other reasonable administrative duties as required by the business.

Requirements

Required Qualifications and Experience

  • Previous experience as a Personal Assistant, Executive Assistant, Administrative Assistant, Office Administrator, or in a similar role.
  • Practical experience in billing, invoice preparation, and basic financial administration.
  • Experience managing calendars, appointments, email correspondence, and business communications.
  • Good understanding of basic accounts payable and accounts receivable processes.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly Outlook, Word, and Excel, or equivalent productivity tools.
  • Experience maintaining spreadsheets, financial trackers, and administrative records.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Excellent organisational skills and attention to detail.
  • Ability to manage multiple tasks, prioritise workloads, and meet deadlines.
  • High level of professionalism and discretion when handling confidential business and financial information.

Preferred Qualifications and Experience

  • Relevant qualifications or training in business administration, finance, accounting, or a related field.
  • Experience supporting senior management, business owners, or executives.
  • Familiarity with accounting and invoicing software such as Xero, QuickBooks, Sage, or similar platforms.
  • Experience preparing financial reports, expense summaries, and payment tracking records.
  • Familiarity with cloud-based document management, scheduling, and task management systems.
  • Experience working independently in a fast-paced or remote working environment.

Role Summary

Nuuly is searching for a DevOps Engineer to join our growing Platform Engineering team. We are looking for a candidate who will build and maintain features to enhance our systems, as well as serve as a deeply technical guide to our business team as they adopt features built by all engineering teams. Your goal will be to allow for seamless scalability of our production infrastructure and apply your technical expertise to help preclude growth concerns before they occur.

In this role, you will have the opportunity to build a breadth of experience with Kubernetes, Kafka, and Google Cloud Platform (GCP). As a DevOps Engineer, you will be responsible for designing, implementing, and maintaining our cloud infrastructure on GCP and managing containerized applications using Kubernetes. The ideal candidate should have more than 3 years of hands-on experience in DevOps practices, with a strong emphasis on GCP services and Kubernetes orchestration, and some experience in asynchronous message brokers (like Kafka & RabbitMQ). You will play a crucial role in optimizing our cloud environment and streamlining our development and deployment processes. This role will impact Nuuly's overall success and growth, driving our scalability, reliability, and efficiency.

Role Responsibilities

A typical week at Nuuly in this role may involve:

  • Design, implement, and manage scalable and highly available cloud infrastructure on Google Cloud Platform, including Compute Engine, Kubernetes Engine, Cloud Storage, Cloud Networking, and Confluent Kafka.
  • Collaborate with software development teams to establish efficient CI/CD pipelines, ensuring smooth and automated application deployments.
  • Implement monitoring, logging, and alerting solutions to maintain the health, performance, and security of the cloud infrastructure.
  • Collaborate with our engineering team to optimize our Kafka message broker to support our event-driven architecture and enhance system performance.
  • Work with cross-functional teams to identify and address performance bottlenecks and optimize the overall system performance.
  • Ensure the security of the cloud infrastructure and applications, implementing best practices and staying up-to-date with the latest security threats and mitigations.
  • Collaborate with developers to troubleshoot and resolve issues related to infrastructure, deployments, and applications.
  • Develop and maintain documentation for the infrastructure, deployment processes, and troubleshooting guides.
  • Stay informed about the latest trends and advancements in cloud technologies, Kubernetes, and DevOps practices, and propose relevant improvements to our infrastructure.

Role Qualifications

Qualifications

  • More than 3 years of hands-on experience as a DevOps Engineer, with a strong focus on cloud infrastructure.
  • Knowledge of streaming data and distributed systems design with asynchronous message brokers like Kafka.
  • Familiarity with infrastructure-as-code tools like Terraform, Ansible, or Deployment Manager.
  • Excellent problem-solving and analytical skills.
  • Strong communication and teamwork abilities.

Job Skills

  • Designing and managing cloud infrastructure on GCP; including virtual machines, storage, networking, and IAM.
  • Managing Kubernetes deployment, monitoring, scaling, and troubleshooting.
  • Maintaining our CI/CD pipelines with GCP and GitHub Actions.
  • Understanding of essential Kafka components like Zookeeper, Brokers, and optimization of Kafka client applications (Producers/Consumers).
  • Proficiency in YAML and experience with writing structured configuration files for infrastructure management and application deployment.
  • Proficiency in scripting languages such as Python, Bash, or Shell.
  • Strong understanding of containerization and orchestration concepts.
  • Knowledge of cloud security best practices and compliance standards.

jobs.excerpt: As a result of the combination of the BD Biosciences and Diagnostic Solutions business with Waters Corporation (NYSE: WAT), by applying to this role, you will be applying for a position with Waters.
jobs.description:
As a result of the combination of the BD Biosciences and Diagnostic Solutions business with Waters Corporation (NYSE: WAT), by applying to this role, you will be applying for a position with Waters. Waters is a global leader in life sciences, dedicated to accelerating the benefits of pioneering science through analytical technologies, informatics, and service. With a focus on regulated, high-volume testing environments, Waters’ innovative portfolio harnesses deep scientific expertise across biology, chemistry, and physics. Waters collaborates with analytical laboratories around the world to advance the release of effective, high-quality medicines, assure the safety of food and water, and drive better patient outcomes by detecting diseases earlier, managing routine infections, and combatting growing antibiotic resistance. Through a shared culture of relentless innovation, Waters’ passionate team of approximately 16,000 colleagues partner with customers to turn scientific challenges into breakthroughs that improve lives worldwide.

We are the people who give possibilities purpose

BD is one of the largest global medical technology companies in the world. Advancing the world of health™ is our Purpose, and it’s no small feat. It takes the imagination and passion of all of us—from design and engineering to the manufacturing and marketing of our billions of MedTech products per year—to look at the impossible and find transformative solutions that turn dreams into possibilities.

Job Description

Summary


We are seeking a Senior Product Cyber Security Engineer to own the cybersecurity deliverables for assigned products end to end and to build the automation that lets a small team cover a large portfolio. You will plan the security activities for each release, lead threat modeling, run composition and static analysis, produce and monitor Software Bills of Materials (SBOMs), coordinate penetration tests, and write the documentation that goes into our design history files, regulatory submissions and customer assurance packages.


This is a product security engineering role, not an IT security, SOC or penetration testing role. You will read code, work in build pipelines, and defend your risk assessments in front of auditors, regulators and customers. You will work daily with R&D, Software Engineering, DevOps, Systems Engineering, Quality and Regulatory Affairs, and with our corporate product security and cyber risk teams.


This position is remote within the United States, with regular overlap with Pacific time working hours.


Key Responsibilities

Product Cybersecurity Planning and Deliverables

  • Own the cybersecurity plan and the Product Security Management Plan for assigned products, covering new development, major releases and sustaining changes, in line with our product cybersecurity procedures.
  • Produce the required deliverable set for each product: product security requirements gap analysis, threat model and data flow map, Product Security White Paper, Incident and Vulnerability Management Plan, Patch Management Plan, Cybersecurity Risk Summary Report, and third-party vendor assessments.
  • Decide with the team which deliverables apply to each product, scale them to the product's risk and regulatory status (research-use-only versus IVD), and document every exemption with its justification.
  • Keep the Product Security Management File complete, traceable and ready for FDA inspections and notified-body audits.

Threat Modeling and Risk Assessment

  • Lead STRIDE-based threat modeling sessions with product teams: assets, data flows, trust boundaries, threats, controls, and the risk register entries that result.
  • Assess products against our product security requirements, score findings with CVSS, and work with R&D on remediation or documented risk acceptance.
  • Document unresolved and accepted risks in the Cybersecurity Risk Summary Report that supports release decisions, and feed cybersecurity hazards into the product risk management file where patient safety is affected.

Security Testing, SBOM and Vulnerability Management

  • Run static code analysis and software composition analysis (e.g., Snyk) on product releases, triage findings with engineering, and archive the reports.
  • Generate and validate CycloneDX SBOMs from the actual release artifacts of every software-enabled product, integrate SBOM generation into build and release pipelines, and load SBOMs into our post-market vulnerability monitoring tool (e.g., CyBeats).
  • Monitor post-market vulnerability reports against product SBOMs, assess impact with R&D, and drive remediation within the timelines our procedures set.
  • Coordinate penetration tests with our corporate product security engineering team: define scope from the roadmap, schedule tests early in development and before submissions, evaluate results and assess mitigations.
  • Support investigation of externally reported vulnerabilities and potential cybersecurity complaints together with our corporate cyber risk team.

Patch Management and Secure Baselines

  • Maintain product Patch Management Plans and author or review Security Patch Verification Protocols and Reports.
  • Deliver the annual operating system patch verification bulletins for IVD products in the patch verification program.
  • Contribute to hardened Windows 11 baseline images for instrument workstations and to the process for managing product-level exceptions.

Customer and Regulatory Assurance

  • Assemble cyber assurance packages for key customers (SBOMs, Product Security White Papers, penetration test attestations, SOC 2 summaries) and answer customer security questionnaires.
  • Prepare the cybersecurity content of regulatory submissions (FDA premarket cybersecurity requirements, EU IVDR) and support internal reviews, audits and regulator interactions.
  • Review third-party security checklists and SOC 2 reports for third-party software and services used in or with our products.

Automation, Metrics and Scaling

  • Build and maintain scripts and pipeline steps that generate SBOMs, scan results and audit evidence automatically, so deliverables stay current with every release instead of being rebuilt by hand.
  • Produce cross-portfolio security risk reporting and in-market risk metrics for leadership, and keep work-item tracking for security activities current.
  • Help evaluate and adopt AI-assisted tooling for drafting and checking security documentation.
  • Contribute to updates of our product security procedures and security requirements as corporate policy, FDA expectations and submission feedback evolve.

Cross-Functional Guidance

  • Act as the product security subject matter expert for R&D, DevOps, Quality, Regulatory and partner teams.
  • Provide practical guidance on secure design, secure update and installation mechanisms, vulnerability remediation and compliance expectations.
  • What Success Looks Like in the First Year
  • Within 90 days: you own the cybersecurity deliverables for one product release end to end, from the cybersecurity plan to the Cybersecurity Risk Summary Report.
  • Within six months: SBOM generation and composition analysis run automatically in the build for the products you support, with results loaded into post-market monitoring.
  • Within twelve months: you cover two to three products in parallel, penetration tests and patch verification bulletins for your products are delivered on schedule, and leadership receives regular in-market risk metrics for them.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Cybersecurity or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 10+ years of experience in software engineering, product or application security, or cybersecurity engineering, including hands-on security work on software products that shipped to customers.
  • Basic software engineering fluency: you read and write code in some language, you are comfortable with commandline, you are aware of build systems and package ecosystems (npm, pip, NuGet) and CI/CD pipelines (Azure DevOps or similar).
  • Hands-on experience with threat modeling (STRIDE or similar), vulnerability assessment, CVSS scoring, remediation workflows and risk acceptance.
  • Experience with static analysis and software composition analysis tools and with SBOM formats (CycloneDX or SPDX).
  • Experience producing formal security deliverables (threat models, risk assessments, vulnerability reports, SBOMs) that have been reviewed in audits or regulatory submissions.
  • Strong written communication: clear, structured technical documentation in English suitable for auditors, regulators and customers.
  • Demonstrated ability to run several product workstreams in parallel in a procedure-driven, documentation-heavy environment, with a bias toward automation and reuse over manual effort.

Preferred Qualifications


  • Experience in medical devices, in vitro diagnostics, life sciences or other regulated software, including familiarity with FDA premarket cybersecurity guidance (section 524B), EU MDR/IVDR, ISO 14971, AAMI TIR57, IEC 81001-5-1 or UL 2900.
  • Experience with Snyk, CyBeats or similar composition analysis and SBOM monitoring platforms, and with vulnerability scanners such as Tenable or Qualys.
  • Experience with Windows operating system hardening, image management and security patch verification.
  • Experience coordinating penetration tests and performing supplier security assessments (third-party checklists, SOC 2 report reviews).
  • Experience building security metrics, dashboards or operational reporting.
  • Experience using AI and large language model tools to accelerate documentation and analysis while keeping outputs reviewable and traceable.
  • Experience supporting FDA inspections, notified-body audits or ISO 13485 quality system audits.


Why Join Us?

To find purpose in the possibilities, we need people who can see the bigger picture, who understand the human story that underpins everything we do. We welcome people with the imagination and drive to help us reinvent the future of healthcare. At BD, you’ll discover a culture in which you can learn, grow and thrive.

jobs.description:
﻿﻿Welcome to MICE DESK

﻿

MICE DESK is the leading European company automating the sales process in the hospitality industry — and we are now expanding to the US.

Our platform, Rocket, turns event, meeting, and group inquiries into autonomous end-to- end workflows: from RFP to signed contract, across email, CRM, and PMS systems. We integrate with the systems hotels actually run on — Oracle OPERA Cloud, SIHOT, Guestline, Salesforce, Marriott's enterprise stack — which means our engineers work inside real hotel operations, not against sandbox APIs.

We are a Series A-stage company with a deliberately small team and real enterprise traction: major hotel groups across Europe run their group sales on Rocket. The people joining now shape the product, the deployment playbook, and the culture.

﻿﻿

The Role

You own engineering at MICE DESK. Fully. There is no CTO layer above you — our technical co-founder is moving into the CPO role, and engineering direction, architecture, delivery, and team are yours. You report directly to the founders.

This is a hands-on leadership role: you will lead the engineering team including our AI/Data function, own the interface to Product, and be accountable for everything that ships.

﻿

What You Will Own

1. Engineering, end-to-end. Architecture, system design, delivery against the roadmap, reliability, and technical debt. Backend, frontend, DevOps, QA, and the AI/Data team all roll up to you. You set lightweight processes that make a small team ship fast without breaking things.

2.An AI-enabled engineering pipeline. We don't just build AI products — we build with AI. You will push the engineering organization itself to be AI-native: agentic coding workflows, AI-assisted review and testing, automation of everything repetitive. A team of [10] should ship like a team of 30, and making that true is your job.

3. AI as a core system capability. Architect the integration of LLMs and agentic workflows into production systems: combining deterministic logic with AI-generated outputs, with real validation, fallback, and reliability strategies. Hospitality operations run on our platform — non-determinism is not an excuse for unreliability.

4. The team. Hire, mentor, and scale. You inherit a strong small team and grow it into a high-performance engineering organization with a culture of ownership and speed. You will also own our distributed hiring strategy [Germany + Armenia — confirm].

5.Product and business alignment. Work directly with the founders and Product. Challenge requirements, simplify complexity, and connect engineering work to outcomes: revenue, automation, customer impact. As we enter the US market, engineering has to keep pace with enterprise-scale customers on two continents.

﻿

What Success Looks Like

  • 6 months: Delivery is predictable, the AI-enabled dev pipeline is running, and the team has grown with A-players you hired.
  • 12 months: The platform scales with US enterprise customers, core systems are reliable and observable, and engineering is a competitive advantage — not a bottleneck.
    ﻿

Who You Are

﻿

Must-have

  • ﻿﻿10+ years of software engineering, 5+ in engineering leadership at high-growth product companies
  • Strong hands-on backend or full-stack background — you can still go deep
  • Proven experience scaling engineering teams at Series A–C startups
  • Strong architecture expertise: APIs, distributed systems, event-driven design, cloud
  • LLM / agentic AI systems in production — and conviction about AI-assisted engineering itself
  • Product mindset; you connect technical decisions to business outcomes

  • Comfortable with ambiguity, speed, and full accountability


﻿Nice-to-have

  • Hospitality tech, CRM, PMS, or revenue management background
  • Enterprise integration experience (Salesforce, Oracle OPERA Cloud, Microsoft Graph API)
  • Experience leading distributed/international teams

Hiring Process

  1. Intro interview — background, leadership experience, motivation
  2. Technical & leadership deep dive — architecture, system design, team scaling, AI-native development
  3. Founder interview — product vision, ownership, long-term impact

Why MICE DESK

  • Full ownership ofengineering at the European market leader, now going to the US
  • Real enterprise integrations and real-world workﬂows — not a demo product
  • A Series A company where your decisions shape the product, the architecture, and the culture

jobs.description:
Overview

HealthEdge® offers AI-powered operational infrastructure for health insurance companies, guaranteeing an enduring financial edge in an increasingly competitive market. We're experiencing strong market momentum, with a growing number of health plans choosing HealthEdge to modernize their operations and compete more effectively. As we expand, we're investing in the people who power that growth, making this a pivotal moment to join us and shape the future of healthcare technology. Learn more at HealthEdge.com.

The Healthcare IT Technical Operations Associate III (L2) owns failure handling, reprocessing, and data reconciliation across healthcare systems and workflows. The role picks up job failures, fallouts, and reprocessing requests detected and raised by L1, performs initial investigation and triage, and works alongside L3, product, and other stakeholders to drive resolution. Once a fix or instruction is available, L2 executes reprocessing and data correction hands-on. The L2 associate owns end-to-end data integrity through structured reconciliation and validation controls, and partners with L1, development, and client teams to ensure operational continuity.

As a Healthcare IT Technical Operations Associate III (L2), you will be accountable for the following:

  • Investigate and triage job failures, fallouts, and reprocessing requests raised by L1
  • Perform initial analysis using application logs, database queries, monitoring tools, and upstream/downstream dependency checks to support root cause identification
  • Work alongside L3, product, and other stakeholders to drive root cause identification and resolution, providing analysis, context, and coordination throughout
  • Execute data correction and reprocess failed or fallout records per standard procedures once a fix or instruction is available
  • Validate outcomes after reprocessing and confirm successful completion
  • Support implementation of preventive actions for recurring failures in coordination with L3 and product teams
  • Perform record count reconciliation between input and output files, tables, and messages, and detailed reconciliation beyond basic counts as defined in the runbook
  • Execute periodic reconciliations across all interfaces to ensure end-to-end data integrity
  • Timely completion of adhoc customer requests
  • Analyze and resolve record count mismatches, data mismatches, duplicates, missing transactions, and out-of-balance conditions
  • Define and enhance reconciliation control mechanisms and validation checkpoints
  • Maintain reconciliation logs and audit trails for all data correction and reprocessing activity
  • Analyze inbound and outbound interface issues across systems
  • Coordinate with external vendors, trading partners, and upstream/downstream teams for file failures, format issues, delays, and data discrepancies
  • Provide functional guidance to L1 for complex monitoring and triage scenarios
  • Review L1-raised tickets for completeness and drive faster resolution
  • Contribute to runbook and SOP updates so recurring patterns are easier for L1 to detect, report, and route
  • Publish periodic reports on reconciliation status, fallout and reprocessing volumes, and SLA performance
  • Document and communicate open reprocessing activities, pending reconciliations, and business-critical risks during shift handover
  • Identify recurring failures and support permanent fixes and process improvements
  • Recommend automation opportunities for reconciliation and monitoring activities
  • Contribute to best practices and process standardization across interfaces

This position description identifies the responsibilities and tasks typically associated with the performance of the position. Other relevant essential functions may be required.

What You Need:

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field
  • Minimum 3-4 years of experience in application support, technical operations, or production support roles
  • Experience with healthcare platforms such as HealthEdge, Facets, or QNXT
  • Experience with healthcare data formats such as EDI X12 (270/271, 276/277, 834, 835, 837)
  • Ability to clearly communicate with external customers
  • Experience with production monitoring tools for investigation and support
  • Experience with ITSM tools such as Jira or ServiceNow
  • Hands-on experience with SQL for data validation, log analysis, and reconciliation queries
  • Solid understanding of incident management, SLA tracking, and escalation processes
  • Strong analytical skills with attention to detail
  • Familiarity with monitoring tools such as Dynatrace
  • Basic scripting knowledge for log review or automation
  • Awareness of ITIL practices
  • Understanding of US healthcare workflows including claims processing, member enrollment, and provider interactions
  • Familiarity with HIPAA compliance and healthcare data security standards

Geographic Responsibility: Remote, US

Type of Employment: Full-time, permanent

Work Environment: The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job: 

  • The employee is occasionally required to move around the office. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus.
  • Work across multiple time zones in a hybrid or remote work environment.
  • Long periods of time sitting and/or standing in front of a computer using video technology.
  • May require travel dependent on company needs.

The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of the job being performed by the individual(s) assigned to this position. They are not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities, and skills required. HealthEdge reserves the right to modify, add, or remove duties and to assign other duties as necessary. In addition, reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of this position in compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990. Candidates may be required to go through a pre-employment criminal background check.

HealthEdge is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to workforce diversity and actively encourage all qualified persons to seek employment with us, including, but not limited to, racial and ethnic minorities, women, veterans and persons with disabilities.

Purpose of the Role

Reporting directly to the Manager of Development Data, the Development Data & Systems Analyst is a critical technical role responsible for optimizing, maintaining, and innovating within the Foundation’s Salesforce CRM ecosystem. As the Foundation expands its Principal Gifts function, this role ensures our data architecture, donor recognition tracking, and reporting pipelines run with peak efficiency.

The Analyst serves as the primary technical lead for the Development division's internal data ticketing system, fulfilling custom report requests, troubleshooting user issues, and delivering technical support to frontline fundraisers. Additionally, this role co-designs and tests new Salesforce workflows - specifically for duplicate management, activity tracking, and complex grant reporting - while performing regular database quality control audits. While not a primary gift processor, the Analyst maintains cross-training in gift intake to serve as strategic backup during peak fiscal thresholds and PTO coverage.

Division Ticketing Lead & Technical Support

  • Help Desk Management: Take direct ownership of the Development team’s Salesforce ticketing system. Receive, prioritize, triage, and resolve incoming data, reporting, and system access requests from frontline fundraisers and operations staff within established SLAs.
  • Frontline Technical Support & Training: Provide technical guidance and user support across the team. Salesforce Systems Optimization & Custom Tracking

  • Recognition & Benefit Tracking: Partner with the Manager to design, build, and enforce standardized Salesforce workflows to accurately track donor naming opportunities, physical/digital recognition, and bespoke benefit fulfillment for OPC and Principal Gift donors.
  • Grants & Gift Reporting Architecture: Build custom tracking frameworks, reports, and dashboards in Salesforce to capture the full lifecycle, financial milestones, and reporting triggers for complex institutional gifts and grants.

Data Hygiene, Auditing & Quality Assurance

  • Workflow Automation & Documentation: Identify manual, repetitive data entry pain points across the department and recommend automated solutions. Maintain comprehensive, up-to-date documentation of database configurations and data standards.

Cross-Functional & Revenue Backup

  • Gift Processing Backup: Cross-train on all gift processing, lockbox, wire transfer, and batching procedures under the guidance of the Gift Acceptance team, serving as vital cross-functional surge backup during fiscal year-end and peak fundraising cycles.

  • Rapid, high-touch resolution of all internal data ticketing requests, maintaining reliable and timely responses to internal stakeholders, in support of strong customer service to donors and prospects
  • Standardized, fully functional Salesforce tracking systems, reports, and dashboards for donor benefits, OPC recognition, and fundraising revenue .

  • Comprehensive, updated user documentation and technical knowledge-base resources for the Development team.

Description

The Senior Transformation Program Lead will lead the North America Billing transformation; a critical multi-year initiative focused on modernizing billing capabilities through the implementation of the Majesco platform.

This role serves as the Overall Program Lead (OPL), bringing together business, technology, operations, and delivery partners around a unified transformation roadmap and ensuring the program is positioned to deliver its intended business outcomes. The OPL will provide end-to-end leadership across the transformation, creating clarity across a complex portfolio of work, connecting interdependencies, enabling timely decisions, and ensuring leaders and teams remain aligned on priorities, outcomes, risks, and execution.

Success in this role requires a leader who can operate equally effectively at the executive and delivery levels. The OPL will partner closely with senior business and technology leaders, product and engineering teams, functional experts, and external partners to translate strategy into an executable roadmap and drive disciplined execution across a large, complex transformation.

Ultimately, the Senior Transformation Program Lead is accountable for connecting strategy to execution and creating a culture of execution excellence across the transformation. This leader will establish the operating discipline, accountability, transparency, and ways of working that enable a complex, multi-year program to perform at its best. They will set the tone for how teams work together, how decisions are made, how challenges are surfaced and resolved, and how the organization continuously learns and adapts to deliver meaningful and sustainable business value.

Proactively identify dependencies, sequencing considerations, resource needs, risks, and barriers, and drive issues through resolution to protect outcomes and momentum.

  • Partner across organizational boundaries. Build strong relationships across GRS and with internal and external partners, creating shared accountability for outcomes rather than operating through individual functions or workstreams.
  • Build a culture of execution excellence. Establish the operating discipline, behaviors, and ways of working required for a high-performing transformation. Create clear accountability for outcomes, reinforce transparency and constructive challenge, and ensure teams consistently follow through on decisions and commitments while continuously improving how the program executes.

How You’ll Show Up

  • Create a culture of execution excellence. Set a high bar for how the program operates and delivers. Foster a culture where accountability is clear, commitments matter, risks and issues are surfaced early, constructive challenge is welcomed, and teams work together to solve problems and deliver outcomes.
  • Lead through influence and partnership. Build trusted relationships across business, technology, operations, and external partners, creating shared ownership and bringing people together around the outcomes of the transformation.

Hold yourself and others accountable for decisions, commitments, and outcomes while maintaining a collaborative, solutions-oriented culture.

jobs.description:
About Celldex

Celldex is pioneering new horizons in immunology to deliver life-changing therapies. We are relentless in our pursuit of novel antibody-based treatments that engage the human immune system and directly affect critical pathways to improve the lives of patients with allergic, inflammatory and autoimmune disorders. We have built a culture where innovative and talented people thrive—focusing a significant effort on attracting and retaining passionate and motivated employees who want to play a role in helping people with serious health conditions and who see this effort as personally rewarding. In our highly entrepreneurial environment, employees are empowered and the opportunity for professional development occurs every day.

Celldex is now entering an exciting new chapter – building a commercial team to launch barzolvolimab - the most advanced anti-KIT therapy in pivotal development that has the potential to redefine treatment for multiple allergy and dermatological diseases with Phase 3 studies in CSU, ColdU, SD and phase 2 studies in AD. We’re looking for curious, driven builders who can connect their day-to-day work to enterprise-level impact, endlessly prioritize what matters most, and deliver on their commitments with urgency and ownership. If you’re energized by building something meaningful, excited to grow personally and professionally, and motivated to create lasting impact in a fast-moving, entrepreneurial environment, we’d love to meet you.

Ready to make an impact? Learn more about joining the Celldex Team today!

Overview

Celldex is seeking an accomplished market access leader to serve as Executive Director, National and Key Accounts, reporting to the Vice President, Managed Markets. This individual will lead the national and regional payer account organization responsible for securing and optimizing access for barzolvolimab, Celldex's investigational therapy in development for chronic spontaneous urticaria (CSU), subject to regulatory approval. The Executive Director will translate the market access strategy into disciplined account execution across national and regional health plans, pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs), integrated delivery networks, Group Purchasing Organizations (GPOs), government channels, and other priority customers.

The role requires exceptional leadership capabilities, deep market access expertise, and the ability to effectively represent account team insights, customer needs, reimbursement challenges, and market opportunities to Celldex Executive Leadership while ensuring alignment with the company's overall strategic direction. The successful candidate will build and lead a high-performing team of National Account Managers, Regional Account Managers, and Key Account Managers, establish clear performance expectations, guide complex access and contracting negotiations, and ensure launch readiness and post-launch execution. This role requires deep payer expertise, strong command of medical-benefit and buy-and-bill dynamics, sound judgment, and the ability to influence senior internal and external stakeholders.

Responsibilities

  • Lead, coach, and hold accountable the National Account Manager and Regional Account Manager teams responsible for payer access and account execution for barzolvolimab.
  • Develop and execute the national and regional account strategy plan in alignment with Celldex's overall market access, pricing, contracting, distribution, and commercial strategies.
  • Establish account segmentation, prioritization, call planning, objectives, milestones, performance standards, and operating rhythms across the payer account organization.
  • Ensure account strategies align with Celldex's overall commercial, market access, and corporate objectives.
  • Direct engagement with national and regional health plans, PBMs, specialty pharmacies, integrated delivery networks, government accounts, and other strategic customers, as appropriate.
  • Lead and support complex product access and contract negotiations, including medical-benefit and buy-and-bill arrangements, while protecting long-term product value and adhering to approved governance.
  • Ensure the team communicates a compelling, compliant clinical and economic value proposition to payer and population-health decision-makers.
  • Anticipate payer policy, utilization-management, reimbursement, and competitive barriers; develop account-specific strategies to improve timely and appropriate patient access.
  • Partner closely with Market Access Strategy, Pricing and Contracting, Trade and Distribution, HEOR, Medical Affairs, Marketing, Sales, Finance, Legal, Compliance, and Patient Services.
  • Provide high-quality account intelligence, access forecasts, policy updates, contracting insights, and risk assessments to senior leadership and cross-functional launch teams.
  • Build launch-readiness capabilities, tools, dashboards, and key performance indicators; monitor execution and take corrective action when performance is below expectations.
  • Recruit, onboard, develop, retain, and succession-plan a diverse team of market access professionals; foster a culture of ownership, transparency, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
  • Manage the function's budget and external resources responsibly and ensure all activities comply with company policies and applicable laws and regulations.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree required; advanced degree in business, healthcare, pharmacy, public health, or a related discipline preferred.
  • Minimum of 15 years of pharmaceutical, biotechnology, managed markets, healthcare account management, or related commercial experience.
  • Minimum of 8-10 years of progressive leadership experience, including responsibility for leading national account management, market access, or customer-facing organizations.
  • Demonstrated success leading Payer Account Directors, National Account Managers, Regional Account Managers, or comparable customer-facing market access teams.
  • Substantial experience negotiating product access and contracts involving medical-benefit, specialty, infused/injected, or buy-and-bill products.
  • Deep understanding of payer decision-making, formulary and medical-policy processes, utilization management, specialty pharmacy, reimbursement, distribution, and provider economics.
  • Proven ability to lead teams through pre-launch planning, launch execution, and evolving market conditions with clear goals and measurable accountability.
  • Strong executive presence, negotiation skills, business judgment, financial acumen, and ability to communicate complex issues clearly to senior leaders and customers.
  • Exceptional leadership, coaching, organizational development, and talent management capabilities.
  • Track record of effective cross-functional leadership in a matrixed, fast-paced, entrepreneurial environment.
  • Ability to travel up to 60%, including overnight travel, based on business needs.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in immunology, allergy, dermatology, rare disease, or other specialty markets with complex payer and provider access dynamics.

Company Overview:Blink Health is the fastest growing healthcare technology company that builds products to make prescriptions accessible and affordable to everybody. Our two primary products – BlinkRx and Quick Save – remove traditional roadblocks within the current prescription supply chain, resulting in better access to critical medications and improved health outcomes for patients.

BlinkRx is the world’s first pharma-to-patient cloud that offers a digital concierge service for patients who are prescribed branded medications. Patients benefit from transparent low prices, free home delivery, and world-class support on this first-of-its-kind centralized platform. With BlinkRx, never again will a patient show up at the pharmacy only to discover that they can’t afford their medication, their doctor needs to fill out a form for them, or the pharmacy doesn’t have the medication in stock.

We are a highly collaborative team of builders and operators who invent new ways of working in an industry that historically has resisted innovation. Join us!

Hours: Full-time, salaried (40hrs/week), Mon-Fri, 7:30am-9pm ET rotating shifts and rotating Saturdays 7:00am-5pm ET

The Opportunity:

As a BlinkRx Pharmacist, you are the clinical backbone of our closed-door facility. You will verify prescriptions with speed and precision, provide proactive phone-based patient counseling, and collaborate with prescribers to keep medications moving without compromising safety. This role is ideal for pharmacists who thrive in a structured, high-throughput environment and are passionate about improving patient outcomes at scale.

Responsibilities:

Prescription Verification and Dispensing

  • Review and clinically verify new and refill prescriptions for therapeutic appropriateness, drug-drug interactions, contraindications, and dosing accuracy
  • Validate prescription data entry performed by pharmacy technicians, ensuring transcription accuracy from provider orders and transfer records
  • Perform pharmacist verification of filled prescriptions in a closed-door fulfillment environment, confirming accuracy of drug, dose, quantity, NDC, and labeling prior to release for shipment
  • Perform daily prospective drug utilization review (DUR) to identify and resolve clinical flags before fulfillment
  • Manage specialty medication handling requirements including cold-chain verification

Patient Care

All patient interaction at BlinkRx is conducted by phone or digital platforms. Our pharmacists are the primary clinical contact for patients and must deliver a high standard of care in every call.

  • Provide proactive outbound patient counseling calls for new prescriptions, addressing drug education, expected side effects, dosing instructions, storage requirements, and adherence strategies
  • Handle inbound clinical patient calls related to counseling and clinical inquiries, while directing non-clinical inquiries, such as refill status and delivery questions, to the patient support team.
  • Document all patient interactions thoroughly in the patient profile within the pharmacy management system
  • Support Spanish-speaking patients with bilingual counseling where applicable

Prescriber Collaboration and Clinical Outreach

  • Contact prescriber offices via phone and electronic messaging to clarify incomplete, ambiguous, or clinically inappropriate prescriptions prior to dispensing
  • Partner with prescribers on therapeutic substitutions, DAW overrides, and formulary alternatives to reduce dispensing delays

Pharmacy Technician Supervision and Workflow Management

  • Supervise pharmacy technicians across data entry, prescription processing, packaging, and fulfillment workflows in accordance with state board regulations and in collaboration with technician management
  • Conduct real-time quality checks on technician work product, providing immediate corrective feedback to maintain accuracy standards
  • Identify and escalate technician performance trends to pharmacy leadership; participate in coaching and training as directed

Compliance, Safety and Quality

  • Ensure strict compliance with HIPAA, state pharmacy practice acts, federal DEA regulations, and all BlinkRx corporate policies
  • Oversee proper handling, documentation, and destruction of PHI-containing records and materials in alignment with privacy protocols
  • Participate in quality assurance activities including internal audits, prescription error tracking, and near-miss reporting
  • Report adverse drug events and medication errors through established pharmacovigilance channels, when applicable
  • Maintain fulfillment area compliance standards, including proper storage of temperature-sensitive medications

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Collaborate with pharmacy leadership, patient services, clinical, compliance, and technology teams to drive operational and clinical improvements
  • Coordinate with the shipping and fulfillment team to resolve packaging errors, return-to-sender issues, and delivery failures affecting patient medication access
  • Provide clinical input on technology enhancements, workflow tools, and software configurations that affect the pharmacist verification or patient counseling experience
  • Participate in team huddles, quality reviews, and department meetings to support continuous improvement initiatives

Qualifications:

Required

  • Doctor of Pharmacy (PharmD) degree from an ACPE-accredited College of Pharmacy
  • Active Pharmacy License in good standing with your state Board of Pharmacy AND Idaho Board of Pharmacy
  • Strong command of the English language (written and verbal); bilingual Spanish preferred for phone-based patient counseling
  • Demonstrated ability to perform high-volume prescription verification with strong attention to detail and accuracy
  • Strong technical aptitude and ability to learn pharmacy management systems, verification platforms, and internal workflow tools

Preferred

  • 3+ years of experience in a mail order, specialty, retail or closed-door fulfillment pharmacy
  • Active pharmacy licensure required in home state; candidates must obtain licensure in 3 additional states from the list below within the first 9 months of hire (prior licensure in any of the following states is a plus):
    • AK, AL, AR, CA, ID, IL, KS, KY, LA, MA, MD, MI, MS, NE, NV, OK, OR, TN, TX, VA, WV
  • Familiarity with pharmacovigilance or adverse drug event reporting protocols

What Success Looks Like:

  • Prescription verification queues are processed accurately and on time without sacrificing clinical quality
  • Every patient who receives a counseling call feels informed, supported, and confident in their therapy
  • Prescriber outreach is proactive and efficient, minimizing dispensing delays caused by incomplete or unclear orders
  • Compliance and quality standards are upheld without exception in a fast-paced environment
  • You are a trusted clinical partner within the BlinkRx team — shaping the patient experience from behind the scenes

#blinkindeed

Why Join Us:It is rare to have a company that both deeply impacts its customers and is able to provide its services across a massive population. At Blink, we have a huge impact on people when they are most vulnerable: at the intersection of their healthcare and finances. We are also the fastest growing healthcare company in the country and are driving that impact across millions of new patients every year. Our business model not only helps people, but drives economics that allow us to build a generational company. We are a relentlessly learning, constantly curious, and aggressively collaborative cross-functional team dedicated to inventing new ways to improve the lives of our customers.
