jobs.description:
Purpose 

Delta Faucet Company is seeking a Salesforce Solution Architect to serve as the design authority for our Salesforce ecosystem within the Channel, Experience & Portfolio function of IT. This is a customer-side architecture role — you will partner closely with business leaders to shape the platform according to our roadmap, own how it evolves over multiple years, and guide its direction beyond how any single project is coded. 


Our environment spans B2B, B2C and B2B2C: wholesale distributors, trade professionals, retail partners, e-commerce and direct consumer service, supported by Sales Cloud, Service Cloud, Experience Cloud, Marketing Cloud, Data Cloud and CPQ/Revenue Cloud, integrated to ERP, PIM/DAM and analytics platforms. You will act as trusted advisor to business partners, set the architectural direction, and hold internal and third-party delivery teams accountable to that direction. 


You will succeed here if you enjoy owning the long-term integrity of a platform inside the company that runs it.


What Success Looks Like in Year One 

  • Within 90 days: You have documented the current-state Salesforce architecture, data model and integration landscape, and identified the top technical-debt risks with a remediation point of view. 
  • Within 6 months: You are the recognized design authority on all Channel & Experience initiatives — no significant design decision, internal or vendor-proposed, moves forward without your review. 
  • Within 12 months: A published multi-year platform architecture roadmap is in place and aligned to enterprise architecture standards; measurable reduction in custom code and rework on delivered releases; business partners come to you early, not after requirements are frozen. 

Key Responsibilities and Duties 

  • Design Authority: Own end-to-end solution design across multiple Salesforce Clouds — object and data model, security and sharing, automation strategy, and integration patterns — balancing near-term delivery against long-term maintainability. 
  • Roadmap Ownership: Translate business strategy into a multi-year platform architecture roadmap; recommend build vs. buy vs. configure, and sequence capability delivery accordingly. 
  • Stakeholder Engagement: Act as trusted advisor to Sales, Marketing, Customer Solutions and channel partners; challenge requirements constructively and translate them into technical specifications. 
  • Technical Leadership: Guide internal and partner development teams on best practices, data modeling, automation and API integration; lead design reviews rather than perform hands-on build. 
  • Vendor Governance: Provide architectural oversight of third-party delivery partners and systems integrators — validate that proposed solutions leverage out-of-the-box functionality wherever possible, and hold external partners accountable to industry best practices, security protocols and our standards. 
  • Documentation & Governance: Maintain architecture artifacts and decision records; establish and enforce standards that minimize technical debt. 
  • Emerging Capability: Evaluate new platform capability — including Data Cloud, generative and agentic AI such as Agentforce — and form a defensible point of view on where it creates value while protecting brand, privacy and governance standards. 
  • Validation: Use prototypes and proof-of-concepts, built personally or directed through the team, to de-risk significant design decisions. 

Required Experience and Skills 

  • Experience: 8+ years working with the Salesforce platform, including 2+ years as the accountable architect on at least two full-lifecycle, multi-cloud implementations. 
  • Multi-Cloud Design Depth: Demonstrated design ownership across at least three of: Sales Cloud, Service Cloud, Experience Cloud, Marketing Cloud, Data Cloud, CPQ/Revenue Cloud. 
  • Core Platform Knowledge: Deep command of data modeling, security and sharing architecture, declarative automation strategy, Lightning Experience and integration patterns (REST/SOAP, event-driven, middleware). 
  • Technical Fluency: Sufficient depth in Cross-cloud integration, Apex, LWC and API development to review, challenge and govern the work of developers — hands-on coding is not the primary function of this role. 
  • Governance Judgment: Track record of saying no to unnecessary customization and defending that position with business stakeholders and vendors. 
  • Strategic Thinking: Ability to design solutions that align to long-term business goals and enterprise architecture standards. 
  • Communication: Excellent written and verbal skills, with a proven ability to translate technical concepts for non-technical and executive audiences. 
  • Education: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience. 
  • Autonomy: Executes responsibilities with limited oversight required. 

Preferred Experience 

  • Experience as an in-house Salesforce architect at a customer organization or consulting experience in a long-term client engagement.
  • B2B, B2C or B2B2C commerce with distributor, dealer or trade-professional channel models. 
  • Manufacturing or consumer products industry background. 
  • Experience governing a systems integrator or managed-service partner, including reviewing SOW-driven deliverables. 
  • Practical exposure to generative or agentic AI on the Salesforce platform, including Agentforce, Einstein or Data Cloud-driven use cases. This is valued and will be developed on the job — it is not a screening requirement. 
  • Experience integrating Salesforce with ERP, PIM/DAM or enterprise analytics platforms. 

Certifications 

Architect-track certification preferred, not required. Demonstrated design ownership will always outweigh credentials. 

  • Preferred: Salesforce Certified Application Architect, System Architect, or B2B/B2C Solution Architect. 
  • Commonly held: Salesforce Administrator, Advanced Administrator, Platform App Builder, Platform Developer I. 

Why Delta Faucet Company 

Delta Faucet Company is one of the largest and most recognized brands in kitchen and bath plumbing fixtures, and part of Masco Corporation. Our Salesforce footprint is expanding rapidly across sales, marketing and customer service, with a multi-year investment roadmap already funded. This role carries real design authority from day one and a direct line to IT and business leadership — the scope of an enterprise architect with the influence of a small team. 

Diversity & Inclusion 

At Delta Faucet Company, we view diversity as a mosaic of thoughts and perspectives that come from people’s varied cultural backgrounds, experiences, education, career paths and other influences that make each of us unique. For us, inclusion means welcoming differing opinions, collaborating, allowing people to come to work as who they are and recognizing everyone’s contributions. We know that in a diverse, inclusive company, ideas flow freely, all voices are heard and all perspectives are valued. Delta Faucet Company continuously strives to be this kind of organization. Diversity and Inclusion (D&I) supports our inherent values, makes us more relevant to customers and consumers and inspires innovation. It is not a goal or a program; it is a vital ingredient in our formula for success and a key to our future growth.

Position Summary

We're looking for an L&D Program Manager who understands modern learning and can help associates learn in the flow of work, build real skills, solve problems, and perform with confidence. Do you see the big picture, know how to keep things moving, and like to challenge the way things have always been done? Then keep reading!

You'll help shape how we deliver high impact learning across thousands of frontline and corporate associates nationwide. You'll connect business needs to the right solutions, whether that's a new technology rollout, a maintenance skills program, a compliance requirement, a performance support tool, or something that doesn't look like traditional training at all.

The L&D Program Manager works collaboratively with internal stakeholders to ensure we are solving the right problems, not just fulfilling training requests. You're equal part strategic thinker, operational driver, systems problem solver, and curious challenger. You know that a course isn't always the answer, completion doesn't automatically equal capability, and great learning requires more than great content. You're energized by finding a smarter way to connect learning, knowledge, technology, and performance and to turn big ideas into scalable, measurable results that meet our audience needs.

jobs.title: Design Engineer, PCB & DFM
jobs.excerpt: It's fun to work in a company where people truly BELIEVE in what they're doing!
jobs.description:
It's fun to work in a company where people truly BELIEVE in what they're doing!

We're committed to bringing passion and customer focus to the business.

The PCB Layout & Design for Manufacturing (DFM) Engineer is a highly visible technical role within Creation Technologies, responsible for driving excellence in printed circuit board design, manufacturability, and production readiness across the organization. This position serves as a key subject matter expert for complex PCB layout, Valor DFM, Design for Assembly, and PCB fabrication and assembly processes.

Working from electrical schematics and engineering requirements, the engineer will develop and support complex, high density, multilayer PCB designs while ensuring electrical, mechanical, reliability, and manufacturing requirements are incorporated from the earliest stages of development. Beyond individual designs, this role will help shape how Creation approaches PCB design and manufacturing by developing DFM methodologies, integrating manufacturing design rules, establishing PCB design standards, and driving continuous improvement across engineering and manufacturing teams.

This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced PCB design professional who enjoys both hands on technical work and the opportunity to influence standards, processes, and best practices across a global electronics manufacturing organization.

The position offers flexibility to be remote, with a strong preference for candidates located in the Denver, Colorado area to support collaboration with key Creation Technologies teams and facilities.

DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES include, but not limited to:

DFM Analysis on Circuit Card Assemblies (~75% of time)

  • Lead Design for Manufacturability (DFM), Design for Assembly (DFA) assessments for printed circuit board assemblies.
  • Utilize Siemens Valor NPI and / or related tools to perform automated manufacturability analysis on customer and internally developed PCB designs.
  • Develop, maintain, and continuously improve DFM rule sets aligned with IPC standards, fabrication capabilities, assembly processes, and customer requirements.
  • Review Gerber, ODB++, BOM, centroid, assembly drawing, and fabrication data packages for completeness and manufacturability.
  • Lead DFM review meetings with manufacturing, process engineering, quality, and customers to resolve design and process concerns.
  • Prepare DFM reports, technical presentations, and executive summaries to communicate findings and recommendations.
  • Stay informed on emerging technologies, tools, and standards to strengthen product performance and maintain industry leadership.
  • Other duties and responsibilities as assigned

PCB Layout & Design (~25% of time)

  • Develop complex multilayer PCB layouts from engineer-approved schematics using industry-standard PCB design tools such as Altium Designer, Cadence Allegro, or equivalent.
  • Create PCB stack-ups, placement strategies, routing topologies, and design constraints that satisfy signal integrity, power integrity, thermal, mechanical, and manufacturing requirements.
  • Collaborate with electrical and mechanical engineers to ensure successful implementation of design intent while optimizing manufacturability and cost.
  • Generate fabrication and assembly deliverables including Gerber, ODB++, IPC-2581, pick-and-place files, fabrication drawings, assembly drawings, and manufacturing documentation.
  • Perform layout reviews and design verification to ensure compliance with company standards, IPC requirements, and customer specifications.
  • Maintain PCB footprint libraries, design rules, and layout standards.
  • Create and maintain CAD structure for symbol and footprint libraries to ensure design consistency and efficiency.
  • Manage CAD tool licenses and support interfaces to maintain tool availability and performance.
  • Generate bills of materials (BOMs) from schematic and layout databases to support material planning and documentation accuracy.
  • Import schematics or netlists into layout CAD tools to prepare designs for routing and verification.
  • Collaborate with responsible engineers and mechanical teams to ensure design intent, compliance, and successful prototype builds.

QUALIFICATIONS:

Education:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Engineering Technology or Data Management desired but equivalent technical expertise accepted.

Experience:

  • 10+ years of PCB layout experience in a manufacturing or electronics development environment.
  • 5+ years of experience supporting PCB fabrication, PCBA assembly, or DFM activities.
  • Extensive experience designing multilayer, high-density PCB layouts from completed electrical schematics.
  • Experience with PCB EDA tools; mainly Altium but familiarity with Cadence Allegro, OrCAD, or PADS will be a plus.

Skills Required

  • Expertise in PCB layout and design principles, including signal integrity, thermal management, and component placement.
  • Proficiency in Design for Manufacturing (DFM) tools such as Siemens Valor NPI
  • Understanding of industry standards including IPC-2221, IPC-7351, IPC-A-610, IPC-6012, and IPC-J-STD-001 preferred
  • Familiar PCB fab suppliers and their capabilities
  • Strong analytical, communication, and leadership skills
  • Advanced Knowledge of PCBA manufacturing processes and production flow
  • Advanced knowledge in Electronics Components designs
  • Ability to interpret Gerber data, BOMs, and DFM reports
  • Strong analytical and data interpretation skills
  • Effective communication in technical and team settings
  • Design for Test (DFT) experience would be an asset but not required

WORKING ENVIRONMENT CONDITIONS


Physical and/or Mental Demands

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to sit and use hands to finger, handle, or feel office equipment, objects, tools, or controls. The employee is regularly required to stand, walk; reach with hands and arms; and occasionally stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl. The employee must regularly lift and/or move up to 10 pounds, and occasionally up to 25 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, color vision and identification, peripheral vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus.


The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential and non-essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.


Working Conditions

This may be a hybrid position but can also work from a Creation site. Occasional travel may be required. The working environment is generally clean; however, if visiting a Creation site, this position may be exposed to occasional dust, metals/solder occasional exposure to high noise levels from operating machines or physical hazards from moving equipment and machine parts. The employee must wear designated PPE and/or electrostatic dissipative protection where required. Otherwise, office/business casual attire, consistent with site specific safety guidelines, is appropriate.


In accordance with pay transparency regulations, the anticipated starting salary for this position ranges from $110k-$135k USD annually. Full-time employees are also eligible for performance-based bonuses and a range of benefits. Please note that this salary range is not guaranteed, and the final offer may vary based on experience, education, location, and shift. Additionally, the benefits and programs available may differ depending on the hire date, schedule type, and hours worked.


If you like wild growth and working with happy, enthusiastic over-achievers, you'll enjoy your career with us!


Creation Technologies is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to sex, race, color, religion, national origin, disability, protected Veteran status, age, or any other characteristic protected by law.


If you require any accommodations to complete the application process or need the job posting in an alternative format, please email . You will be connected with our Talent Acquisition team.


If you are contacted regarding the position, please inform our Talent Acquisition team of any accommodations you may need during the recruiting process. All information related to accommodation requests will be handled confidentially.

Practice Overview:

Ankura’s Health Care team is a recognized leader in health care and life sciences disputes, compliance, and investigations. The team combines clinical, technical, operational, financial, economic, and analytic expertise to help clients and counsel resolve complex matters involving payers, providers, pharmacies, and law firms.

Role Overview

As a key member of our Healthcare and Life Sciences Practice, you will be working with the firm’s health care and Life Sciences industry leadership team in building the firm’s strategies, solutions, and capabilities to provide regulatory compliance, disputes, and investigations services across the Life Sciences sector. You will be joining a team of industry experts with backgrounds in compliance, legal, audit, operations, nursing, pharmacy, medical science, economics, accounting, and data science.

Key Components of the Role will Include:

Technical Expertise: Previous or current consulting experience at a public accounting firm or large to mid-size consulting firm in the life sciences segment (pharma, biotech, healthcare technology, medical devices and/or diagnostics), with experience working in a transformative environment to properly align people/process/technology to improve financial and operational performance.

A strong working knowledge of the laws, regulations and industry trends impacting the Life Sciences industry is required. These include the: Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act and related FDA regulations; Federal False Claims Act and Anti-Kickback statute; and Medicare and Medicaid, Veteran’s Administration and 340 B drug pricing requirements.

Strategic Thought Leadership: Actively engaged in industry groups and events providing executive experience in “innovation thought leadership” for pharmaceutical manufacturers, biotech, and medical device/diagnostic companies and their counsel and private equity firms is important for this position.

Client Service Experience: A proven track record in delivering large/complex compliance, disputes, and investigations and advisory projects is essential. This individual has executive experience in communicating effectively with boards of directors; client executives; governmental authorities; and industry professionals at all working levels.

Growth: You will be part of a group that is pursuing internal and external growth opportunities. A proven track record in driving sustainable financial and operational results at a consulting firm is preferred.

Talent Development: Experience coaching and mentoring talent to help our team grow professionally (regardless of position). Participating in recruiting new talent will also be expected.

Collaborative Influence: As previously noted, Ankura’s largest industry focus is healthcare. Collaborating with consulting professionals across all lines of business within the firm is a core expectation for this position (i.e. Financial Services, Strategy and Performance, Economics, Data Analytics, and other transaction services).

Other Expectations Include:

  • Participate in relevant healthcare or life sciences industry groups and conference events

  • Executing quality service delivery and identifying additional value-added services

  • Experience in providing expert witness testimony is preferred

  • Managing multiple, large engagements, evaluating work quality and performance, including qualitative and quantitative tasks

  • Providing best-in-class experience for our clients

  • Complying with the firm’s expectations around risk management standards as it pertains to client service delivery including timely billing and collections

  • Participating in developing new business, developing relationships, qualifying leads, and scoping opportunities in a highly collaborative manner

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree from an accredited university in business, finance, accounting, economics, data analytics, health care operations, health policy, clinical discipline, or a related field; advanced degree preferred.

  • 10+ years experience at a Partner/Director/Senior Management level --- OR a combination of life sciences industry experience, public accounting, and life sciences consulting required

  • 10 years or more of experience in life sciences accounting/advisory segments required

  • Proven and tangible business development record with a portable book of relationships and revenue generation of at least $3M; demonstrated ability to grow toward $3M to $5M+ annually.

  • Exceptional executive communication skills, including the ability to explain complex technical, analytic, reimbursement, and damages issues to boards, C-suite clients, law firms, regulators, mediators, arbitrators, judges, and juries.

  • Demonstrated commitment to privilege, confidentiality, work-product discipline, expert independence, collaboration, quality, and team development.

  • Ability and willingness to travel; must be legally authorized to work in the United States without employer sponsorship now or in the future.

*

jobs.excerpt: Company OverviewNCS is a leading industrial products, services and technology company whose primary end-market is car wash operators.
jobs.description:
Company Overview

NCS is a leading industrial products, services and technology company whose primary end-market is car wash operators. NCS provides a full suite of manufactured equipment, installation project services, aftermarket parts and services, chemicals (detergents, protectants, etc.), and software. More specifically with equipment, NCS provides tunnel equipment, IBA (In Bay Automatic), vacuums, dryers, water systems, doors, signage, arches, and related components. NCS also sells a range of brands – on both equipment, chemicals and software today – including Armor All, Rain-X, Blue Coral, TSS, VacuTech, NCS, AMP, etc. The company sells primarily in N. America, operates 6 manufacturing plants across N. America, and has ~1600+ employees. The Company operates numerous Distribution Centers and has sales/HQ offices across N. America, with its primary corporate offices in Des Moines, Iowa and Dallas, TX. NCS is currently owned by Berkshire Partners, a leading Boston-based PE firm

We are interested in every qualified candidate who is eligible to work in the United States. However, we are not currently able to sponsor work visas.

POSITION SUMMARY

The Cyber Security Cloud Engineer is the hands-on engineer responsible for implementing, operating, and maturing security controls across NCS's cloud environment, including Microsoft Azure, Amazon Web Services, and the enterprise SaaS platforms that run the business. NCS operates within an established set of NIST-based enterprise security requirements that define the controls, reporting cadences, and audit expectations for the business. This role implements the security controls that protect our cloud, SaaS, identity, workload, and data environments, and serves as the security lead for integrating newly acquired companies into the NCS security framework. As NCS invests in AI to transform how we serve customers and run the business, this engineer ensures those initiatives are deployed with the required safeguards in place. The engineer also partners with Product Engineering and DevOps teams to put required security controls into practice across the software development lifecycle for NCS products, connected equipment, and customer-facing platforms. The role works closely with Infrastructure, Networking, Data, Application Development, and business stakeholders, and provides security leadership with clear visibility into control status, gaps, and remediation progress. Success in this role means delivering required controls on schedule, demonstrating their effectiveness, and reducing enterprise risk without slowing the business.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Cloud Security Implementation & Operations

  • Implement and maintain security controls across Azure and AWS in accordance with NCS security requirements and the enterprise security framework, including identity and access management, network segmentation, encryption and key management, logging, and workload protection.
  • Deploy and operate cloud security posture management (CSPM/CNAPP), infrastructure-as-code guardrails, policy-as-code, and automated compliance checks that enforce required baselines and provide continuous evidence of control effectiveness.
  • Operate and tune cloud-native security services (e.g., Microsoft Defender for Cloud, Microsoft Sentinel, Entra ID Protection, AWS GuardDuty, Security Hub, CloudTrail, IAM Access Analyzer) and integrate cloud telemetry into enterprise SIEM detection and response workflows.
  • Execute detection engineering and incident response for cloud-hosted and identity-centric threats, including alert triage, investigation, root cause analysis, containment, and remediation coordination with managed security providers, following established playbooks and escalation paths; track emerging cloud attack techniques and recommend updates to detections, hardening, and response procedures.

Acquisition Integration & Migration

  • Support cybersecurity due diligence for acquisitions by executing technical assessments of target environments and documenting gaps against NCS security requirements to inform prioritized integration plans.
  • Execute the secure integration and migration of acquired companies onto NCS platforms, including identity consolidation into Microsoft Entra ID, tenant-to-tenant Microsoft 365 migrations, workload migrations to Azure and AWS, network and endpoint onboarding, and decommissioning of legacy infrastructure.
  • Maintain and follow repeatable, documented integration playbooks and security baselines that bring acquired entities to the required security standard within defined integration timelines, with status reporting throughout.

DevOps & Product Security

  • Implement and operate required security controls across the CI/CD pipeline in partnership with Product Engineering and DevOps teams, including static and dynamic application security testing (SAST/DAST), software composition analysis, secrets scanning, container image scanning, and software bill of materials (SBOM) generation, with risk-based gates that protect release velocity.
  • Support secure product development for NCS software, connected equipment, and customer-facing platforms through threat modeling, secure design reviews, application of secure coding standards, API security, and vulnerability management, with particular attention to payment-enabled and field-deployed systems.
  • Track product security metrics, maintain developer-facing documentation, and uphold remediation SLAs that give engineering teams clear, actionable ownership of security findings.

Compliance, Reporting & Leadership

  • Implement the data protection, DLP, identity governance, and access controls required to securely enable approved AI initiatives, including Microsoft 365 Copilot, Azure OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, and enterprise AI tooling, in partnership with Data, IT, and business teams.
  • Maintain security controls across Microsoft 365, identity, endpoint (Windows and Apple), and cloud platforms in line with NCS security requirements; produce the evidence, metrics, and documentation needed for PCI-DSS compliance, NIST CSF alignment, internal and external audits, executive security reviews, and customer security assessments.
  • Mentor engineers, serve as the escalation point for complex cloud and identity security issues, and report clearly on control status, gaps, risk, and remediation progress to technical and executive audiences.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 5 or more years of progressive experience in IT, with broad exposure to infrastructure, networking, identity, and enterprise systems.
  • 3 or more years of hands-on experience in a dedicated cybersecurity role, including securing production workloads in Microsoft Azure and/or AWS.
  • Demonstrated experience implementing security controls within an established enterprise security framework, including translating defined control requirements, audit findings, and assessment results into deployed, documented, and measurable controls.
  • Hands-on implementation experience with cloud security services and patterns on at least one major platform (Azure or AWS) and solid familiarity with the other, including IAM, network security, encryption and key management, logging, and workload protection.
  • Experience with infrastructure as code (e.g., Terraform, Bicep, CloudFormation), CI/CD platforms (e.g., Azure DevOps, GitHub, GitLab), and application security tooling (SAST/DAST, SCA, secrets and container scanning), with a track record of partnering with development teams to embed security into the SDLC.
  • Working knowledge of the NIST Cybersecurity Framework and experience supporting PCI-DSS compliance and audit or assessment processes, including evidence collection and remediation tracking.
  • Clear, professional written and verbal communication, with the ability to report control status, gaps, and remediation progress to technical and non-technical audiences.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • One or more current, industry-recognized security certifications such as CISSP, CCSP, AWS Certified Security – Specialty, or Microsoft Certified: Azure Security Engineer Associate (AZ-500); equivalent demonstrated experience will be considered.
  • Direct experience executing security workstreams for mergers, acquisitions, or divestitures, including tenant-to-tenant migrations and identity consolidation.
  • Experience securing AI/ML platforms and services (Azure OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, Microsoft 365 Copilot, enterprise data platforms) and familiarity with the NIST AI RMF, OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications, or similar frameworks.
  • Experience with CSPM/CNAPP platforms, container and Kubernetes security, and secrets management.
  • Experience implementing or maturing a product or application security program, including familiarity with OWASP ASVS and SAMM, NIST SSDF, or similar secure development frameworks, and tooling such as GitHub Advanced Security or equivalent integrated DevSecOps platforms.
  • Experience securing embedded, IoT, or payment-enabled products, including PCI-DSS considerations for software and device design.
  • Scripting and automation proficiency (PowerShell, Python, etc.) for detection engineering and security tooling.
  • Experience in manufacturing, distribution, or field service environments, including connected equipment and payment systems.

CORE COMPETENCIES & LEADERSHIP EXPECTATIONS

  • Takes ownership of assigned controls and initiatives and follows through to measurable, documented completion.
  • Executes with discipline against established standards while exercising sound judgment on how to implement them with minimal business friction.
  • Demonstrates calm, decisive leadership during incidents and high-pressure situations.
  • Provides clear, pragmatic implementation guidance to peers and leadership on cloud, product, and AI risk.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS & WORK ENVIRONMENT

  • Primarily office-based or remote-office work using a computer and standard office equipment for extended periods.
  • Ability to communicate effectively through phone, video, and in-person meetings.
  • Periodic participation in after-hours incident response or maintenance windows.
  • Occasional travel to NCS facilities and acquired-company locations to support integration activities.

Grow your career supported by an energized and passionate team, professional development, training, flexibility and opportunities for advancement. We offer competitive wages and benefits including comprehensive health, dental and vision coverage, and more.

National Carwash Solutions is a proud equal opportunity employer. We are a drug free, EEO employer committed to a diverse workforce. We will consider all qualified candidates regardless of race, color, national origin, sex age, marital status, personal appearance, sexual orientation, gender identity, family responsibilities, disability, education, political affiliation or veteran status.

A Sr. Principal Analyst uses research and analytical skills to create thought-leading insights that help Sourcing, Procurement and Vendor Management and other IT leaders navigate software and cloud pricing and contracting. As a Gartner analyst, you will meet daily with senior-level clients to help them achieve their most critical priorities, driving performance and business outcomes. Candidates must have current knowledge of Microsoft’s commercial programs, contracting models, pricing, and discounting approaches as well as a vision for how Microsoft licensing, and overall contracting and negotiations with large vendors, will evolve globally and regionally.

What you’ll do:

  • Provide clients and prospects with compelling, actionable advice regarding their Microsoft pricing and contracting needs, including negotiation strategies and ongoing vendor management, via virtual or face-to-face interactions.

  • Represent Gartner’s insights and methodologies with credibility in client engagements and media interactions.
  • Identify and implement process improvements that drive team success.

What you’ll need:

Gartner analysts are viewed as the experts. This means you need to know your markets, vendors, trends, management practices, etc. and be able to see the forest and the trees. You should have:

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience; Graduate degree preferred.
  • 8+ years’ experience with a minimum of 5 years work experience in SaaS/software contract negotiations, technology procurement, category management, vendor management or software asset management within a buying organization, outsourcer, consulting firm, or reseller.

  • Self-motivated, collaborative, quick-learning, and comfortable working in a multicultural, matrixed environment.
  • Able to conduct occasional travel (usually no more than 25%), regionally and globally.

Who are we?

At Gartner, Inc. (NYSE:IT), we guide the leaders who shape the world.

Our mission relies on expert analysis and bold ideas to deliver actionable, objective business and technology insights, helping enterprise leaders and their teams succeed with their mission-critical priorities.

Since our founding in 1979, we’ve grown to 20,000 associates globally who support over 13,000 client enterprises in ~90 countries and territories. The bar is unapologetically high. So is the impact you can have here.

What makes Gartner a great place to work?

Our vast, virtually untapped market potential offers limitless opportunities – opportunities that may not even exist right now – for you to grow professionally and flourish personally. How far you go is driven by your passion and performance.

We hire remarkable people who collaborate and win as a team. Together, our singular, unifying goal is to deliver results for our clients.

Our teams are inclusive and composed of individuals from different geographies, cultures, religions, ethnicities, races, genders, sexual orientations, abilities and generations.

We invest in great leaders who bring out the best in you and the company, enabling us to multiply our impact and results. This is why, year after year, we are recognized worldwide as a great place to work.

Gartner is the world authority on AI

At Gartner, you’ll join a company at the very center of the AI revolution. Gartner has proactive, objective guidance throughout clients’ AI journeys. We set the standard for how organizations leverage artificial intelligence to drive meaningful impact. You’ll have access to unmatched resources, expertise, and technology, and play a key role in helping Gartner and our clients innovate and grow as we leverage AI to transform business and technology landscapes.

It’s an exciting time to be at Gartner, with limitless opportunities to make a real impact, grow your skills, and build a lasting, meaningful career in a field that’s reshaping the way we operate. If you’re passionate about AI and want to be part of a team that’s guiding the leaders who shape the world, Gartner is the place for you.

What do we offer?

Gartner offers world-class benefits, highly competitive compensation and disproportionate rewards for top performers.

In our hybrid work environment, we provide the flexibility and support for you to thrive — working virtually when it's productive to do so and getting together with colleagues in a vibrant community that is purposeful, engaging and inspiring.

Ready to grow your career with Gartner? Join us.

Gartner believes in fair and equitable pay. A reasonable estimate of the base salary range for this role is 105,000 USD - 140,000 USD. Please note that actual salaries may vary within the range, or be above or below the range, based on factors including, but not limited to, education, training, experience, professional achievement, business need, and location. In addition to base salary, employees will participate in either an annual bonus plan based on company and individual performance, or a role-based, uncapped sales incentive plan. jobs.description:
AlphaGov is seeking an experienced Criminal Investigations Instructor to develop and deliver practical training for government, law enforcement, and public-sector professionals.

We welcome current and former criminal investigators, detectives, special agents, academy instructors, and other professionals with experience teaching investigative methods. Candidates may specialize in one or more investigative disciplines; expertise in every subject area is not required.

What you’ll do

  • Deliver engaging instruction on criminal investigation principles, methods, and practices.
  • Teach topics within your expertise, such as investigative planning, interviewing, evidence collection and preservation, case documentation, and report writing.
  • Develop realistic case studies, practical exercises, and investigative scenarios.
  • Help participants strengthen critical thinking, evaluate information, and identify investigative next steps.
  • Prepare or adapt lesson plans, presentations, instructor guides, and participant materials.
  • Assess participant performance and provide clear, actionable feedback.
  • Incorporate applicable legal standards, agency policies, and ethical practices into instruction.
  • Coordinate with project managers and subject matter experts to meet client training objectives.

Requirements

  • Professional experience conducting, supervising, or supporting criminal investigations.
  • Experience delivering training, teaching, mentoring investigators, or facilitating professional development.
  • Strong knowledge of investigative procedures and practices within your area of expertise.
  • Ability to explain complex concepts clearly and connect instruction to practical investigative work.
  • Strong communication, writing, and organizational skills.
  • Ability to tailor instruction to participants with different experience levels.
  • Availability for travel when required by an assignment.

Preferred experience

  • Service with a federal, state, local, tribal, or military investigative organization.
  • Instruction at a law enforcement academy, government training center, college, or professional training organization.
  • Developing curricula, scenario-based exercises, or performance assessments.
  • Experience with one or more of the following:
    • Investigative interviewing and the P.E.A.C.E. model.
    • Fraud, financial crime, or white-collar investigations.
    • Cybercrime or digital evidence.
    • Violent crime, crimes against persons, or property crime.
    • Internal affairs, public integrity, or administrative investigations.
    • Evidence handling, courtroom testimony, or case presentation.
  • Relevant instructor credentials or specialized investigative training.

Benefits

Assignments may include introductory courses, advanced investigative instruction, curriculum development, instructor coaching, or ongoing training program support.

AlphaGov considers candidates for full-time, part-time, and project-based opportunities. This posting supports current and anticipated client needs; specific assignments, schedules, locations, and employment arrangements depend on project requirements and, where applicable, contract award.

Minimum experience, credentials, and subject matter requirements vary by assignment. Compensation will be discussed based on qualifications and scope.

How to apply

Submit your résumé and a brief summary of your investigative and instructional experience. Include your areas of specialization, courses taught, audiences trained, relevant credentials, and preferred employment arrangement.

jobs.excerpt: Senior Director, Reach Operations and EventsCollege Board - Engagement and Reach (EaR) Location: This is a remote role.
jobs.description:
Senior Director, Reach Operations and Events

College Board - Engagement and Reach (EaR)


Location: This is a remote role. Candidates who live near College Board offices have the option of being fully remote or hybrid (Tuesday and Wednesday in office). All College Board employees are required to occasionally travel to meet in person for business purposes.

Role Type: This is a full-time position.


*Strong candidate already identified for this role


About the Team

The Engagement and Reach (EaR) team — roughly ninety professionals across Reach, Communications, and Counselor Community Engagement — drives College Board's strategy for reaching, engaging, and converting prospective students, families, and partners into the organization's programs. This role sits within Reach, which is responsible for connecting College Board with more students, families, and communities than ever before. That includes the work you'd expect from marketing — building interest in College Board's programs and services, and helping teams engage state and district leaders — but it also means thinking in new ways about audience engagement, including working through associations and other outside organizations to reach people College Board could not reach on its own.


About the Opportunity

This is a newly created role responsible for building, from the ground up, two enterprise-level systems that do not yet exist at College Board: a standardized approach to how the organization defines, scores, routes, and converts marketing leads, and a framework for how the organization prioritizes, resources, and measures impact across its full portfolio of over three hundred annual industry events and sponsorships. This role also builds the documentation and training infrastructure that drives adoption of these systems and establishes marketing as a cross-functional data and process partner across the organization, rather than a reactive service function.

This role will work through significant ambiguity, set direction for teams across State and District Partnerships (SDP), Global Programs and External Relations (GPER), Higher Education Membership and Access (HMA), and Program, and serve as a trusted point of view for senior leadership on questions of field marketing strategy, lead operations, event investment, and organization-wide measurement standards. This is an individual contributor role within Engagement and Reach (Reach), reporting to the Executive Director, Reach Operations, with the expectation that this person will design both systems and execute within them during this foundational period, building the supporting documentation and training that drive adoption, and refining the standards as the function matures.

In this role, you will:


Own the Enterprise Marketing Lead Operations System (35%)

  • Define and own the enterprise standard for what constitutes a qualified marketing lead and contact, including scoring methodology, routing logic, and conversion tracking
  • Architect the operating system connecting lead capture, scoring, and routing to sales pipeline outcomes — designed to be adopted across marketing, sales, and partner functions, not run manually
  • Continuously test, refine, and improve the lead and contact operations system as volume and complexity grow, treating this as a living standard rather than a one-time build
  • Build the reporting and analytics infrastructure that gives leadership visibility into lead velocity, conversion, and pipeline health

Own the Enterprise Event Strategy and Portfolio System (35%)

  • Define and own the enterprise-wide framework for how the organization evaluates, prioritizes, and resources its full portfolio of over three hundred annual industry events, sponsorships, and third-party engagements
  • Set the standards by which future events are selected, funded, and measured — building a system that other teams and future hires will operate within, not a calendar that this role runs alone
  • Establish the impact measurement model for event investment, including cost-per-lead, pipeline contribution, and return on investment (ROI), where no standardized model exists today
  • Lead negotiation and structuring of major sponsorships and speaking opportunities that carry enterprise-level visibility or investment

Shape Cross-Functional and Enterprise Direction (20%)

  • Serve as the trusted point of view for the Executive Director and VP of Reach on questions of field marketing strategy, lead operations, event investment, and organization-wide measurement standards brining a clear, defensible recommendation to every significant decision.
  • Align State and District Partnerships (SDP), Global Programs and External Relations (GPER), Program, and other functions to a shared standard for how the organization shows up externally and converts that presence into pipeline
  • Build and maintain centralized documentation and structured training on marketing measurement and CRM best practices, driving adoption across partner divisions and establishing marketing as a cross-functional data and process partner rather than a reactive service function
  • Anticipate second-order impacts of event and lead strategy decisions on sales forecasting, budget planning, and brand presence across the organization
  • Benchmark lead operations and event-portfolio practices against peer nonprofit and enterprise marketing organizations, bringing external models to bear rather than defaulting to internal legacy approaches

Execute Within the Systems You Build (10%)

  • Direct the build and initial operations of both systems during this foundational period, while the function is being stood up and before additional capacity is added
  • Identify, over time, where execution should transfer to future hires, agency partners, or a split of the combined role, and flag when scope has outgrown a single-person structure

About You

You have:

  • Seven or more years of experience across marketing operations, demand generation, or field/event marketing, with demonstrated ownership of enterprise-level systems or frameworks — not just execution within an existing one
  • A proven track record of building something from ambiguity: designing a process, system, or standard where none existed, rather than optimizing an established one
  • Deep proficiency with marketing automation platforms (for example, HubSpot or Marketo) and customer relationship management (CRM) systems (for example, Salesforce), including lead scoring, routing logic, and attribution modeling
  • Experience negotiating high-value sponsorships, partnerships, or vendor contracts with enterprise-level financial or reputational stakes
  • A demonstrated ability to set strategy and influence senior leaders — including Vice Presidents (VPs) and above — without relying on formal authority over the teams being aligned
  • Skilled at driving alignment across teams and functions that do not report to you — using data, credibility, and a clear point of view to move senior stakeholders toward a shared standard, rather than positional authority
  • Demonstrated track record of holding cross functional teams accountable to enterprise standards, and using data and adoption metrics without formal management responsibility over that team
  • Strong analytical skills, including building reporting and dashboards that connect marketing activity to pipeline and revenue outcomes
  • A track record of anticipating second-order impacts of decisions across functions, rather than optimizing for a single team's metrics
  • Degree requirement: Bachelor's degree required; equivalent professional experience will be considered in place of a degree
  • Ability to travel up to thirty percent of the time for on-site event execution and industry engagement
  • Ability to sit, stand, and work at a computer for extended periods; ability to travel to and navigate event venues and conference environments, including standing for extended periods during on-site event execution and occasionally lifting or transporting event materials (up to 25 pounds)

Preferred:

  • Experience standing up a net-new function or system within a growing organization, including navigating the ambiguity of building without a template
  • Experience operating at the intersection of marketing and sales, with a track record of improving lead-to-revenue conversion through system design rather than campaign tactics alone
  • A history of point of view being sought proactively by senior leadership on strategy, not just brought in to execute

All roles at College Board require:

  • A passion for expanding educational and career opportunities and mission-driven work
  • Curiosity and enthusiasm for emerging technologies, with a willingness to experiment with and adopt new AI-driven solutions and comfort with learning and applying new digital tools independently and proactively
  • Clear and concise communication skills, written and verbal
  • A learner's mindset and a commitment to growth: welcoming diverse perspectives, giving and receiving timely, respectful feedback, and continuously improving through iterative learning and user input
  • A drive for impact and excellence: solving complex problems, making data-informed decisions, prioritizing what matters most, and continuously improving through learning, user input, and external benchmarking
  • A collaborative and empathetic approach: working across differences, fostering trust, and contributing to a culture of shared success
  • Authorization to work in the United States

About Our Process

  • Application review will begin immediately and will continue until the position is filled. This role is expected to accept applications for a minimum of five business days.
  • While the hiring process may vary, it generally includes: resume and application submission, recruiter phone/video screen, hiring manager interview, performance exercise, a panel interview, a conversation with leadership, and reference checks.

What We Offer

At College Board, we offer more than a paycheck: we provide a meaningful career, a supportive team, and a comprehensive package designed to help you thrive. We're a self-sustaining nonprofit that believes in fair and competitive compensation grounded in your qualifications, experience, impact, and the market.


A Thoughtful Approach to Compensation

  • The hiring range for this role is $104,000–$160,000.
  • Your exact salary will depend on your location, experience, and how your background compares to others in similar roles at the College Board.
  • We aim to make our best offer upfront, rooted in fairness, transparency, and market data.
  • We adjust salaries by location to ensure fairness, no matter where you live.

You'll have open, transparent conversations about compensation, benefits, and what it's like to work at College Board throughout your hiring process. Check out our careers page for more.

jobs.excerpt: The RoleAs Forward Deployed Staff - Engineering, you'll be embedded with client teams building production-grade AI systems.
jobs.description:
The Role

As Forward Deployed Staff - Engineering, you'll be embedded with client teams building production-grade AI systems. This is a hands-on engineering role where you'll design, build, and ship AI products and internal tools that solve real business problems.

The "Forward Deployed" Philosophy:

Everyone at LevelUp Labs is a generalist. You'll be expected to contribute across engineering, training, and content when needed. However, this role has a spike in engineering and implementation—you're someone who loves building production systems, debugging hard problems, and shipping code that works at scale.

What "spike" means: You can teach and create content, but your edge is in building. You're the person others go to when the system is broken, when the architecture needs rethinking, or when something needs to actually ship.

What You'll Do

Build

  • Design and implement production-grade AI systems alongside client engineering teams

  • Build LLM-powered applications: RAG systems, agents, evaluation frameworks, etc.

  • Own technical architecture decisions and trade-offs

  • Write code that's maintainable, tested, documented, and built to last

  • Debug complex issues across the stack

Embed

  • Work directly with client engineering teams as a peer, not an outside consultant

  • Understand client constraints, existing systems, and organizational context

  • Communicate progress and challenges to both technical and non-technical stakeholders

  • Transfer knowledge to client teams—leave them better than you found them

Learn & Share

  • Distill learnings from implementations into patterns we can reuse

  • Contribute to our courses, documentation, and internal tooling

  • Stay current with AI developments—evaluate what actually works in production

  • Participate in technical discussions and code reviews

What We're Looking For

Must Have

Engineering

  • 2+ years building production software systems

  • Strong programming skills (Python required; experience with TypeScript/JavaScript, Go, or Rust a plus)

  • Deep experience with AI/ML systems: LLMs, RAG, agents, fine-tuning, evaluations

  • Strong understanding of software engineering best practices (testing, CI/CD, observability, documentation)

  • Experience with cloud platforms (AWS, GCP, or Azure)

Production Mindset

  • You've shipped systems that handle real traffic and real users

  • You think about failure modes, edge cases, and operational concerns

  • You know the difference between demo code and production code

  • You've been paged at 2am and fixed something that was broken

Communication

  • Can explain technical decisions to non-technical stakeholders

  • Comfortable presenting architecture and progress to client leadership

  • Clear written communication (documentation, design docs, async updates)

  • Can work effectively with client teams across different cultures and timezones

Mindset

  • Self-directed—you don't need someone telling you what to do next

  • Comfortable with ambiguity and rapidly changing requirements

  • Ego-free: you'll do whatever needs doing to ship

  • Strong opinions, loosely held

Nice to Have

  • Experience with enterprise clients (understanding their constraints and pace)

  • Prior consulting or client-facing engineering experience

  • Contributions to open source projects

  • Background with observability and evaluation frameworks for AI

  • Experience leading technical projects or mentoring engineers

What You'll Get

  • Competitive compensation (base + performance bonuses + outcome-based bonus per engagement)

  • Work on challenging problems with leading companies

  • Learn from a team with 30+ enterprise implementations and published AI research

  • Flexibility: remote-first, async-friendly

  • Direct impact: you're building real systems, not maintaining legacy code

  • Growth: as an early team member, you'll shape our engineering culture

Job Summary

As an AI Deployment Strategist (Customer Outcome Leader) within Forward Deployment Engineering, you are the single-threaded business owner responsible for driving realized value, user adoption, and long-term expansion across our enterprise AI engagements.


Deploying enterprise AI is fundamentally different from traditional software delivery—it mutates operational workflows, alters decision-making rights, and spans multiple complex technical streams.


Working directly alongside our Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs) who build and optimize the technical architecture, you own the business realization.


You will bridge the gap between executive AI vision and day-to-day operational reality, ensuring our solutions deliver clear, measurable ROI while insulating technical teams from reactive firefighting and unmanaged scope creep.

3. Workflow Redesign & Operational Change Management

jobs.excerpt: OVERVIEWFractured Atlas is seeking two full‐time Member Advisors - one Grants & Member Advisor and one Fundraising & Member Advisor.
jobs.description:
OVERVIEW

Fractured Atlas is seeking two full‐time Member Advisors - one Grants & Member Advisor and one Fundraising & Member Advisor. Fractured Atlas is a national, fully remote nonprofit arts service organization. Our work is guided by the belief that some of the boldest, most urgent creative work happens outside of institutions, led by individual artists, emerging collectives, and grassroots organizations. Our mission is to make the journey from inspiration to living practice more accessible and equitable for artists and creatives. We run the largest fiscal sponsorship program in the country, supporting thousands of active projects in every creative medium across all 50 states. Through fundraising tools, educational resources, visa letters, community programming, and 1-on-1 support, we help artists access the funding, time, and community they need to make the art the world needs.

A successful candidate in both roles will be a creative problem solver and quick learner who has an enthusiasm for the arts, is incredibly personable over the phone and email, possesses a high level of patience and understanding (particularly as it relates to explaining the same information multiple times), and is able to operate and respond in a fast-paced environment while remaining calm and collected. The Grants & Member Advisor will have expertise around supporting our fiscally sponsored projects through the grant process from application through reporting. The Fundraising & Member Advisor will have expertise around advising our fiscally sponsored projects on fundraising and donation processes, including individual appeals, crowdfunding, giving day campaigns, donation policies and processes, and donation investigation.

Candidates with a work history that includes grant writing, fundraising, development, and/or customer service will likely excel. Since Fractured Atlas works virtually, these positions require strong self-motivation and both will be remotely supervised by the Associate Director of Education & Engagement.

At Fractured Atlas, we individually and collectively work hard to carry out our organization’s mission. We also understand that work is just one part of life and, through a culture of care, support team members having full and robust lives outside of work. With that foundation, our organizational culture embraces people who are open to:

  • Building trust with others and addressing equitable distribution of responsibilities when collaborating.
  • Learning new ways of working while welcoming change as a way to reshape processes/policies/programming that no longer serve our values.
  • Transparency in communications, decision making, and feedback.
  • Centering care and connection in our individual work and in relation to our colleagues.

We recognize that the culture and core values of an organization should continue to evolve to reflect the world we live in. At any given time, we recognize that there might be emerging values other than ourstated values and we continue to have conversations about stated and emerging values.

Additionally, at Fractured Atlas we work to adhere toanti-racism and anti-oppression principlesin all areas of our internal and external work. This commitment is grounded in our belief that change is possible, and that our work and that of the artistic community as a whole will grow stronger as oppression is eliminated.

In our current phase of this journey towards being an Anti-Racist Anti-Oppressive organization, the whole staff is engaged in all staff ARAO meetings led by rotating teams and undergo training as part of their onboarding process. We recognize that we do not have all of the answers as we pursue this work. This work will continue to shift as the Fractured Atlas team changes. We ask that new team members join us as we continue to learn, practice, and grow in this work. Learn more about what it’s like to work at Fractured Atlashere.

MAJOR DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES

BOTH MEMBER ADVISOR ROLES:

  • Manage ongoing email communication with artist members through Zendesk.
  • Conduct consultative and onboarding calls using Calendly and Zendesk Talk.
  • Review and approve fundraising materials, including grant applications, individual appeals, and crowdfunding campaigns.
  • Demonstrate Fractured Atlas’ software tools and provide walk-through support to members and fellow Member Advisors as needed.
  • Troubleshoot login, navigation, and other basic access issues.
  • Other duties as assigned to support the team and our members

GRANTS & MEMBER ADVISOR ROLE:

  • Provide member advising and grant administration support for Fractured Atlas’ fiscally sponsored projects:
    • Manage a high volume of grant application reviews while meeting funder deadlines and maintaining accuracy and consistency.
    • Review grant guidelines, applications, budgets, and supporting materials to assess eligibility, ensure compliance, and provide constructive feedback.
    • Advise members on applying for grants through fiscal sponsorship and communicate revisions, missing information, deadlines, and next steps.
    • Review and approve grant-related fundraising materials before submission.
    • Review and approve grant final reports, including narrative and financial reporting requirements.
    • Process grant award payments, review award documentation, and track payment and reporting requirements.
    • Correspond with members and funders regarding applications, awards, payments, required documentation, and final reports.
    • Maintain accurate grant records and handle sensitive member, funder, and financial information with care and discretion.
    • Collaborate with the Grants Manager and Programs team to improve grant-review processes and strengthen member education.

FUNDRAISING & MEMBER ADVISOR ROLE:

  • Provide member advising and financial administrative oversight for Fractured Atlas’ fiscal sponsorship and fundraising tools:
    • Manage a high volume of support queries and reviews while meeting deadlines and maintaining accuracy and consistency.
    • Advise artist members on the use of Fractured Atlas’s fiscal sponsorship program, including its fundraising and financial tools, and how to follow donation and financial procedures.
    • Review and approve fundraising materials: including profile/general support edits, individual appeals, third-party giving campaigns, and crowdfunding campaigns.
    • Support donation tracking and investigation, including logging donations in Airtable, confirming matching gifts, and resolving donation-related issues.
    • Correspond with members and donors regarding returned or disputed donations.
    • Provide back up support with artist visa services program.

WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

BOTH MEMBER ADVISOR ROLES:

  • Knowledge of the fundraising landscape and grant application processes
  • 1-2 years experience or strong familiarity with web-based software (Slack, Google Drive, Airtable, Trello, Zendesk, Calendly, or any ticketing or CRM software)
  • Experience with individual time management in a remote-work environment
  • Possesses self awareness of their professional needs in the workplace
  • Strong collaboration and team communication skills
  • Experience handling sensitive information and tracking specific details with accuracy
  • Experience explaining policies, procedures, or technical processes to non-expert audiences
  • A successful Member Advisor, Programs on the Programs team will be passionate about or committed to:
    • Advising and/or educating artists and creative business owners
    • Streamlining processes and training others to do the same
    • Exercising research, analytical, and investigative skills to problem solve.
    • Using and exploring new technologies
    • Efficient, effective, understanding communication
    • Managing a personal workload
    • Staying flexible and juggling changing priorities
    • Knowing when to take initiative, follow direction, and when to pause
    • Engaging in collaboration and teamwork
  • Experience in arts administration, arts management, or information technology - a plus!
  • Direct experience with financial oversight - a plus!

GRANTS & MEMBER ADVISOR ROLE:

  • 2+ years Direct experience with grants oversight or grant application review.
  • Direct experience with New York State Council on the Arts grants - a plus!

FUNDRAISING & MEMBER ADVISOR ROLE:

  • 2+ years of experience in a member, customer, or client support role - financial, fiscal sponsorship, or compliance-related experience a plus!
  • Experience reviewing materials or requests against established guidelines and making approval decisions
  • Knowledge of donation, payment, or transaction processing

LOCATION

This position is U.S.-based and 100% virtual (with travel about 1-2 times per year*). You can live anywhere in the country but most meetings fall during a 9 AM-6 PM ET window.

*We have full staff and team in person/hybrid gatherings 1-2 times a year, but we respect that individuals have different risk levels with travel and will work with employees to determine what is possible, with consideration for what is unsafe or uncomfortable for team members.

COMPENSATION

This is a full-timenon-exempt position. Salary is $32.70/hr ($68,016 annualized).Fractured Atlas has fixed-tier compensation, so everyone at each tier makes the same. Learn more about our compensation structure here.

Benefits include employer-contributed dental, vision, medical insurance; flexible spending account; employer-contributed 401K plan; commuter benefits; professional development allowance; ticket and staff donation allowance for artist member projects; internet and cell-phone stipend; workplace supplies allowance; unlimited paid vacation days; paid sick days; paid family and medical leave; half-day Fridays (full time is 36 hours), and a casual but hard-working, friendly, and supportive work environment.Learn more about our benefits here.

TO APPLY

When submitting your application, you will be asked which role you are applying for and if you are open to and interested in being considered for both.

To be considered for the position, please use the application portal to upload all the items below in one PDF-formatted file:

  1. Answers to the following prompts (please keep responses to 200 words or less per prompt)
  • Tell us about a time you successfully helped someone achieve their goal(s).
  • What kind of work environment do you thrive in or enjoy contributing to?
  • What’s something in the fundraising or grant landscape that excites you right now? Please consider your top choice of the two roles as you decide (Grants & Member Advisor, Programs or Fundraising & Member Advisor, Programs).
  1. Resume no longer than (1) page
  2. A list of (3) professional references complete with phone number, email address, and explanation of the relationship. (References will not be contacted without your prior consent.)

If you're looking for a way to merge PDFs, iLovePDF is a free browser based option. Incomplete submissions will not be considered, nor will submissions sent outside of the application portal.

When applying, you can use any name that you’d like to be referred to—it does not need to be your legal name. If at any point in the process you’d like for us to update your name in our applicant tracking system, please email and we can update it for you.

We receive many applications for each job and cannot respond to questions about the position unless you are having a technical issue with the job portal or are requesting accommodations for the process. If you need help with a technical issue or are requesting accommodations, please email .

Want to know what’s next after you apply?Here is a breakdown of the steps of the hiring process. We have two or more staff members reviewing materials at each stage and we do not use AI screening tools. We use platforms to help manage the process (Spark Hire and JazzHR) but we do not use their AI screening add-ons.

You can learn more about Fractured Atlas by reviewing our website, blog, and .

OUR COMMITMENT

Fractured Atlas is an equal opportunity employer that values diversity, equity, and inclusion. (Read more about our Anti-Racism and Anti-Oppression commitment.) We do not discriminate based on race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.

October 7th, 2026. Deadline for submissions is October 21st, 2026 at 11:59 PM Pacific Time

jobs.description:
Who we are: Yourgi is on a mission to become Earth's most trusted pet care connector, connecting pet parents with a reliable local network of certified professionals, pet resorts, and veterinary centers. Backed by a passionate team, our mission is to make pet care simple, accessible, and joyful for all. Because pets aren't just animals—they're family.

Yourgi's mission is to be pet parents' most trusted source for pet care services. We are building a differentiated experience for both pet parents and pros through our marketplace and software platform. Pet parents book grooming, boarding, daycare, and training, and independent pet-care pros run their businesses with Yourgi Pro, Connect, and Match. We also power booking for Destination Pet's own locations.

You'll build Yourgi's engineering services function from the ground up: DevOps, SRE, release engineering, infrastructure as code, data pipelines, security operations, and data governance. Your job is to make deploys boring, rollbacks instant, production visible, and data trustworthy. You'll lead a small team of DevOps and SRE engineers, some nearshore, stay hands-on, and set the operating practices every product team follows.

LOCATION : Remote (US only; must be authorized to work in the US, no visa sponsorship)

REPORTS TO: VP of Engineering

PAY: $190,000 base +10% bonus

CORE RESPONSIBILITES:

  • DevOps and release engineering: own CI/CD for API, web, and mobile (GitHub Actions and Azure Pipelines), with unattended deploys, staged or canary releases, one-click rollback, and controlled production deploy access.
  • SRE: stand up production monitoring and alerting on AWS (CloudWatch, X-Ray, synthetics, and PagerDuty), define SLOs for critical customer journeys, and replace noisy alert channels with alerts that are actionable and owned.
  • Incident and change management: launch a shared on-call rotation, incident response, blameless postmortems, and weekly operational reviews.
  • Infrastructure as code: bring AWS infrastructure and database operations under code (OpenTofu, Terraform, or CDK), with consistent environments and reviewed changes.
  • Data pipelines: own the reliability of pipelines that move data from our services and partner systems into the data lake and warehouse, with monitoring, retries, and clear owners.
  • Security operations: run secrets management, least-privilege IAM, dependency and vulnerability scanning, and supply-chain hygiene in every pipeline.
  • Data governance: set standards for data access, retention, classification, and logging so customer data is handled safely across systems.
  • Measures and cost: report DORA metrics (deploy frequency, lead time, change failure rate, and time to restore) and make cloud cost visible by team and service.
  • People: hire, manage, and develop DevOps and SRE engineers, and help product teams own their services in production.

30/60/90 plan


First 30 Days: Inventory the existing pipelines, environments, AWS accounts, alerts, data pipelines, and production access permissions. Establish baseline monitoring for the most critical services. By the end of the first 30 days, review the current-state inventory and the key operational and security risks with the VP of Engineering, and ensure that baseline monitoring dashboards are live.


By Day 60: Establish and launch the on-call rotation and incident management process. Deliver at least one pipeline with automated deployment and rollback capabilities. Publish the initial standards for secrets management, access controls, and data handling. By day 60, ensure the on-call rotation is staffed, the first incident postmortems are documented, weekly operational dashboards are being reported, and the standards have been approved.


By Day 90: Define service-level objectives (SLOs) and configure alerts for the five most important customer journeys. Transition most production services into a continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) process. Introduce a monthly report covering DORA metrics and cloud costs. By the end of 90 days, ensure that SLOs and paging alerts are operational for all five customer journeys, deliver the first DORA and cloud-cost report to leadership, and establish an agreed-upon team hiring plan.

What will you need?

Required skills and experience

  • 8+ years in DevOps, SRE, or platform engineering, including 2+ years leading engineers.
  • Deep AWS experience, especially serverless (Lambda, EventBridge, and API Gateway), IAM, and RDS.
  • Built CI/CD with GitHub Actions, Azure Pipelines, or similar, including automated rollback.
  • Infrastructure as code in production (Terraform, OpenTofu, or CDK).
  • Ran on-call and incident management that measurably reduced incidents and time to restore.
  • Hands-on security operations: secrets management, access control, and vulnerability scanning.
  • Comfortable managing nearshore or distributed team members.

Differentiators

  • Data pipeline and data governance experience (e.g., Snowflake, data lakes, or event pipelines).
  • Datadog or CloudWatch at scale; OpenTelemetry.
  • Mobile release pipelines (App Store and Google Play).
  • PCI awareness from working with payments (Stripe).
  • AI tools for operations, such as incident summarization and runbook automation.

PERKS:

  • Health, vision, dental, long & short-term disability, and Life insurance
  • A Startup mentality company with stable funding
  • 401k match
  • Pet Care discounts
  • Flexible Time Off
  • Opportunity to grow your career with a network of like-minded professionals
