jobs.excerpt: About the RoleWe are hiring a Principal Platform Engineer to help build and scale our Azure-native cloud platform as we migrate services from an on-premises data center to the cloud.
jobs.description:
About the Role

We are hiring a Principal Platform Engineer to help build and scale our Azure-native cloud platform as we migrate services from an on-premises data center to the cloud. This is a hands-on engineering role with a strong mentoring component -- you will design and build alongside the team while raising the technical bar for engineers earlier in their careers. You will work across infrastructure, deployment automation, observability, and security tooling, with exposure to both legacy automation modernization and net-new platform capability.

This is an individual contributor role. You will not have direct reports, but you will be expected to mentor and provide technical guidance to junior and mid-level engineers on the team, including reviewing designs, pairing on complex problems, and setting technical direction by example.


What You'll Do

  • Design and build Azure infrastructure using a cloud native approach, leveraging managed services wherever they meet reliability and cost requirements.
  • Lead technical execution of the migration of services from an on-premises data center to Azure, including dependency mapping, migration sequencing, and cutover risk management.
  • Operate and extend our AKS-based platform, including GitOps deployment patterns, namespace isolation, and policy enforcement.
  • Own and evolve reusable Terraform modules that other engineering teams consume, with clear interface contracts between platform-owned and application-owned infrastructure.
  • Build and maintain observability coverage (metrics, logs, alerting) so that platform and application health are measurable and actionable, not just instrumented.
  • Apply policy-as-code to enforce security, compliance, and operational standards across the platform, and reduce reliance on manual review gates.
  • Design and review Identity and Access Management patterns, including workload identity, least-privilege access models, and secrets management -- with a clear bias away from static credentials.
  • Participate in business continuity and disaster recovery planning for platform services, including failover design, RTO/RPO definition, and recovery testing.
  • Contribute to CI/CD pipeline design and standards used across engineering teams building on the platform.
  • Use AI-assisted engineering tools (e.g., Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, or equivalent) as part of the standard workflow, and evaluate where AI-driven platform capabilities (automated remediation, intelligent alerting, natural-language operational tooling) can be responsibly introduced into the platform itself.
  • Mentor junior and mid-level engineers through code/design review, pairing, and informal technical coaching. Help less experienced engineers build sound judgment around idempotency, error handling, and migration candidacy when evaluating legacy automation.

Required Qualifications

  • 8+ years in platform, infrastructure, or site reliability engineering roles, with demonstrated Principal-level scope (technical leadership without formal management).
  • Deep hands-on experience with Azure, building cloud native architectures using managed services rather than defaulting to IaaS.
  • Production experience running and operating Kubernetes at scale, ideally AKS specifically.
  • Strong GitOps experience (ArgoCD, Flux, or equivalent) -- all infrastructure and cluster changes should trace to a git commit as a matter of practice, not preference.
  • Experience leading or significantly contributing to a data center-to-cloud migration, including business continuity and disaster recovery planning.
  • Working fluency in policy-as-code tooling (Kyverno, OPA/Gatekeeper, or equivalent) for security and compliance enforcement.
  • Strong Identity and Access Management background: workload identity federation, least-privilege IAM design, secrets management patterns that avoid static credentials.
  • Experience building and maintaining an observability stack (Prometheus, Grafana, Thanos, or equivalent).
  • Solid Terraform experience, including designing reusable modules consumed by other teams, not just single-project usage.
  • Practical, current experience using AI-assisted development tools in daily engineering work.
  • Demonstrated ability to mentor other engineers -- through review, pairing, or informal technical leadership -- without formal authority.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience designing or operating hub-and-spoke network architectures in Azure.
  • Familiarity with CI/CD pipeline design for multi-team, multi-repo environments (e.g., GitHub Actions-based runner infrastructure).
  • Exposure to evaluating or building genuinely AI-driven operational tooling (as distinct from rules-based automation mislabeled as AI).
  • Experience presenting technical tradeoffs to both engineering and business stakeholders.

jobs.description:
A vaga:

Esta vaga é destinada a um(a) Analista de Qualidade Pleno (QA) que atuará alocado(a) em um squad de desenvolvimento em um cliente do setor de energia.

No seu dia-a-dia você vai:

  • Atuar de forma integrada ao squad de desenvolvimento do cliente, trabalhando em conjunto com PO, desenvolvedores, UX/UI e demais profissionais envolvidos.
  • Participar das cerimônias ágeis do squad, contribuindo ativamente para o planejamento e acompanhamento das entregas.
  • Analisar requisitos, histórias de usuário e critérios de aceite, identificando inconsistências, riscos e possíveis cenários de falha.
  • Elaborar cenários e casos de teste considerando as regras de negócio e os diferentes fluxos da aplicação.
  • Executar testes funcionais, exploratórios, de integração, regressão e validação de regras de negócio.
  • Validar as funcionalidades desenvolvidas antes da disponibilização para homologação e/ou produção.
  • Identificar, registrar, documentar e acompanhar bugs e não conformidades, garantindo sua correta tratativa.
  • Trabalhar em conjunto com os desenvolvedores na investigação, reprodução e validação da correção de defeitos.
  • Realizar testes de regressão para garantir que novas implementações não impactem funcionalidades existentes.
  • Registrar evidências dos testes realizados e manter a documentação de qualidade atualizada.
  • Contribuir para a definição e evolução dos critérios de aceite e Definition of Done (DoD) do squad.
  • Apoiar o processo de homologação junto ao PO e stakeholders do cliente.
  • Identificar riscos de qualidade antecipadamente, atuando de forma preventiva durante o ciclo de desenvolvimento.
  • Contribuir para a melhoria contínua dos processos, padrões e práticas de qualidade utilizados pelo squad.
  • Apoiar a identificação de oportunidades para automação de testes, quando aplicável.
  • Acompanhar indicadores de qualidade e contribuir para a redução de bugs, retrabalho e reincidência de problemas.
  • Utilizar ferramentas e recursos de IA para apoiar atividades de análise, criação de cenários, testes e ganho de produtividade, quando aplicável.

Para fazer parte do time você deve ter:

Autonomia, visão crítica e postura propositiva, sendo capaz de questionar requisitos, antecipar problemas e sugerir melhorias e não apenas executar testes previamente definidos. É essencial que este profissional seja capaz de realizar testes automatizados.

Também é legal se você tiver:

  • Experiência em atuação dentro de squads ágeis.
  • Conhecimento em automação de testes e testes de API.
  • Experiência com ferramentas como Jira, Git e pipelines CI/CD.
  • Conhecimento e aplicação de IA para ganho de produtividade e melhoria das práticas de qualidade.

  • Design an academic program for “at risk” students and meet more frequently with students that have been placed on academic warning and probation.

Work with us
Our team are passionate in the pursuit of excellence and in pushing the boundaries of cancer therapy and Autoimmune disease to deliver life-changing treatments to patients.

Whilst working at Autolus you will enjoy a flexible, diverse and dynamic working environment which actively promotes creativity, leadership and teamwork – together we are ONE Autolus.

Job Description:

Job Title: Medical Science Liaison (MSL)

Reports to: Senior Director, National MSL Lead

Department: Medical Affairs

Hours: Full Time – 40 hours

Location: US – Remote

About Autolus

Autolus is a biopharmaceutical company, advancing innovative therapies at both clinical and commercial stages of development, focused on next-generation, programmed T cell therapies for the treatment of cancer. Using a broad suite of proprietary and modular T cell programming technologies, the company is engineering precisely targeted, controlled, and highly active T cell therapies designed to better recognize cancer cells, break down their defence mechanisms, and eliminate these cells. Autolus has a pipeline of product candidates in development for the treatment of haematological malignancies, solid tumours, and autoimmune diseases.

Why Autolus

Our team is passionate in the pursuit of excellence and in pushing the boundaries of cancer therapy and autoimmune diseases to deliver life-changing treatments to patients. Whilst working at Autolus you will enjoy a flexible, diverse, and dynamic working environment which actively promotes creativity, leadership and teamwork. In addition to this Autolus is proud to offer a competitive salary, performance related bonus as well as a comprehensive benefits package.

Our Promise

Autolus is developing complex, breakthrough therapies for a globally diverse market and equally recognises that diversity amongst our people is critical to our mission. As we draw on our differences, what we’ve experienced, and how we work, we celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

Role Summary

The MSL is responsible for scientifically engaging, collaborating and aligning with a broad range of external stakeholders to address identified patient needs and ultimately improve the practice of medicine for better patient access and outcomes.

MSLs leverage the right evidence at the right time during their scientific engagements and identify medical intelligence and opportunities that impact and inform medical scientific communication and collaboration, science data generation plans, launch excellence roadmap, patient journey and medical strategy.

MSLs also contribute to innovative partnerships and implement relevant disease area strategies. They act as a strategic scientific partner, and collaborate with other field colleagues (e.g., commercial, market access, HEOR, clinical research colleagues) supporting healthcare systems in order to strengthen and improve patient access and outcomes.

MSLs have a highly developed expertise in the role and therapeutic area and expect to undertake an enhanced level of responsibility.

Please note: This the ideal candidate will be based in New England or MA.

Key Responsibilities

  • Through scientific exchange establish, develop, maintain, and personalise long term professional partnerships with a broad range of external stakeholders including, but not limited to, healthcare professionals, medical experts, investigators, researchers, pharmacists, payers, opinion leaders in key hospitals, institutions, and organizations.
  • Communicate the right evidence to the right stakeholder at the right time in scientifically appropriate fashion, enabling stakeholders to make informed decisions.
  • Partnering with health systems and identifying external medical intelligence, data gaps, data generation opportunities (including RWE and implementation science, precision medicine, research collaborations), and key unmet needs and opportunities to help improve patient access and outcomes.
  • In collaboration with clinical research colleagues, support clinical trial process, including, but not limited to, research site recommendations, assistance in managing Investigator relationships, providing medical expertise when required.
  • Respond to unsolicited requests for information from stakeholders by sharing appropriate data regarding marketed and pipeline compounds in a timely, compliant, and stakeholder-focused manner.
  • Identify and share external medical intelligence, data gaps, data generation opportunities (including RWE and implementation science, precision medicine), and key un-met needs and opportunities to help improve patient access and outcomes.
  • Ensure appropriate identification and mapping of external stakeholders, aligned to the medical strategy, and in collaboration with other colleagues. Able to create personalised, flexible engagement strategies and plans, leveraging multiple channels and tailored content to meet the changing needs of external stakeholders.
  • Adopt and leverage digital channels for a broader, effective, personalised reach and impact, in addition to leading high level impactful scientific events, exchanges and medical education.
  • Apply foundational impactful scientific engagement principles in stakeholder interactions in alignment with medical strategy and portfolio/pipeline prioritisation.
  • Be a strategic internal partner, gather and leverage medical intelligence for an impactful contribution to Patient Journey mapping, launch excellence roadmap, integrated evidence generation plans, integrated product strategy and subsequently the medical strategy.
  • Utilise knowledge of assigned therapeutic area and compounds to serve as the medical, clinical, and scientific expert to field colleagues.
  • Typical activities of an MSL may include, but are not limited to, providing mentoring, guidance and formal field-training to Autolus colleagues, leading high level projects, executing special projects for the MSL Team Leader and representing the at Regional and Global meetings.
  • Manage personal and professional development.
  • Manage administrative responsibilities in a timely manner (customer relationship management tool, compliance training and other modules, expense reporting, etc.).
  • Promote and adhere to all company Ethics and Compliance Policies, and company guidelines for External Engagement.
  • Ability to travel 50% of the time, occasionally with short notice
  • KPIs
    • Time on field-related activities
    • Implementation of activities identified in plans
    • Quality of medical Intelligence gathered from external stakeholders
    • Management of processes and systems associated with field medical excellence

Demonstrated skills and competencies

Experience

  • Five years of MSL, or relevant industry, experience with CAR T launch experience and extensive knowledge of hematologic malignancies.
  • Solid business mentality including leadership skills; innovative, solution-oriented, and critical thinking with performance-focused drive to achieve objectives and execute tactics.
  • Proven history of process improvement and team building.
  • Experienced in attaining customer insights and driving change in day-to-day operations.
  • Ability to operate in an environment with little direction and produce exceptional results.
  • Excellent communication, interpersonal, and influencing skills, with the ability to communicate effectively across different channels to a variety of audiences.
  • Acts with credibility and clarity of purpose to build and maintain effective and collaborative relationships.
  • Application of a curious mindset, employing active listening skills and asking open questions to gain medical intelligence and uncover current thinking.
  • Capable of self-directed learning and having a growth mindset.
  • Capable to adapt, organise, prioritise, and work effectively and collaboratively in multifunctional teams in a dynamic field-based environment.
  • Strong personal integrity reflected in all actions and behaviours.

Qualifications

  • Allopathic or Osteopathic Medical degree. Pharm.D., PhD, Doctor of Nursing Practice, or an APP (MSN/Nurse Practitioner or MS/Physician Assistant, other Terminal degree in health/life sciences (preferred). Bachelors of Science in Nursing with a minimum of 5 years experience in patient care and/or clinical research focused on hematologic malignancies, combined with 5 years of relevant industry experience focused on CART therapies. (acceptable)

Skills/Specialist knowledge

  • Proven ability to successfully leverage new technology/digital/IT solutions for effective stakeholder mapping, development, management, and field medical intelligence gathering.
  • Deep knowledge of CAR-T therapy.
  • Good awareness of research procedures and guidelines relevant to the pharmaceutical industry.
  • High-level of critical thinking and problem-solving acumen.
  • Process mapping and analytical problem solving leading to improved outcomes.
  • Proficient in communicating plans/progress to different audiences (manager, director, V.P., GM, etc).
  • Proficient in PowerPoint, excel, word, and a variety of project management software.
  • Direct approach to solving problems with a level of ingenuity reflective of a small pharmaceutical company.
  • Resilient under high-pressure environments especially during the immediate months following launch.
  • Ability to demonstrate matrix management & leadership behaviours with project teams:
    • Set clear and compelling goals that show project team how their work contributes to our purpose and strategy.
    • Creating joint plans with your project team to deliver your goals, holding yourself and others accountable for delivering quality results.
    • Cultivating a network of relationships across the organisation and building high performing teams based on mutual trust and respect.
    • Acting as a role model ensuring everything you do is in line with our values of respect, integrity, focus and breakthrough.

Autolus Core Competencies

Focus on Results: Works to meet business goals set by management and leaders

What success looks like in this role:

We are seeking a motivated Automation Engineer with 6-8 years of experience to identify and eliminate repetitive manual work across our Steady State teams (Windows, Linux, Storage, and Backup) and turn it into reliable, reusable automation. This role is centered on discovery as much as delivery: partnering with Steady State to surface recurring tasks through interviews and ServiceNow ticket data, then codifying best practices, critical procedures, and common maintenance/deployment work using Ansible, GitLab CI/CD, HashiCorp Vault, Terraform, and the JFrog Artifactory suite (Xray, Catalog, and Curation).


Key Responsibilities:

  • Partner directly with Steady State teams to understand day-to-day operational work through interviews and shadowing.
  • Mine and analyze ServiceNow ticket data to identify recurring, manual, and time-consuming tasks, and quantify their frequency and effort.
  • Prioritize automation opportunities based on ticket volume, risk, and operational impact, and build use cases in partnership with Steady State leadership.
  • Codify best practices, critical procedures, and common maintenance/deployment tasks into reusable Ansible playbooks and roles.
  • Design and maintain Infrastructure as Code (IaC) using Terraform for repeatable provisioning and configuration.
  • Build and maintain GitLab CI/CD pipelines to package, test, and safely roll out automation to production.
  • Manage secrets, credentials, and certificates used by automation workflows through HashiCorp Vault.
  • Utilize JFrog Artifactory, including Xray, Catalog, and Curation, to manage and secure the artifacts produced by automation pipelines.
  • Validate that new automation matches or exceeds existing manual procedures before retiring the manual process.
  • Track and report on automation coverage and the resulting reduction in manual ticket volume.
  • Document automated processes, playbooks, and pipeline configurations.
  • Continuously revisit ticket trends to catch newly emerging repeat work and keep the automation backlog current.

You will be successful in this role if you have:

Qualifications:

  • BA/BS degree or equivalent experience and 6-8 years of experience in automation, DevOps, or platform engineering roles.
  • Hands-on experience with Ansible, Terraform, GitLab CI/CD, and HashiCorp Vault in a production environment.
  • Experience analyzing ticket/incident data (ServiceNow or similar ITSM tool) to identify automation opportunities.
  • Comfortable gathering requirements directly from operations teams through interviews and process walkthroughs.
  • Working knowledge of Windows and Linux systems administration, storage, and backup operations.
  • Solid scripting ability (Bash, Python, PowerShell, or similar).
  • Understanding of DevSecOps principles and software supply chain security.
  • Self-motivated and able to operate independently with minimal oversight.
  • Strong communication skills, with the ability to work across development, security, and operations teams.

Preferred Skills:

  • Experience with containerization and orchestration (Docker, Kubernetes).

jobs.title: Director - Member Engagement
jobs.excerpt: About Advanced Energy United Advanced Energy United is a national industry association representing businesses that provide the full range of advanced energy and transportation solutions.
jobs.description:
About Advanced Energy United

Advanced Energy United is a national industry association representing businesses that provide the full range of advanced energy and transportation solutions. Our team works to educate, advocate, and activate in decisionmaker venues across the country.

We advocate for public policies that enable competition and work alongside our member companies to create economic opportunity, lower consumer costs, and bolster energy reliability and resilience across the country. We work with decision makers at every level of government as well as regulators of energy markets to build progress toward an economy built on advanced energy.

If you’re an entrepreneurial, innovative, analytical and thoughtful person looking to make an impact in the clean energy space, United might be the perfect place for you to share your talents. Team members at United are given the trust and responsibility to make big things happen, and myriad opportunities to learn new skills, explore new issue areas, and work with a broad cross section of the clean energy community. Being a team member at United also means working with a talented and diverse group of people, some who bring decades of experience spanning advocacy, philanthropy, clean tech, government and more—and our collaborative approach means we get to learn from each other, expert and novice, every day. And while our organization is fully remote, we are proud of the people-focused culture we have built and the connectedness of our team.

We work on serious issues, take our mission seriously, but never take ourselves too seriously.

Position Description

Advanced Energy United (United) is seeking a highly energetic, organized, self-starting candidate who will think of member engagement holistically, incorporating high value industry events and ongoing member activities with a focus on growth for our member companies and for our organization. The Director of Member Engagement will be responsible for all aspects of United’s member engagement, including designing and implementing strategies to increase member value, foster retention, and build deeper engagement across the association’s membership base.

This role is responsible for creating a best-in-class member experience by developing programs, communications, and opportunities that connect members to each other, to policymakers, and to market intelligence. The candidate should be a relationship-driven leader with experience in membership organizations or customer success who thrives in a fast-paced, mission-driven environment. The ideal Director of Engagement will become an expert in the value, benefits, and features of all forms of Advanced Energy United membership.

This role requires a person that is able to thrive in a fast-paced and ever-dynamic business sector environment. The successful candidate will possess a high level of emotional intelligence.

The Director champions the member experience, ensuring that member companies understand, access, and realize value from their engagement with Advanced Energy United.

The Director of Engagement will report to the VP of Sales and Business Relations, working collaboratively with our sales, marketing, communications, and policy teams and will manage a team of their own.

Responsibilities

  • Lead strategy and activities to build and maintain member relationships and engagement with United
  • Develop and execute a data-driven member engagement strategy that strengthens relationships, increases meaningful participation, and demonstrates membership value.
  • Partner across Sales, Policy, Programs, Events, Communications, and other teams to deliver a coordinated member experience that connects member priorities with relevant advocacy initiatives, educational programming, events, and industry relationships.
  • Proactively address relationship gaps, emerging concerns, and disengagement risks through timely follow-up, issue resolution, and fulfillment of commitments.
  • Manage United’s annual member survey process
  • Lead United’s event strategy, planning, and execution. Work closely with policy team on successful member engagement and event content
  • Initiate and coordinate engagement activities in alignment with organization’s mission, vision, and goals
  • Manage and develop Advanced Energy United’s member engagement and data team along with external vendors

Required Qualifications

  • 7-10 years of member-related experience at a non-profit membership association, with a clear understanding of the role of trade associations
  • Direct experience coordinating small to mid-scale events both online and in-person in geographically dispersed locations
  • Independent and effective time management with excellent organizational skills and attention to detail
  • Interest in energy and transportation issues and an understanding of the importance of policy advocacy to advance an organizational agenda
  • Excellent interpersonal and relationship-building skills
  • Experience managing and mentoring junior staff
  • Excellent verbal and written communications skills, including the ability to independently draft clear, comprehensive, and persuasive written documents appropriate for intended audiences
  • Entrepreneurial approach, intellectual curiosity, and excellent listening and problem-solving skills
  • Performance-oriented individual with a strong work ethic, demonstrated initiative and commitment to achieving goals
  • Ability to travel on an as-needed basis up to 33% of the year for events, meetings, member engagement opportunities and staff training.

Physical Requirements

The physical requirements described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

The employee is regularly required to use hands and talk or hear. The employee is required to sit for long periods of time; reach with hands and arms; may need to balance, stoop, kneel or crouch, walk up and down stairs.

Job type: Full-time, regular (residence in the U.S. required)

Location: Remote.

Start date: November 2026

Salary: Starting at $120,000

Advanced Energy United Perks include:

• Medical, dental, and vision insurance for employees and their families

• Medical premiums covered for employees at 100%

• Flexible spending plans for health care and dependent care

• Profit Sharing opportunities, and annual merit-based compensation increases

• $75/month personal wellness reimbursement

• $50/month phone stipend

• Up to $200 reimbursement for home office set-up

• Accrued Paid Time Off, 11 Federal Holidays, and an annual end-of-year closure

• Parental Leave

• Professional development reimbursement

• 401(k) plan (with matching incentives)

• WMATA Transit Smart Benefits (DMV employees)

Advanced Energy United is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate in hiring or employment on the basis of race, color, religion, national origin, citizenship status, age, disability, sex, veteran status or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state or local laws, regulations or ordinances. If reasonable accommodations are needed to participate in the job application, interview process, and/ or to perform essential job functions please contact the Talent Acquisition team at . We are committed to the values of diversity, equity, inclusion, and justice across our organization (“DEIJ”). We also incorporate these values into our mission of making the energy we use secure, clean, and affordable. We know that varied perspectives and a commitment to social justice are needed to succeed in making the United States an advanced energy economy. We commit to building and supporting an inclusive workforce that represents different cultures, backgrounds, and viewpoints.

jobs.description:

This is a remote position.

GENERAL PURPOSE OF THE JOB:

The Prevailing Wage Administratoris primarily responsible for:

Responsible for coordination of all General Services project administration staff and GC Supervisor. Will oversee all facets of the WTI General Services product lines. Will be direct back up for GC Supervisor and assist with training and other special projects. Oversee performance metrics and administration based reporting.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Apply your understanding of prevailing wage laws to obtain and maintain compliance.
  • Conduct and Participate in project reviews.
  • Coordinate and track all prevailing wage projects.
  • Monitor fringe benefit values.
  • Perform a variety of administrative/clerical tasks related to prevailing wages, gather, compile, track, and report on information relevant to project assignments from multiple sources.
  • Compile and generate reports, statistics, timelines, tables, graphs, correspondence, presentations, and data entry related to prevailing wage.
  • Ensure timely and accurate processing, recording, and reporting of company’s certified payroll in various states including California, Washington, and Illinois.
  • Work with LCP Tracker or other software to complete certified payroll and other prevailing wage required documents.
  • Conduct reviews of sub-contractor’s Certified Payroll Registers and compliance documentation.
  • Ensure accurate processing, recording, and reporting of Certified Payroll Records (CPR).
  • Monitor and resolve any labor compliance violations.
  • Maintaining compliance spreadsheets.
  • Review and approve fringe benefit packages and fringe benefit statements.
  • Ensure Apprentice ratios are enforced.
  • Independently monitors contracts to ensure compliance, verifies that contractors have met contract wages and provided required reports and documentation, reviews and resolves differences in areas of non-compliance, and addresses other concerns, as necessary.
  • Serves as a liaison to the legal and compliance teams in cases of contract or other agency audits and researches, compiles, and provides agency data, files, documents, and records.
  • Ensure that the regular and prevailing wage/certified payroll is processed accurately, efficiently and in a timely manner.
  • Ensure the government agency rules and reporting deadlines are met and adhered to consistently.
  • Calculate and process timecards and corrections, including calculating overtime, deductions, per diems, subsistence, fringe benefits etc. in accordance with company policies and State, Federal and Union laws.

EXPERIENCE:

Two to four years related experience and/or training

SKILLS AND ABILITIES:

  • Must be action oriented
  • Ability to look for ways to achieve greater efficiency in process and procedure
  • Must demonstrate independent thinking and decision making skills
  • Must be customer focused with strong written and verbal communication
  • Strong interpersonal skills with the ability to make group presentations
  • Knowledge of Sarbanes-Oxley (compliance regulations for publicly traded companies)
  • Knowledge of Public procurement vehicles and Job Order Contracting work
  • Knowledge of State Prevailing Wage
  • Knowledge of David Bacon and SCA wages

OTHER QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities.
  • Exemplary organization and time management techniques.
  • Advanced course work or certification in business, finance, and/or accounting with applicable work experience.
  • Progressive experience related to payroll, accounting and finance experience in industry or consulting services.
  • Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Outlook, Excel, Word).
  • Advanced knowledge of Certified Payroll (California Prevailing Wage and Davis-Bacon) regulations and requirements.
  • Proven experience as payroll specialist or payroll coordinator.
  • Must be extremely organized, accurate, possess high level of attention to detail and be able to perform successfully under pressure and in a timely manner.
  • Maintain confidential information when required by legal and ethical standards of professionalism to ensure privacy of employee records.

Associate Director, Instructional Impact

College Board - CRA

Location: This is a remote role. Candidates who live near CB offices have the option of being fully remote or hybrid (Tuesday and Wednesday in office). All CB employees are required to occasionally travel to meet in person for business purposes.

Role Type: This is a full-time position

About the Team

The SAT Suite Program Access team leads the national strategy, implementation, and partner engagement efforts supporting states and districts administering the SAT Suite of Assessments. As digital transformation accelerates, our work increasingly centers on scalable systems, strong district partnerships, and effective implementation models that ensure every student benefits from high-quality assessment insights. As part of the K-12 SAT Suite Program Management & Partner Success team, we enable customer success, reinforce the value of the SAT Suite, and strengthen College Board's partnership with critical customers.

Program Access is organized around three peer Director functions, Instructional Strategy & Resource Systems, Community Strategy & Implementation, and Program Success Enablement, each of which owns a distinct set of educator- and partner-facing resources. This role sits alongside all three, providing the shared technical and instructional design capacity that turns each function's flagship resources into interactive, scalable digital experiences.


About the Opportunity

The Associate Director, Instructional Impact designs and builds digital companions, interactive, technology-enabled complements to core instructional, community, and enablement resources, in direct support of all three Program Access Directors and determines how each flagship resource is translated into an interactive experience. This role reports to the Senior Director, SAT Suite Program Access and Instructional Impact, and advises each Director on which resources warrant a companion and sets the design approach for each.

In the first months of this role, primary focus will be placed on partnering with the Director, SAT Suite Instructional Strategy & Resource Systems, building digital companions for flagship assets such as the Skills Insight Instructional Resource, the MVP Toolkit, and Teacher Implementation Guide updates, bringing these programs to scale quickly. From there, this role expands standardized digital companion support to the Community Strategy & Implementation and Program Success Enablement functions, ensuring all three directors benefit from a single, consistent, and reusable approach to digital companion development.


In this role, you will:

Build Digital Companions Supporting Our Instructional Strategy Team (≈40%)

  • Advise the director on which instructional assets to prioritize for companions and recommend the design approach for each.
  • Design and build digital companions for flagship instructional assets, including an interactive resource that helps students build test-taking skills, a starter toolkit for new districts, and updated guides that help teachers apply assessment results in the classroom
  • Decide how to restructure, condense, and sequence complex instructional content for interactive formats, weighing audience needs, accessibility, and build effort
  • Accelerate time-to-scale for priority instructional resources by pairing static materials with companion digital experiences

Extend Digital Companion Support Across Our District Engagement and Field Enablement Teams (≈30%)

  • Build digital companions in support of district engagement resources (for example, materials used to onboard and engage school districts in our community network, and kits used for in-person and virtual convenings)
  • Build digital companions in support of field enablement resources (for example, our field team's implementation and training deck used on the road, and content in our internal enablement resource hub)
  • Select the design approach for each companion based on its audience and use case (educators, districts, or field teams)

Establish a Standardized, Reusable Digital Companion Format (≈15%)

  • Own the companion standard, making and documenting decisions on format, tooling, accessibility approach, and component design, and determining when a request warrants an exception.
  • Set and maintain the documentation, templates, and component library that govern future builds
  • Reduce build time and increase consistency as companion coverage expands

Drive Cross-Functional Prioritization & Alignment (≈15%)

  • Recommend which resources receive digital companions and in what sequence, based on expected engagement impact and build effort, and secure alignment from the senior director and directors before development begins
  • Use usage data and partner feedback to continuously refine and expand digital companion coverage
  • Report on digital companion adoption and engagement impact across all three functions

About You

  • Bachelor's degree required; advanced degree (e.g., M.Ed., instructional design, educational technology) preferred
  • 3–5+ years of experience in instructional design, digital learning development, or educational technology content development
  • Required proficiency in authoring and publishing tools, including Articulate Storyline 360, Articulate Rise, Adobe Captivate, and Adobe Creative Cloud
  • Experience developing interactive digital learning assets, including simulations, multimedia, and JavaScript extensions
  • Familiarity with LMS technologies and emerging standards such as xAPI and cmi5
  • Experience implementing ADA Section 508/WCAG accessibility requirements in digital learning materials
  • Strong project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple concurrent stakeholders and priorities
  • Strong collaboration skills and the ability to work across a diverse set of colleagues, functions, and divisions
  • Commitment to educational equity and improving outcomes for students nationwide
  • The ability to travel occasionally to College Board offices or on behalf of College Board business
  • Bilingual candidates preferred
  • Experience building scalable "digital companion" or micro-learning models that complement larger static instructional or resource assets
  • Experience supporting multiple internal stakeholders or teams simultaneously with competing priorities and timelines
  • A track record of standing up reusable design systems, templates, or component libraries that reduced production time across a team

All roles at College Board require:

  • A passion for expanding educational and career opportunities and mission-driven work
  • Curiosity and enthusiasm for emerging technologies, with a willingness to experiment with and adopt new AI-driven solutions and comfort with learning and applying new digital tools independently and proactively.
  • Clear and concise communication skills, written and verbal
  • A learner's mindset and a commitment to growth: welcoming diverse perspectives, giving and receiving timely, respectful feedback, and continuously improving through iterative learning and user input.
  • A drive for impact and excellence: solving complex problems, making data-informed decisions, prioritizing what matters most, and continuously improving through learning, user input, and external benchmarking.
  • A collaborative and empathetic approach: working across differences, fostering trust, and contributing to a culture of shared success
  • Authorization to work in the United States

About Our Process

  • Application review will begin immediately and will continue until the position is filled. This role is expected to accept applications for a minimum of 5 business days.
  • While the hiring process may vary, it generally includes: resume and application submission, recruiter phone/video screen, hiring manager interview, performance exercise such as live coding, a panel interview, a conversation with leadership and reference checks.

What We Offer

At College Board, we offer more than a paycheck: we provide a meaningful career, a supportive team, and a comprehensive package designed to help you thrive. We’re a self-sustaining nonprofit that believes in fair and competitive compensation grounded in your qualifications, experience, impact, and the market.

A Thoughtful Approach to Compensation

  • The hiring range for this role is $56,000 - $95,000.
  • Your exact salary will depend on your location, experience, and how your background compares to others in similar roles at the College Board.
  • We aim to make our best offer upfront, rooted in fairness, transparency, and market data.
  • We adjust salaries by location to ensure fairness, no matter where you live.

You’ll have open, transparent conversations about compensation, benefits, and what it’s like to work at College Board throughout your hiring process. Check out our careers page for more.

jobs.description:
Job Position: Paid & Performance Marketing Lead

Company: Pro Coffee Gear

Location: Remote (Anywhere)

Type: Full-time

Reports to: VP of Product & Growth

About Us:Pro Coffee Gear is a fast-growing ecommerce and wholesale distributor of commercial and home espresso equipment. We serve cafés, roasters, restaurants, and serious home baristas with new and refurbished espresso machines, grinders, and accessories from the most respected brands in coffee. We’re building a disciplined, data-driven growth engine — and paid media is a critical part of that foundation.

The Role: We’re hiring a Paid & Performance Marketing Lead to own the strategy, performance, and evolution of paid acquisition at PCG. This role will manage and lead our existing Google and Meta ad agencies, while also setting the roadmap to progressively bring paid media in-house as the business scales.

You will be the single owner of paid performance — accountable for results, agency direction, channel expansion, and long-term capability building.

What You'll Own:

1. Paid Media Ownership & Agency Leadership

  • Own overall paid media strategy and performance across Google Ads (Search, Shopping, Performance Max, YouTube) and Meta (Facebook & Instagram)
  • Act as the primary owner and point of accountability for external paid media agencies, channel-level strategy and prioritization, and budget allocation and pacing
  • Set clear goals, KPIs, and expectations for agencies
  • Review performance, challenge assumptions, and approve strategy
  • Ensure agency work aligns with PCG business goals, merchandising priorities, and creative and brand standards
  • You are not a passive agency manager — you own the outcome

2. Transition from Agency-Led to In-House Execution

  • Assess what should remain agency-managed vs brought in-house
  • Build a roadmap to reduce agency dependency over time and increase internal ownership of strategy and execution
  • Personally execute and optimize campaigns where appropriate
  • Define tooling, processes, and documentation required to scale in-house
  • Hire or develop additional paid media support as needed

3. Google Ads (Primary Revenue Channel)

  • Own Google Ads performance end-to-end, whether executed by agency or in-house: brand, non-brand, and SKU-level search; shopping and feed optimization; Performance Max (with strict controls); YouTube for upper-funnel education
  • Partner with merchandising to prioritize SKUs, manage inventory constraints, and support launches, refurbished inventory, and clearance
  • Ensure strong alignment between search intent, landing pages, and conversion tracking

4. Meta Ads (Demand Creation + Retargeting)

  • Own Meta strategy across prospecting (education-driven, high-intent audiences), retargeting (site, CRM, engagement-based), and product launches and promotional bursts
  • Direct creative strategy in partnership with internal creative teams
  • Review and approve creative testing plans and results
  • Ensure Meta is used to create demand, support high-AOV consideration cycles, and feed lifecycle marketing

5. Channel Expansion & Experimentation

  • Own testing and expansion into additional paid channels: Reddit, LinkedIn (wholesale, restaurant operators), affiliate and partner marketing, and influencer whitelisting/paid creator ads
  • Decide when experiments are agency-led vs in-house
  • Define clear hypotheses, success metrics, and scale/kill decisions

6. Measurement, Reporting & Forecasting

  • Own performance reporting across all paid channels and agencies
  • Track and optimize toward blended MER, contribution margin, paid revenue vs plan, and lead revenue conversion (30/60/120 days)
  • Build clear weekly and monthly reporting for leadership
  • Ensure attribution, tracking, and data integrity are solid and improving

7. Cross-Functional Leadership

  • Partner closely with merchandising (inventory, pricing, promotions), lifecycle marketing (email/SMS, lead nurturing), creative (ads, landing pages, messaging), and sales/wholesale (lead quality, follow-up loops)
  • Translate company goals into actionable paid media strategy
  • Represent paid media in planning, launches, and retrospectives

What Success Looks Like:

First 3–6 months

  • Clear ownership and accountability over agency performance
  • Strong visibility into spend, performance, and ROI
  • Improved alignment between paid media, merch, and creative

6–12 months

  • More paid execution owned internally
  • Reduced agency dependency without performance loss
  • At least one new paid channel successfully tested
  • Paid media viewed as a predictable, scalable growth engine

Who You Are:

Required

  • 5–8+ years in paid/performance marketing
  • Deep experience with Google Ads and Meta Ads
  • Proven experience managing and scaling agency relationships
  • Strong analytical and financial mindset
  • Comfortable owning revenue and efficiency metrics

Bonus

  • Experience bringing paid media in-house from agencies
  • High-AOV ecommerce or B2B-adjacent experience
  • Shopify-based ecommerce experience
  • Experience in coffee, hospitality, or equipment-based businesses

Why This Role Is Compelling:

  • True ownership over a critical growth lever
  • Authority to challenge agencies and set direction
  • Opportunity to build a best-in-class in-house paid function
  • High-impact role with visibility across the business
  • Work on meaningful, long-consideration products

Benefits:

  • Flexible schedule with opportunities for growth
  • Work remotely from the comfort of your own home
  • Join a dynamic and passionate international team in the exciting world of coffee

How to Apply:If you're ready to join our team and play a key role in shaping our talented workforce, please submit your resume in English (resumes in other languages will be immediately disqualified). We look forward to hearing from you!

Pro Coffee Gear is an equal-opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

MiracleFeet is a global nonprofit working to eliminate one of the leading causes of physical disability worldwide. Since 2010, MiracleFeet’s proven, scalable model is supported by a suite of custom measurement and evaluation tools developed with our partners. To date, MiracleFeet has delivered quality clubfoot treatment to more than 127,000 children in 555 clinics in 38 countries across Sub-Saharan Africa, Latin America, Asia, and the Middle East and North Africa. Arrow Enterprise Computing Solutions (ECS), a part of Arrow Electronics, brings innovative IT solutions to the market to solve complex business challenges. We help businesses grow faster, operate efficiently and transform in a dynamic market.

As a Copilot Lead, you own Arrow’s strategy for the Microsoft Copilot portfolio — a strategic, high-visibility area of Microsoft’s AI business. You define, in alignment with the AI Business Solutions Lead, how Arrow accelerates Copilot adoption and sales as a distributor, and you make that strategy real through frameworks, motions and campaigns.

You are the connection point between Microsoft, Arrow’s country teams and our partners. Your job is to enable our teams first, then our partners, and ultimately their customers — turning Microsoft’s Copilot vision into practical offers that land in every region and country.


Key responsibilities

  • Own the strategy for the Copilot pillar for Arrow, in alignment with the direction set by the AI Business Solutions Lead, and translate it into a concrete, prioritised plan.
  • Align with Microsoft and stakeholders by acting as Arrow’s point of contact with Microsoft and internal/external stakeholders to agree the joint strategy, priorities and investments for Copilot.
  • Build frameworks and go-to-market motions that make it easy for countries and partners to sell and deliver — repeatable initiatives, offers and playbooks designed to accelerate sales.
  • Drive country adoption as the central point of contact for all country teams: launch initiatives, follow up on execution, and make sure every motion lands consistently across all regions and countries.
  • Serve the layers: internal country team, partners and their end customers — enabling each layer before moving to the next.
  • Lead marketing campaigns for the pillar, in coordination with our marketing contact and Microsoft, to generate demand and pipeline.
  • Skill up teams and partners by defining and running enablement on Copilot products for internal teams and the partner ecosystem.
  • Create packaged services — turning products into ready-to-sell services, motions and frameworks that partners and countries can take to market.

Example initiatives you will build

Concrete examples of the kind of motions and frameworks you will design and roll out:

  • Copilot Adoption Workshops — a repeatable, country-ready workshop format that partners can deliver to customers.
  • Copilot readiness and assessment frameworks to help partners qualify and prepare customers.
  • AI adoption and change-management playbooks that drive usage, seats and consumption after go-live.
  • Copilot Center of Excellence blueprints for partners and larger customers.
  • Sales-acceleration frameworks and packaged offers that shorten the path from interest to deployment.

  • Experience building go-to-market motions, sales enablement frameworks, or channel/partner programmes.

Key competencies

  • Fluent English — 100% written and spoken; this role works across all countries and directly with Microsoft.
  • Organised and structured — keeps many initiatives, countries and stakeholders moving without dropping follow-up.
  • Creative — able to design new motions, campaigns and frameworks from a blank page.

jobs.title: Director, Finance & Investment
jobs.excerpt: About Encore Renewable EnergyEncore Renewable Energy is a leading integrated clean energy services company headquartered in Burlington, Vermont, focused on developing, building, owning and operating sustainable, high return community-scale solar PV systems, large scale energy storage applications and 21st century solutions for the redevelopment of underutilized property.
jobs.description:
About Encore Renewable Energy

Encore Renewable Energy is a leading integrated clean energy services company headquartered in Burlington, Vermont, focused on developing, building, owning and operating sustainable, high return community-scale solar PV systems, large scale energy storage applications and 21st century solutions for the redevelopment of underutilized property.
Encore is a dynamic, high-growth, team-oriented, entrepreneurial company. We are a group of colleagues committed to the triple bottom line of people, planet, profit, and are willing to take on responsibilities outside of our comfort zone. We hope you are too!

Encore seeks an experienced, commercially minded finance professional to serve as Director / Senior Director - Finance & Investment. This individual will be a senior member of Encore's finance team, with responsibility for leading project finance underwriting, capital formation, investment analysis, and transaction execution across Encore's solar and energy storage portfolio. The role requires the ability to independently own complex workstreams, exercise sound investment judgment, communicate effectively with senior management and capital partners, and drive transactions from initial evaluation through closing and ongoing portfolio management.

Encore is a dynamic, high-growth, team-oriented, fast-paced entrepreneurial company. We want colleagues who are willing to take on broad ownership and accountability to achieve results. Working closely with the Chief Financial and Investment Officer, the successful candidate will be expected to operate with a high degree of autonomy, develop and mentor junior team members, and serve as a trusted partner to colleagues across development, construction, asset management, accounting, legal, and executive leadership.

Your Responsibilities

  • Lead financial modeling, underwriting, and investment decision-making across Encore's project finance investments, M&A, capital raising (including construction debt, back-leverage, tax equity and tax credit transfers), and business development activities

  • Own the evaluation of project and portfolio investments, including returns analysis, capital-at-risk assessment, financing assumptions, downside cases, sensitivities, and recommendations to senior leadership

  • Lead the preparation and presentation of investment materials to management and investment committees throughout the project lifecycle, clearly articulating key risks, value drivers, underwriting assumptions, and recommendations

  • Lead financing transactions from strategy through closing, including structuring, financial modeling, lender and investor engagement, due diligence, term sheet negotiation, documentation, closing mechanics, and post-closing compliance and relationship management

  • Develop and maintain relationships with banks, tax equity investors, tax credit buyers, institutional capital providers, advisors, and other financing counterparties; support capital-markets strategy and evaluation of new financing structures

  • Partner with development and commercial teams to evaluate project economics, price offtake opportunities, assess acquisition opportunities, and establish financial parameters that support disciplined investment decisions

  • Oversee recurring financial and portfolio reporting to capital partners and senior management, ensuring accurate, timely, decision-useful analysis and clear communication of performance, risks, liquidity, and capital requirements

  • Partner closely with accounting, treasury, legal, construction, and asset management teams to ensure financing assumptions, forecasts, transaction requirements, and financial reporting are appropriately integrated

  • Own and continuously improve Encore's project finance models, underwriting standards, investment-committee processes, reporting tools, and transaction workflows, with an emphasis on scalability, consistency, controls, and efficient use of data

  • Provide leadership, coaching, and quality control for junior finance team members, including review of models, analyses, presentations, and transaction deliverables

  • Serve as a senior finance resource across the organization and take ownership of strategic and ad hoc analyses as business needs evolve

Your Experience

  • 8+ years of relevant transactional experience in project finance, infrastructure investing, M&A, investment banking, or principal investing, with significant experience in the U.S. renewable energy sector; Senior Director candidates will generally be expected to bring 10+ years of relevant experience and a demonstrated record of leading complex transactions

  • Demonstrated experience independently leading renewable energy financings or investments through closing, including responsibility for structuring, underwriting, diligence, negotiation, documentation, and internal approvals

  • Deep understanding of U.S. renewable energy project finance, including construction debt, back-leverage, tax equity, ITC transferability, project-level cash waterfalls, debt sizing and covenant analysis; experience with both solar and energy storage strongly preferred

  • Advanced financial modeling skills and demonstrated ability to build, audit, manage, and interpret complex project and portfolio finance models; ability to translate model outputs into clear investment recommendations

  • Strong commercial and investment judgment, with the ability to identify material risks, challenge assumptions, balance competing considerations, and make recommendations with incomplete information

  • Demonstrated ability to manage multiple complex transactions and priorities simultaneously, establish workplans and deadlines, and drive cross-functional teams toward decisions and closing milestones

  • Experience managing relationships with senior internal stakeholders and external capital providers, including banks, institutional investors, tax equity investors, advisors, and legal counsel

  • Strong executive-level written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to distill complex financial and transaction matters for senior management, investment committees, boards, and external counterparties

  • Demonstrated leadership capabilities, including mentoring and developing junior team members, reviewing analytical work product, and establishing high standards for accuracy, judgment, and execution

  • Bachelor's degree in finance, economics, business, engineering, mathematics, statistics, or a related field; MBA or other relevant graduate degree is a plus

  • Expert-level proficiency in Excel and PowerPoint; experience with VBA, Python, Power BI, or other analytical and automation tools is a plus

  • Working technical and commercial knowledge of solar and battery energy storage technologies and the principal revenue, operating, interconnection, and construction considerations affecting project economics

  • Self-starter with a high degree of ownership, accountability, integrity, and emotional intelligence; comfortable operating independently in an entrepreneurial environment while collaborating effectively across functions

  • Team-oriented leader with a willingness to work across organizational boundaries and take on responsibilities beyond a narrowly defined role when needed

Life at Encore

Our team is our single greatest asset and that of which we are most proud. Encore team members share a single mission – building the clean energy economy of the future in a responsible manner that creates high quality jobs and enhances the communities in which our projects operate.
We invest heavily in our team – here are a few of the perks and benefits we offer:
●Complete, high quality medical benefits that include flex time options for child and family care and extended parental leave
●100% of health-care premiums funded by Encore
●Work-life balance with flexible work schedules (remote work opportunities) and attractive paid-time off policy
●11 paid holidays (includes 1 floating holiday of employee’s choice)
●One paid volunteer day each fiscal quarter
●401k profit sharing
●Employee equity participation program
●Continuing education and tuition assistance

Justice, Diversity, Equity, Inclusion

Encore believes that an equitable and inclusive work environment, and a diverse, empowered team are key to achieving our mission. We are not looking for candidates who are “culture fits.” We are looking for candidates who can expand our culture, challenge business as usual, and bring their whole selves to work. We strive to provide all candidates with an equitable and accessible recruitment process.
Encore provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, veteran status, or genetics. In addition to federal law requirements, Encore complies with applicable state and local laws governing nondiscrimination in employment in every location in which Encore has facilities. This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation and training.
Don’t meet every single requirement? Studies have shown that women and people of color are less likely to apply to jobs unless they meet every single qualification. If you’re excited about this role but your experience doesn’t align perfectly with every qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate.

The Client Manager Associate is responsible for supporting the profitability, persistency, and expansion of their assigned book of business. Success in this role requires strong relationship management skills, a customer-focused mindset, analytical capabilities, and broad knowledge of group insurance products and services.

You Are

A relationship-driven professional who enjoys partnering with clients and brokers to solve problems and deliver value.   • Eligible for variable compensation based on achievement of persistency, renewal, and cross-sell/add-issue goals in accordance with the annual Group Sales Incentive Compensation Plan for Client Manager Associates.

Reporting Relationships

  • As our Client Manager Associate, Premier Market, you will report to the appropriate Client Management Leader within the Premier Market organization.

Location

  • Preferred locations include Northern California, Denver, CO, Seattle, WA, Portland, OR, Salt Lake City, UT, or Spokane, WA.
  • This position is remote-based.

Travel

The salary for this position ultimately will be determined based on the education, experience, knowledge, and abilities of the successful candidate. jobs.excerpt: EARLY CHILDHOOD DEVELOPMENT AND HEALTH BOARDFirst Things First (Arizona Early Childhood Development and Health Board) is an essential leader and partner in creating a family-centered, equitable, high-quality early childhood system that supports the development, well-being, health and early education of all Arizona’s children, birth to age 5.
jobs.description:
EARLY CHILDHOOD DEVELOPMENT AND HEALTH BOARD

First Things First (Arizona Early Childhood Development and Health Board) is an essential leader and partner in creating a family-centered, equitable, high-quality early childhood system that supports the development, well-being, health and early education of all Arizona’s children, birth to age 5. Created by voter initiative in 2006, First Things First is governed by a state Board with 28 regional partnership councils. First Things First is a decentralized organization that engages diverse constituencies to accomplish its mission. Organizational values include a commitment to diversity, equity and inclusion; a focus on accountability, transparency, coordination and collaboration; and an emphasis on the outcomes that will ensure young children start kindergarten healthy and ready to succeed in school and in life.

Sr Director Programs & Research and Evaluation

Job Location:

Address: 4000 N Central Avenue, Suite 500, Phoenix, AZ 85012

Posting Details:

Salary: 99,000

Grade: 25

Job Summary:

The Programs & Research and Evaluation Senior Director works under the direction of the Chief Program & Evaluation Officer and is a member of the senior leadership team responsible for leading an integrated portfolio combining program strategy development, implementation, and evaluation. The Senior Director oversees the planning and execution of agency-wide research, strategy development and implementation, and evaluation studies in alignment to the FTF Strategic Plan. Simultaneously, this position is responsible for directing programmatic grant processes and technical assistance to ensure strategies are supported by research evidence and best practice, aligned with regional needs and Board priorities, and connected to measurable outcomes. Additionally, the Senior Director oversees data systems development, manages vendor performance, disseminates findings to key stakeholders, and provides direct supervision to Program and Evaluation Specialists.

This position may offer the ability to work remotely, within Arizona, based upon the department's business needs and continual meeting of expected performance measures.

The State of Arizona strives for a work culture that affords employees flexibility, autonomy, and trust. Across our many agencies, boards, and commissions, many State employees participate in the State’s Remote Work Program and are able to work remotely in their homes, in offices, and in hoteling spaces. All work, including remote work, should be performed within Arizona unless an exception is properly authorized in advance.

Job Duties:

Program Leadership & Strategy Development and Implementation
● Supervise and support Program Specialists in the development, revision, and implementation of early education, literacy and family support and children’s health strategies, services, and programs, ensuring alignment with current research evidence, effective practices, and regional/tribal needs.
● Lead the programmatic aspects of the grant process—including development and revision of standards of practice, scopes of work, and theories of change—ensuring work is cohesive, supported by research evidence, and connected to outcomes.
● Develop and implement an approach to synthesize qualitative and quantitative data to monitor program implementation, provide timely technical assistance and ensure grant partner accountability.
● Guide Program Specialists to use data to support staff across FTF teams and FTF councils with strategy implementation and strategic priorities.
● Possess strong communication skills to lead and facilitate discussions with regional councils, state agencies and other system partners, and grant partners to solicit and listen to feedback, navigate differing perspectives, communicate planned changes, rationale and decisions clearly to build shared understanding. Additionally, synthesize and incorporate relevant feedback into strategy development and revisions and work products.
● Knowledge of current research and issues, including effective programs and policy related to the early childhood system.
● Inform FTF strategies, decision-making, and policy work using latest research available
on early childhood topics, including emerging state and national issues affecting Arizona.

Research & Evaluation Oversight

  • Lead and supervise Evaluation Specialists in analysis of statewide and regional strategy implementation and outcome data collection, monitoring and reporting, as well as population-level and/or programmatic early childhood data, to identify trends that inform program and policy implications.
    ● Plan and manage multiple studies (e.g., statutorily required studies,
    strategy-specific studies) and other ad hoc projects identified as part of executing the FTF Strategic Plan. This includes, establishing goals with the Chief Program/Data Officer, setting timelines, effectively communicating priorities to FTF colleagues, developing project scopes of work including methodology/design, developing deliverable plans, and managing vendor performance to meet deliverables.
    ● Coordinate with the FTF Tribal Relations team to plan implementation data efforts, tribal regional studies and develop related materials (e.g., tribal approval documents) in compliance with the FTF Tribal Data Policy.
    ● Lead efforts and/or direct Program and Evaluation Specialists in the development of data systems with internal IT staff and/or external contractors (e.g., Early Childhood Workforce Registry) to support grant partner data submission that will inform strategy outcomes. This is inclusive of developing business requirements, planning data system design and specific fields, writing report logic and codebook, and providing overall direction to IT report writers, for internal and external systems.
    ● Summarize analytical results in technical data reports, policy briefs, and presentations tailored for the FTF Board, Regional Councils, staff, and external stakeholder groups.
    ● Meet with FTF Regional Councils, staff, and local stakeholders to collect input related to FTF research and evaluation activities.

Early Childhood System Work and Data System Integration
● Represent First Things First in statewide early childhood coalitions, advisory groups, workgroups, and other cross-agency initiatives, providing programmatic and early childhood systems expertise and advancing coordination and alignment among state, local, tribal, public, and private partners.
● Represent FTF with state and local partners to develop shared data fields and related protocols and processes towards accessing data as part of FTF research and evaluation efforts and Early Childhood System work.
● Convene cross-agency/system partner committees to gather stakeholder input to identify opportunities for alignment and coordination, build shared understanding,
and support collaborative solutions that improve services and outcomes for young children and families and strengthen the Arizona early childhood system.
● Provide strategic leadership in connecting and leveraging data across FTF and partner systems to answer broader programmatic, policy, and early childhood systems questions. Identify opportunities to link or integrate data sources, develop cross-system questions and analytical approaches. Additionally, collaborate with agency partners, IT, and other stakeholders to use data to better understand service reach, system interactions, gaps, outcomes, and opportunities for improvement.
● Collaborate with FTF IT, Finance, and External Affairs staff (e.g., Communications, Tribal Relations) to handle data exchanges/data sharing agreements (e.g., MOUs), data security and maintenance protocols, as well as policies related to public dissemination of data.

Supervision & Cross-Functional Support

  • Provide direct and project-based supervision to Program and Evaluation Specialists in accordance with agency policies and applicable laws.
    ● Serve as a subject matter expert on internal Cross-Functional Teams (CFTs), providing evaluation, reporting, and data expertise to support regional councils and staff through tools, training, and strategic guidance.
    ● Collaborate with other Senior Directors to support shared agency work, such as grant application processes and programmatic improvement initiatives.
    ● Perform duties in a manner that supports the internal culture and mission with respect and cooperation.
    ● Support additional opportunities as related to the role and Program & Research and Evaluation functions.
Knowledge, Skills & Abilities (KSAs):
  • Doctoral degree (PhD) with three years of experience or Master’s degree with five years of experience in early childhood development/education, developmental psychology, research methodology, public health, social work, public policy, public administration, educational psychology, or related field. Doctoral degree (PhD) is preferred.
    ● Excellent interpersonal and communication skills and ability to collaborate within and between teams, give and receive constructive feedback, work independently, take initiative, and be self-directed.
    ● Exceptional personal and professional integrity and credibility with the propensity to identify areas for self-improvement.
    ● Demonstrates flexibility and ability to adapt to changing demands to manage multiple and often simultaneous tasks with accuracy while meeting deadlines; demonstrates strong critical thinking, problem solving, and analytical skills.
    ● Experience in leading/mentoring team members through professional growth, constructive feedback, and regular coaching. Ability to build a collaborative, equitable work culture that supports diverse team perspectives and builds morale, while motivating staff to meet deadlines.
    ● Demonstrated experience in both program development/implementation and research/evaluation methodologies within early childhood or human services systems.
    ● Experience with statistical software (e.g., SPSS) to manage data sets (including codebooks and syntax); conduct quantitative data analyses ranging from descriptive to multivariate analyses (including trend analyses); and conduct qualitative data analyses.
    ● Experience creating data reports, inclusive of the ability to communicate a blueprint and/or report specifications and logic to internal IT staff and/or external database vendors.
    ● Adaptable and reliable in the face of conflict and crisis; ability to discern and be tactful; attentive to the perspectives and competing interests of various internal and external stakeholders; effectively handle situations requiring tact, judgment, and composure; discernment in communication with staff members from various levels of the organization, including executive leadership.

Remote work is a management option and not an employee entitlement or right. An agency may terminate a remote work agreement at its discretion.
