jobs.excerpt: About SlasifySlasify is a global HR platform that helps businesses hire, pay, and manage teams in 150+ countries and 130+ currencies — without setting up local entities.
jobs.description:
About Slasify

Slasify is a global HR platform that helps businesses hire, pay, and manage teams in 150+ countries and 130+ currencies — without setting up local entities. Through our Employer of Record (EOR), global payroll, and contractor management solutions, we take on the compliance, tax, and administrative complexity of international employment so you can focus on growth.

We put the human in HR tech. Rather than relying on software alone, we pair smart technology with real people — dedicated account manager support, localized expertise, and hands-on guidance at every step.

Headquartered in Singapore, with teams across the Americas, Europe, and Asia-Pacific, we deliver expert support with local understanding wherever our clients grow.

Slasify — Where People Thrive.

The Role

We are building a talent pool of freelance writers for upcoming content needs. We will review applications and contact suitable candidates as assignments become available.

We have built an AI-assisted content workflow that creates briefs, first drafts, and editorial reviews. We are looking for a writer who can run this workflow, check every fact, and turn AI drafts into articles that sound human and are safe to publish.

You will not write from a blank page, but you need a solid understanding of SEO and GEO. You will review each AI-generated brief and catch anything that looks off before drafting starts. Your value is your judgment: knowing what is wrong, what is missing, and what does not sound right.

Location: Remote — open to freelancers worldwide | Type: Freelance, paid per article

What You Will Do

  • Run our content workflow: Use our AI tools and writing guides to create a brief, a first draft, and an editorial review for each assigned topic.
  • Review the brief: Check that the keyword, angle, and structure make sense before drafting. Flag anything that looks off.
  • Match search intent: Make sure every article answers what the reader actually searched for. If a section does not help answer that question, fix it or cut it.
  • Verify every fact: Our drafts mark every legal, tax, and payroll figure for checking. You find the current figure on the official government source and add an inline link.
  • Edit for voice: Remove generic AI phrasing so each article sounds clear, specific, and human.
  • Check SEO and GEO structure: Make sure keywords, headings, FAQ answers, and internal links follow our guidelines.
  • Find and prepare images: Download images from Canva, convert them to WebP (under 150 KB), and write descriptive alt text for each one.
  • Submit and revise: Send the finished article to our content lead and update it based on feedback.
  • Proofread: Review existing articles for grammar, clarity, and outdated facts when needed.

Our Writing Style

  • Clear, direct, and helpful
  • Simple words and short sentences, because many of our readers are not native English speakers
  • American English spelling
  • No em dashes

What to Expect

  • About 4 to 6 articles per month
  • 1,200 to 2,500 words per article, depending on the topic type
  • Article ready for review within 5 business days
  • Up to 2 rounds of revisions included
  • You will use your own paid Claude account
  • All work is confidential. You will sign an NDA before you start.

Pay

  • Full article (brief to final draft, including images): from USD 50
  • Proofreading an existing article: USD 20
  • Rates for longer or more complex articles are open to discussion.

Must-Haves

  • Fluent English Writing: Native-level English writing and editing skills, with clear grammar and a natural style.
  • SEO & GEO Knowledge: Working knowledge of search intent, keyword placement, heading structure, and how AI search tools pick up content. You should be able to spot problems in a brief before drafting starts.
  • AI Tool Experience: Hands-on experience using AI tools, such as Claude or ChatGPT, to create professional content.
  • Fact-Checking Skills: Strong habits for checking facts, and comfortable finding and reading official government sources.
  • AI Voice Editing: Able to spot AI-sounding text and rewrite it in a natural, human way.

Nice to Have

  • B2B Content Experience: Prior experience writing for a B2B audience, ideally in HR tech, fintech, or SaaS.
  • GEO/AEO Expertise: Familiarity with Google’s E-E-A-T principles (Experience, Expertise, Authoritativeness, Trustworthiness) and how to show them in content.
  • Industry Knowledge: Basic understanding of global remote work, cross-border compliance, payroll, or EOR.
  • AI Workflow Experience: Experience with prompt-based or multi-step AI workflows.
  • SEO Tools: Experience with Ahrefs, SEMrush, or Ubersuggest.
  • Canva Pro Account: Gives you access to a wider range of images.

How to Apply

In the application, please include the following:

  1. Your resume
  2. 2 to 3 links to published articles. B2B or regulated topics are preferred.
  3. A few sentences on how you use AI tools in your writing today, and how you check what they produce.

Shortlisted candidates will complete a paid editing test. We will send you an AI-generated draft, and you will fix it for accuracy, voice, and structure.

Equal Employment Opportunity Disclaimer

At Slasify, we value your privacy and are committed to protecting your personal data. We provide equal employment opportunities and do not discriminate against candidates based on race, color, gender, age, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, marital status, citizenship, disability, or any other legally protected status or characteristic. Additionally, we do not require candidates to provide photographs or any personal information unrelated to the applied position during the application process. Our hiring decisions are based solely on qualifications, skills, and experience relevant to the position.

jobs.excerpt: About K3 Tax AdvisoryK3 Tax Advisory provides strategic tax advisory and planning services to clients undertaking complex transactions and business planning, helping them manage tax risk and maximise value.
jobs.description:
About K3 Tax Advisory

K3 Tax Advisory provides strategic tax advisory and planning services to clients undertaking complex transactions and business planning, helping them manage tax risk and maximise value.

Our team comprises highly experienced Chartered Accountants and Chartered Tax Advisers who provide a broad range of specialist tax advisory services. We work with owner-managed businesses, private equity-backed organisations and corporates operating both in the UK and internationally.

We operate a fully remote working model, giving our people the flexibility to work from the location that suits them, with the option to use office space across the UK.

We are committed to attracting, developing and retaining early-career talent. Our structured Internship Programme is an important part of this commitment and acts as the primary pathway into our Graduate Programme.

K3 Tax Advisory is part of K3 Advisory Group, a market-leading professional services group providing high-quality advice across Business Sales, Tax, Restructuring, Technology Solutions and Financial Services.

About the Internship Programme

Our paid Summer Internship Programme runs for six weeks, four days per week from Monday to Thursday.

The programme gives you the opportunity to experience the tax profession first-hand, working alongside experienced tax professionals and contributing to real client assignments.

Tax is constantly evolving, and the work we undertake helps clients understand and manage their tax affairs while making significant business and commercial decisions.

Throughout your internship, you will be supported by a dedicated buddy and mentor, helping to ensure your experience is productive, engaging and gives you a genuine insight into what a career with K3 Tax Advisory could look like.

What You’ll Experience

Group Induction

You will spend the early part of your first week in London, where you will join interns from across K3 Advisory Group for a general induction and have the opportunity to start building your professional network as part of a group social activity.

You will also spend time with the K3 Tax Advisory team, receiving introductory training. This will prepare you to contribute to real client work throughout your internship.

Your buddy will meet with you to help you set objectives for the programme.

Real Client Work

You will work alongside K3 Tax Advisory colleagues on client assignments, undertaking tax work similar to that expected of a first-year graduate trainee. This is designed to give you a realistic understanding of what a graduate career with us involves. This could involve assisting in preparing tax technical reports, researching points of tax law, drafting client correspondence, sitting in on client meetings, etc.

Your buddy will support you throughout the programme and help you work towards the objectives established during your first week.

Alongside your client work, you will prepare a final presentation to deliver towards the end of your internship.

Professional Development

Together with fellow interns from across K3 Advisory Group, you will take part in shared learning modules covering areas including:

· Professional skills

· Networking

· Wellbeing

These sessions are designed to develop skills that will support you throughout your career.

Programme Wrap-Up

In the last few days of your internship, you will spend another few days in London with our other interns, rounding off your Internship Programme.

Your Path to Our Graduate Programme

If, following your internship, you decide you would like to pursue a career in tax, you may be offered a place on our three-year Graduate Programme starting in September 2028, subject to achieving a 2:1 degree.

We aim to let successful interns know as soon as possible following completion of the programme.

About You

To be eligible for the Internship Programme, you must be in the penultimate year of your degree and expect to achieve at least a 2:1.

You will also need:

  • At least three A Levels at grades A–C, or the Scottish Advanced Higher/Higher equivalent
  • GCSE English Language and Mathematics at grades 9–6, or Scottish National 5 equivalent at grades A or B
  • Confidence working with numbers and strong attention to detail
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills
  • The ability to understand and communicate complex information clearly
  • Curiosity and a willingness to ask questions
  • The motivation to investigate problems and find answers
  • A strong sense of pride in the quality of your work
  • A genuine desire to help clients and their businesses succeed

You do not need to have studied tax before joining us. We are looking for people who are curious, motivated to learn and interested in developing a career in professional services.

What We Offer

  • Paid, hands-on professional experience within a specialist tax advisory business
  • Exposure to real client assignments and work typically undertaken by graduate trainees
  • Transferable professional skills and structured learning modules

· Support from a dedicated buddy

  • Opportunities to network with fellow interns, experienced professionals and leaders from across K3 Advisory Group

· Flexible, primarily remote, working

  • A clear potential pathway to our three-year Graduate Programme, starting September 2028

Start Your Career in Tax with K3

Our Internship Programme is designed to give you more than an introduction to the workplace. You will experience genuine client work, learn from experienced professionals and develop the skills and confidence needed to begin a career in tax.

If you are curious, comfortable working with numbers, keen to learn and want to understand how tax influences real business decisions, we would like to hear from you.

jobs.description:
Telestream is a leading provider of digital media tools and software solutions for the broadcast, streaming, and media industries. We empower content creators and distributors to produce and deliver high-quality video content while optimizing operations and maximizing revenue. Our teams work diligently to innovate and support world-class services, and we are looking for a Senior Technical Support Engineer to join our support team.

Technical Support Engineer – Content Management (DIVA)

  • Department: Support – Content Management
  • Reports To: Manager, Technical Support – Content Management
  • Classification: Individual Contributor
  • Experience: Typically 3–5+ years of technical support or related experience, ideally in a B2B software, storage, or media technology environment
  • Location: US Remote ; global support environment

**Work Authorization - Candidates must be legally authorized to work in the United States. This role is not eligible for employer-sponsored work authorization or visa sponsorship of any kind, now or in the future.

Role Summary

  • The Technical Support Engineer – Content Management is responsible for providing post-sales technical support to customers using Telestream’s Content Management products, with a focus on DIVA, Telestream’s video archive management platform. Customers rely on these systems to archive, protect, and retrieve their most valuable media assets across disk, LTO tape, and cloud storage. This role handles troubleshooting, issue tracking, escalation, and resolution across on-premises and cloud-connected archive deployments, maintaining clear and professional communication with customers throughout the case lifecycle.
  • This is a technically oriented support role, not a call center position. The Technical Support Engineer works directly with customers to diagnose product and infrastructure issues, replicates problems in lab environments, runs database queries and reads application logs as part of the diagnostic process, and collaborates with Engineering when issues require software fixes or product changes. The role requires the ability to understand media workflows spanning multiple systems, such as asset management, storage, tape libraries, and networks, and to determine when to escalate issues to senior team members, subject matter experts, or Engineering.
  • The Technical Support Engineer coordinates closely with the Professional Services (Delivery) team to manage handoffs between implementation and support, and back to Professional Services when customer issues require additional delivery engagement. This role must participate in an on-call rotation to support Telestream’s global customer base. Strong adherence to SLAs (first response and resolution times), accurate case documentation, and disciplined use of Salesforce, Jira, and Confluence are essential to this role.

Key Responsibilities

Technical Troubleshooting and Issue Resolution

  • Provide technical support to customers using the DIVA platform, including its archive, restore, partial restore, copy, and delete operations.
  • Diagnose and resolve issues across the archive environment, including the DIVA software, databases, source and destination storage, tape libraries and drives, cloud storage targets, and the networks that connect them.
  • Troubleshoot integrations between DIVA and customer media asset management, production, and automation systems, such as Avid Interplay and other third-party applications that use DIVA’s APIs.
  • Take ownership of customer issues from initial contact through resolution, including trouble ticket generation, incident diagnosis, root cause analysis, and customer communication throughout the case lifecycle.
  • Replicate customer issues in lab environments to isolate root causes, using database queries, log analysis, and product configuration review as part of the diagnostic process.
  • Identify hardware and software failures that can be addressed through patches, upgrades, configuration changes, or solution redesign, and document findings clearly for Engineering.
  • Maintain strong adherence to SLA targets for first response and resolution times, ensuring service objectives are consistently met.
  • Review assigned cases daily, update each with current status and next steps, and keep customer communication timely and clear.

Escalation and Cross-Team Coordination

  • Determine when to escalate issues to senior staff or subject matter experts within the support team based on complexity, severity, or product area expertise.
  • Prepare clear, well-documented escalation packages for Engineering when issues require software fixes or product changes, including steps to reproduce, error reports, log data, configuration files, and environmental details.
  • Coordinate with the Professional Services (Delivery) team to manage handoffs between implementation and support, ensuring customers experience continuity when transitioning between teams.
  • Follow associated Jira development tickets, follow up with Engineering when progress stalls, and provide logs, configuration files, or other data as requested.
  • Communicate with Sales and Renewals teams regarding licenses, expired support, or project-related issues.

jobs.title: Vice President of CRM, Lifecycle & Automation
jobs.excerpt: Position: Vice President of CRM, Lifecycle & Automation Status: Full-Time / Permanent / Exempt Reports To: Chief Growth Officer Location: Remote (U.
jobs.description:
Position: Vice President of CRM, Lifecycle & Automation

Status: Full-Time / Permanent / Exempt
Reports To: Chief Growth Officer
Location: Remote (U.S.)
Salary: $200,000-$240,000 Per Year
Incentives: Annual Bonus + Equity

The Opportunity

This is a new, senior role reporting directly to the Chief Growth Officer, building and owning the CRM, lifecycle, and marketing-automation engine for the SavATree brand. Where our demand team fills the top of the funnel, you own what happens next with your northstar metric being long-term customer lifetime value (LTV). You will set the lifecycle and retention strategy that moves it, across a strong foundation of retention above 80% and over a third of revenue already recurring.

You will operate as a super-senior individual contributor — owning strategy and driving execution yourself. This isn't for everyone, but for the right person it's the way they prefer to work. You'll stand up and in some cases modify our lifecycle programs end to end — email and SMS journeys, retention and prepay campaigns, cross-sell and reactivation, winback, and automated review generation — on a modern stack (Braze, Dynamics, Hatch), pulling the data you need yourself from Snowflake.

A defining feature of this role: because so much of our customer experience happens at the local level, your work drives action well beyond the inbox. The lead scores and signals you build will trigger not just emails and texts, but actions taken at the branch and in the field. We're looking for someone who sees around corners on how AI and automation reshape the funnel and the customer experience, and who has the taste and technical depth to build this function from the ground up.

What you'll own

The LTV mandate & strategy

  • Own long-term customer LTV as your core KPI and set the lifecycle and retention strategy to move it
  • Own cancellation / winback timing and approach company-wide, and measure the outcomes
  • Establish lead scoring that drives action across the org, which will drive not just emails and texts but also call center and local salesperson prioritization and action
  • Operationalize personalization and segmentation so the right SMS/email/call reaches the right customer at the right time
  • Set direct-mail strategy for retention and winback, activated by the growth channel leader

Programs, platform & measurement

  • Email / SMS lifecycle programs and customer journeys
  • Retention, prepay, cross-sell, and reactivation programs
  • Marketing automation & administration (Braze, CDP)
  • Customer data, audiences, segmentation & suppression
  • Identify any gaps in event streams needed for triggers and partner with Technology team to stand them up
  • Automated customer notifications that improve the service experience (appointment and service scheduling, reminders, post-service notification)
  • AI embedded into flows, reporting, and creative generation
  • Automated review-generation engine
  • Measurement on all lifecycle campaigns – focusing on sales activity (appointments and purchases, not open rates and clicks)
  • NPS / CSAT measurement and closed-loop learning

Where you'll partner

You'll collaborate across the business to action the plan that maximizes LTV and growth:

  • VP Growth: fills the top of the funnel and activates the retention/winback direct mail you set strategy for
  • Director of Brand & Integrated Marketing: owns the campaign calendar, offers, and creative you deploy through lifecycle channels
  • Technology team: Snowflake, data pipelines, and the ERP/CRM systems your programs run on
  • Sales & Operations: local actions your lead scores trigger
  • Finance: LTV measurement

Your team

This role is built for a super-senior individual contributor: you'll own strategy and drive execution yourself, with contractor and agency support (including existing Braze support) and deep enough data and technical chops to unblock yourself. You can leverage agency/contractor support as needed. We’ll expect that you’ll eventually take on CRM & Lifecycle for our Thrive house of brands division (20+ lawn care focused brands), which would come with bringing on additional support for you.

Why you'll love this role

You get to build. This is a greenfield opportunity to stand up the lifecycle and CRM engine for a scaling, category-leading company that has the data that has high growth expectations and the organizational ability to move quickly. We are data-driven, with access to the data you'll need to succeed. This role's executive sponsor operates with a highly aligned, loosely coupled approach to people management — the person in this role will have the latitude to move fast because they exhibit superior judgment and strategic thinking behind their decisions.

The right candidate has expertise in:

  • Retention, lifecycle, loyalty, or subscriber marketing — with a quantifiable track record of moving LTV via xsell/upsell/winback
  • Standing up lifecycle where the data wasn't ready — scoping a minimum viable event set, partnering with data engineering, and shipping flows off clean triggers
  • Designing and building email/SMS journeys, segmentation, and personalization that drive conversion and retention
  • Using AI in production — not just in experiments — to automate flows, reporting, or personalization
  • Enterprise CRM (e.g., Salesforce, Microsoft Dynamics) and a modern ESP (e.g., Braze, Klaviyo, Iterable)
  • Deep data and technology chops to unblock yourself — using data tables in Snowflake to build the audiences you need and the pipelines to your tools
  • Retention and lifetime-value programs — prepay, cross-sell, reactivation, referral, winback
  • Review-generation / reputation automation (a plus)
  • B2C multi-location / field-based business (a huge plus)

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree
  • 8+ years in retention, lifecycle, loyalty, or subscriber marketing
  • Has operated as a senior leader (Sr. Director / VP or equivalent) in a B2C environment
  • Quantifiable track record of moving a primary LTV or retention metric at scale
  • Deeply analytical — lifetime value, cohort / retention, funnel conversion, and incrementality
  • Hands-on with a modern martech stack (enterprise CRM + ESP) and comfortable in a data warehouse (Snowflake)
  • Strong project-management skills and attention to detail, with the ability to run many programs simultaneously
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills — experienced in executive presentation
  • Track record collaborating with cross-functional teams — Technology, Sales, Marketing, and Finance

Approach to the role

  • Treats LTV like their own P&L and works backward from it relentlessly
  • Sees the full customer journey, not just the inbox
  • Ships and tests fast
  • Strong judgment: a clear point of view on what good lifecycle looks like that is founded on customer strategy
  • Comfortable as a super-senior individual contributor: owns strategy and drives execution, and prefers to work that way
  • Creates lightweight process where needed to simplify
  • Low ego: you focus on team wins and care little who gets credit
  • High ambition: you do great work because it’s core to who you are
  • Thrives in ambiguity and a fast-changing environment

jobs.excerpt: OverviewNakupuna Companies is looking for a Splunk ITSI Engineer.
jobs.description:
Overview

Nakupuna Companies is looking for a Splunk ITSI Engineer. Lead the architecture, deployment, configuration, and operationalization of Splunk IT Service Intelligence (ITSI) for Naval Supply Systems Command (NAVSUP) Business Systems Center (BSC). The engineer will work with the existing Splunk team to bring security and IT data into a unified monitoring view, improve visibility into service health, reduce alert noise, and help teams identify issues before they disrupt operations. This role will build service health models, alert aggregation policies, and dashboards that reflect vulnerability management priorities and the organization’s risk posture.

Responsibilities

The following reflects management’s definition of essential functions for this position. Management may assign additional duties and responsibilities to this job at any time due to reasonable accommodation or other reasons.

  • Lead the design, installation, hardening, configuration, and operationalization of Splunk ITSI in coordination with the existing Splunk engineering team.
  • Ingest and normalize security, application, and infrastructure telemetry from disparate data sources; assess log quality, field consistency, and collection methods.
  • Define ITSI entities, services, key performance indicators (KPIs), thresholds, and dependencies to provide proactive service health monitoring.
  • Develop and tune Notable Event Aggregation Policies (NEAP) to correlate related events, reduce duplicate alerts, and support incident investigation.
  • Build Glass Tables, Deep Dives, and executive dashboards that present real-time service health, trends, and operational risk.
  • Align service health models and alerting with vulnerability management priorities in consultation with Government cybersecurity and operations stakeholders.
  • Configure and troubleshoot related Splunk searches, alerts, reports, visualizations, add-ons, and data onboarding within the existing platform.
  • Support secure configuration and access controls in accordance with applicable DoD and DON requirements, DISA STIGs, and the Risk Management Framework.
  • Validate data flows, ITSI calculations, dashboards, and event grouping; refine configurations as operational needs evolve.
  • Document architecture, configurations, standard operating procedures, lessons learned, and best practices; provide training and knowledge transfer to NAVSUP BSC personnel.
  • Provide weekly status updates on work completed, remaining tasks, dependencies, and issues.

Qualifications

Skills/Qualifications:

  • Experience designing, installing, administering, and troubleshooting Splunk ITSI in a Splunk Enterprise environment.
  • Ability to model IT services, entities, KPIs, health scores, thresholds, and dependencies that reflect operational priorities.
  • Experience with ITSI Glass Tables, Deep Dives, Event Analytics, Notable Event Aggregation Policies, and Episode Review.
  • Strong Splunk Search Processing Language (SPL) skills and experience developing searches, alerts, reports, dashboards, and data models.
  • Experience onboarding, normalizing, and correlating logs and telemetry from security, application, and infrastructure systems.
  • Knowledge of Splunk forwarders, search and deployment servers, clustered indexers, add-ons, and data collection methods such as Syslog, JDBC, and APIs.
  • Experience with Linux and Windows environments and with Splunk configuration files, field extractions, lookups, and access controls.
  • Ability to work with Government cybersecurity and operations teams on vulnerability priorities, secure configuration, continuous monitoring, auditing, and reporting.
  • Experience developing technical documentation, training users, communicating progress, and resolving dependencies across teams.

Education and Experience: A bachelor’s degree in a technical field, such as engineering or computer science, is required. Experience in Government or DoD environments is desired.

Clearance: Must be able to obtain a Top Secret clearance and be a U.S. Citizen.

Certification:

This position requires:

  • CompTIA Security+ CE certification or an equivalent certification approved for the position.

Additionally, candidates must have ONE of the following Splunk certifications; the ITSI certification is preferred:

  • Splunk IT Service Intelligence Certified Admin (Legacy)
  • Splunk Enterprise Certified Admin
  • Splunk Enterprise Certified Architect
  • Splunk Cloud Certified Admin
  • Splunk Enterprise Security Certified Admin
  • Splunk Certified Developer

Job Description:

We are GDIT. We stay at the forefront of innovation to solve complex technical challenges.

GDIT is your place. Make it your own by discovering new ways to apply the latest technology and processes. Own your opportunity at GDIT and you’ll be a meaningful part of improving how agencies operate. Our work depends on a Committee Operations Lead joining our team to lead IT professionals supporting the Health Resources & Services Administration (HRSA).

The Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA) aims to improve health outcomes by enhancing access to quality services, developing a skilled health workforce, and implementing innovative programs that benefit geographically isolated, economically or medically vulnerable populations. HRSA focuses on increasing health equity and strengthening local health systems through initiatives such as community health centers, the Organ Procurement & Transplantation Network (OPTN), the Ryan White HIV/AIDS Program, and support for maternal and child health.

At GDIT, we foster a people-centric environment. The Committee Operations Lead will manage and facilitate the activities of Organ Procurement and Transplantation Network (OPTN) committees, including subcommittees, workgroups, and ad hoc groups. This role ensures that committees responsible for membership, patient safety, and policy development operate efficiently, transparently, and in alignment with statutory, regulatory, and policy-driven goals.

The Committee Operations Lead functions as a pivotal project manager, policy facilitator, and liaison, supporting committees in their critical decision-making, managing governance documentation, streamlining meeting logistics, and collaborating with internal and external stakeholders. They also support the development and implementation of evidence-based transplantation and allocation policies, ensuring compliance with HRSA and federal regulations.

This role combines project management expertise, policy analysis skills, and regulatory knowledge to deliver high-quality support to committee operations and optimize system performance. In this role, the responsibilities of the Committee Operations Lead will include:

  • Lead and support OPTN committees tasked with membership oversight, patient safety, and policy development.

  • Oversee the schedule and facilitation of committee meetings, develop detailed agendas, prepare support materials, and lead discussions in a manner promoting collaboration and timely decision-making.

  • Collaborate with committee chairs and leadership to ensure accurate tracking of activities, timely communication, and seamless facilitation of committee initiatives.

  • Fully implement a Committee(s) Meeting Facilitation Plan that ensures secure, efficient, and compliant virtual meetings, including maintaining schedules, technical support, and post-meeting documentation (recordings, minutes, summaries).

  • Develop, implement, and maintain the Committee(s) Management Plan, which outlines procedures for tracking committee activities, milestones, composition, and outputs.

  • Create and maintain governance documents, operational manuals, and SOPs related to committee structures, member selection processes, decision-making responsibilities, and conflict-of-interest logs.

  • Prepare public-facing materials highlighting committee activities, accomplishments, and membership, ensuring transparency and alignment with organizational goals.

  • Support policy development by identifying opportunities to improve organ transplantation and allocation policies through evidence-based research and committee-led initiatives.

  • Draft policy proposals, guidance documents, public comment reports, and board recommendations based on committee deliberations and feedback.

  • Collaborate with OPTN committees and stakeholders to ensure all proposed policies align with federal regulations (e.g., CMS, HRSA). Maintain thorough documentation for policy audits and regulatory reporting.

  • Analyze quantitative and qualitative data (using tools such as Excel, Tableau, or NVivo) to support committee decision-making and policy recommendations.

  • Provide detailed reports and dashboards on committee outputs, performance trends, and policy impact to OPTN leadership, HRSA, and other stakeholders.

  • Track and monitor committee projects and policy proposals through all stages (inception to implementation), ensuring alignment with public comment periods and board approval timelines.

  • Act as the primary point of contact for committee members and stakeholders, facilitating communication, responding to inquiries, and resolving operational challenges.

  • Engage with the broader transplant community to gather input, understand concerns, and encourage collaboration in policy discussions and system improvements.

  • Collaborate with external contractors, OPTN support teams, and other divisions, such as IT and policy experts, to facilitate seamless coordination across all committee activities.

  • Lead the development of the Committee(s) Training Plan, which provides onboarding, annual training, and up-to-date resources for committee members.

  • Ensure training materials address committee structures, workflows, regulatory requirements, and membership expectations.

  • Deliver virtual training sessions and maintain a secure repository of training recordings and resources.

  • Implement the Subject Matter Expertise Plan to identify, onboard, and track expert contributors across clinical, analytical, policy, and risk management domains.

  • Ensure timely and sustained access to experts who support committee initiatives related to membership evaluation, patient safety reviews, and policy recommendations.

WHAT YOU'LL NEED

  • Bachelor’s degree in Public Health, Public Policy, Health Administration, Business Administration, or a related field. Master’s degree (MPH, MPP, MHA) is preferred.

  • At least 5+ years of experience in committee coordination, project management, or policy development.

  • Experience in healthcare, compliance, regulatory, and/or nonprofit environments, especially in roles requiring meeting facilitation and multi-stakeholder engagement.

  • Proven ability to lead virtual committee meetings, guide collaborative decision-making, and manage cross-functional initiatives.

  • Strong understanding of policy drafting, federal regulations, and evidence-based research to inform recommendations and decisions.

  • Proficiency in quantitative and qualitative data analysis, with tools such as Tableau, NVivo, and Excel.

  • Familiarity with healthcare regulations (e.g., CMS, HRSA) and experience ensuring policies meet federal and organizational requirements.

  • Exceptional written and verbal communication abilities, with a focus on preparing detailed reports, agendas, and governance materials.

  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (SharePoint, Teams), virtual meeting platforms, and committee documentation systems.

  • Excellent attention to detail, time management, and multitasking in fast-paced, deadline-driven environments.

  • Must be able to obtain a Public Trust clearance

About Crosswalk Health, Inc.

At Crosswalk Health, we are reshaping pulmonary care delivery by empowering primary care providers—especially those in rural and underserved communities—to better manage chronic conditions like COPD while reducing overall healthcare costs. COPD is the third leading cause of death in the U.S., a major driver of hospital admissions, and responsible for over $60 billion in annual costs.

Our Mission is to deliver high quality, virtual-first, guideline-based pulmonary care at scale to measurably improve Americans’ respiratory health. We are working toward a health care system that provides patients, their families, and the clinicians who care for them access to affordable, high quality, and data-driven care and supports regardless of where they live.

Key Responsibilities

  • Scheduling & Coverage: Manage regional RT schedules, coordinate absences and schedule changes, resolve call-out coverage needs, and arrange backup or float coverage when available.
  • RT Support: Serve as the primary contact for routine operational questions, communicate updates and expectations, support new RTs, and escalate recurring performance or attendance concerns to Operations Leadership.
  • Clinic Relationships: Maintain strong relationships with clinic managers, address routine scheduling and operational concerns, and communicate changes affecting clinic operations.
  • Clinical Support: Continue performing scheduled spirometry services while serving as a resource for routine workflow, equipment, technology, and documentation questions.
  • Regional Oversight: Monitor staffing and coverage needs, identify potential service disruptions, participate in operational check-ins, and provide weekly updates to Operations on staffing, coverage, clinic concerns, and other relevant issues.
  • Other duties may be assigned as necessary to meet business and operational needs.

Decision-Making & Escalation

The Regional Lead is expected to independently resolve routine operational issues, including scheduling adjustments, call-out coverage, routine clinic communication, and coordination with available float RTs.

Hiring and termination decisions, formal discipline, payroll, compensation, contract negotiations, major client escalations, and HR matters remain the responsibility of Operations leadership. Significant or unresolved issues should be escalated promptly.

Qualifications

  • Active Respiratory Therapist credentials and all required state licensure
  • Strong clinical performance and understanding of spirometry
  • Demonstrated reliability and attendance
  • Excellent communication and organizational skills
  • Ability to manage changing schedules and priorities
  • Strong problem-solving and decision-making skills
  • Comfortable communicating directly with clinic managers and healthcare professionals
  • Ability to remain calm and solution-oriented when unexpected issues occur
  • Strong knowledge of Crosswalk workflows and expectations

What Success Looks Like

  • Consistent and dependable clinic coverage.
  • Timely resolution of routine scheduling and operational issues.
  • Strong relationships with RTs and clinic partners.
  • Proactive identification and communication of regional concerns.
  • Consistent clinical quality and minimal need for day-to-day intervention from Operations.

Compensation Structure

Regional Leads receive a recommended starting leadership stipend of $750 bi-weekly, in addition to their established daily rate of $245-$300 for clinical spirometry service.

Regional Lead stipends may vary based on the size and complexity of the assigned region, including the number of clinics, RTs, scheduled clinic days, customers, and overall operational workload.

More than 700,000 members across three continents have completed over 10 million AI sessions, helping 1,000+ enterprise clients avoid more than $1 billion in unnecessary healthcare costs.   • Experience working with brokers, consultants, or health plan partners in the benefits ecosystem.

jobs.excerpt: What we're doing at UscreenUscreen is the video monetization platform for businesses building recurring revenue from video content.
jobs.description:
What we're doing at Uscreen

Uscreen is the video monetization platform for businesses building recurring revenue from video content. Our customers replace a patchwork stack of separate hosting, community, courses, email, and app vendors with one branded experience across web, mobile, and TV.

The platform is only half of it. We believe growth requires behavior, not just software. Customers don't stall because a feature is missing. They stall because they priced wrong, never built an email list, or launched an offer nobody wanted. Coaching is how we fix that, and it's part of the product rather than an add-on.

The job

You own a segment.

We have a cohort of smaller video businesses where retention is not where it should be. Nobody owns it today. You will. That means the revenue that stays in that segment, and the revenue that grows inside it, is yours. Your lemonade stand, your numbers, your call on how to run it.

This is a coaching role measured in dollars. You'll be accountable for gross revenue retention in your cohort first, and expansion second. Not tickets closed, not calls booked.

It's also a one-to-many job. Your cohort is larger than a 1:1 book, so the work is designing coaching that scales: cohort programs, group sessions, office hours, triggered outreach when the data says a business is drifting. You'll build that motion rather than inherit it.

What you'll do

  • Own gross revenue retention and expansion for an assigned segment of customers
  • Find the pattern in why businesses in your cohort stall, and build coaching that addresses it at scale rather than one conversation at a time
  • Run group coaching sessions, cohort programs, and asynchronous coaching inside Membership+
  • Coach customers through the decisions that move revenue: pricing, packaging, positioning, offer design, email and funnel strategy, retention mechanics
  • Read your own data. Spot the accounts drifting before they churn, and know which interventions actually worked
  • Build the playbooks and session formats that make this repeatable. You're the first person in this seat, and what you build becomes how we scale it
  • Bring what you learn back to Product and Success. You'll be closer to this segment than anyone at the company.

Who we're looking for

Someone who has grown something online and can explain how. Maybe you ran marketing for a small business, coached founders, built your own audience, or worked inside a membership or subscription business. What matters is that you can sit with an operator, see the real constraint, and say the honest thing.

  • 3 to 5 years in coaching, consulting, customer success, or digital marketing, with real ownership of an outcome
  • Comfortable advising solo operators and small teams on how to grow
  • Strong live facilitation: group sessions, workshops, webinars, 1:1 calls
  • Can read a dashboard and form a point of view on retention curves, cohort behavior, and funnel conversion
  • Working fluency with AI tools for research, prep, and synthesis. Our team uses Claude daily to prep sessions, analyze customer data, and build coaching assets. You don't need to be technical, but you should reach for these tools rather than around them.
  • Motivated by being paid on results. A third of this package is variable and there's no ceiling on it.
  • Clear, simple communication. Complex idea in, plain sentence out.

Bonus points if you:

  • Have been a creator, coach, or small business owner yourself
  • Have worked with video businesses, online educators, or subscription and membership businesses
  • Know the surrounding stack: Kit/ConvertKit, YouTube, Kajabi, Circle, Squarespace, Meta and IG
  • Have built a scaled or one-to-many customer program before

What's hard about this job

We'd rather you know now.

  • You'll own a number you can't fully control. Some customers won't take the advice and will churn anyway. You have to be able to own influence over an outcome rather than the outcome itself.
  • It's a lagging metric. Retention moves slowly. Your first two quarters are guaranteed at target because of this, but you'll be doing the work for months before the number reflects it.
  • The motion doesn't exist yet. Playbooks exist for our 1:1 coaching. The scaled version for this segment is an open question you'll help answer. If you need a finished playbook on day one, this will frustrate you.
  • You'll deliver honest assessments to people emotionally invested in what they've built. That takes a specific kind of nerve.

What we offer

  • 100% remote first company
  • Flexible PTO + 8 company holidays
  • Remote, global team
  • Paid parental leave
  • Medical, dental, and vision (US Based)
  • Technology and home office stipend
  • Coworking space stipend
  • Annual learning stipend

Note: Benefits may vary depending on location and local regulations. Final eligibility and coverage details will be shared during the hiring process.

jobs.description:
About Perle

Perle is an AI infrastructure company building expert-driven training data, evaluation systems, and applied AI products for the world's leading labs and enterprises. Headquartered in San Francisco with experts across more than forty markets, we specialize in the work that requires real human judgment: domain expertise, linguistic nuance, and cultural fidelity that generic data vendors cannot deliver.

Imagine earning extra money without changing a thing about your day. No second shift, no commute, no time away from the work or the life you already have. You film what you are already doing, and you get paid for it.

Perle is building the data that teaches AI and robotics how real people move, work, and get things done. To do that, we need video recorded from a first-person point of view: the world as you see it, through a small camera mounted on a lightweight headstrap. We are looking for contributors across the Indonesia & Malaysia to capture everyday footage and turn their ordinary routines into real income.

What You'll Actually Be Doing

The role is simple: you wear a headstrap with your phone, press record, and go about your day. The footage is captured hands-free from your perspective, so you can keep both hands on whatever you are doing.

Contributors record everyday activities and real work. That includes things like:

  • Household life: doing tasks around the house, cooking, cleaning, organizing, repairs, and other daily routines.
  • On the job: filming while you do your actual job, whether you work in manufacturing, roofing, construction, a restaurant kitchen, a warehouse, or any other hands-on trade.
  • Everyday activities: the small, ordinary moments that make up a normal day, captured naturally as they happen.

There is no script and no acting. The whole point is authentic, real footage of real life. If you can do your job and your daily tasks, you can do this.

Why This Is Worth Your Time

  • Earn while you already work: Record while you work or while you handle things at home. Your day does not change; you just capture it.
  • Total flexibility: There are no fixed shifts. You decide when to record and how much. The more quality footage you submit, the more you earn.
  • Real, steady income: Pay is competitive and varies by region. You are compensated for every hour of accepted footage you deliver.
  • We cover your gear: Perle provides a budget to purchase the headstrap you need to get started, so the equipment is covered.

The primary purpose of the Senior Pricing Manager is to provide end to end support to the Head of Pricing across product pricing, pricing governance, fair value assessments, commercial deal management, and profitability analysis. They will be responsible managing key strategies initiatives from analysis to execution working closely with the Commercial Management team and senior leaders across the organisation.
They are to operate as a “second in command” to the Head of Pricing acting as a delegate and key point person for functional partners in Finance, Risk, Product, Strategy, Commercial and Operations ensuring pricing decisions are data-driven and aligned with business objectives.
The role holder is to operate in a self-sufficient manner, leveraging resources and expertise across the business without relying on dedicated team beneath them to deliver outcomes. As such they must take a ‘hands on’ approach to their work, being comfortable moving between strategic thinking, detailed analysis and execution.
The role therefore requires an individual with strong commercial judgement and analytical capability combined with the drive, judgement and delivery focus to get into the detail when required, independently navigate complexity and see work through to completion.

Key Accountabilities:
  • Pricing strategy: Support Head of Pricing to develop and maintain the firm's pricing strategy and pricing framework. Proactively identify enhancements and seek continuous improvement in the function.
  • Pricing Governance: Responsible for ensuring pricing policies, methodologies and controls remain fit for purpose and aligned with regulatory expectations. Provide content for governance forums such as Customer Outcomes Committee and Cash Interest Share Forum.
  • Product pricing and commercial support: Support product-level pricing reviews and recommendations. Support proposition development through pricing analysis and commercial modelling.
  • Deal analysis and implementation: Support Distribution with processing, tracking and reporting on firm level discounts/deals as per deals framework.
  • Pricing Insight: Provide subject matter expertise to support business performance, firm/customer profitability and pricing effectiveness. Assess pricing impacts on customer outcomes, profitability and growth objectives.
  • Financial analysis: Support strategic decision making through commercial and financial analysis including identification of actions to improve deal performance, mitigate income erosion, drive growth and improve margin.
  • Re-platforming: Support the Head of Pricing in designing and implementing the migration pricing strategy for customers and advisers transitioning from Nucleus Wrap and Curtis Banks platforms to the Nucleus platform.
Knowledge, Skills and Experience:

Essential
  • Experience in commercial finance, profitability analysis or related analytical disciplines.
  • Advanced analytical and financial modelling skills.
  • Ability to interpret complex data and translate findings into commercial actions.
  • Strong organisation skills and capacity to collaborate with multiple stakeholders across different projects.
  • Ability to independently identify and resolve issues, develop robust recommendations, manage stakeholders and mobilise expertise to deliver.
  • Understanding of pricing strategy, pricing governance and commercial decision-making.
  • Experience developing and presenting recommendations to senior management.
  • Resilient, with the ability to work independently and take the initiative.
Desirable
  • Experience within financial services or other regulated environments.
  • Knowledge of Consumer Duty, Fair Value Assessments and customer outcome requirements.
  • Experience of pricing systems, product management platforms or transformation programmes.

  • Experience managing cross-functional projects and business change initiatives.
  • Relevant professional qualification in Finance, Analytics, Economics or a related discipline.
Values and Behaviours:
  • Positively demonstrate the Nucleus values and behaviours
  • Ensure compliance with Code of Conduct at all times

A little about us 
We’re the Nucleus Financial Platforms group and we help make retirement more rewarding.
People come first - whether it’s our colleagues, or the advisers and customers we support, we know that working in partnership and collaboration leads to the best outcomes. Together, we’ve shaped the platform to how it is today. We work hard, and we celebrate hard too. 
Our ambition is to create a platform with a difference, putting the customer centre stage meant tearing up the rule book and starting from scratch. We’ve come a long way since then, but our mission remains just as focused. That’s why our culture, values, and social responsibility are things we keep at the top of our agenda – because we know they matter and have a big impact. 
Our culture is one of the many things that sets us apart from the pack. We want to have an environment where our people feel that they can make a real difference, know they’ll be rewarded for their efforts and more importantly, enjoy themselves at work. 
Inclusion and diversity at Nucleus 
As with most things in life, who cares, wins. We really care about inclusion. 
For us it’s not a tick box exercise; inclusion and diversity are embedded in our culture and everything we do. It’s a commercial imperative. It isn’t about being PC. It’s about being future-relevant and durable. We owe it to ourselves and the industry to ensure we are playing our part in creating a fair, balanced and transparent financial services sector. 
More diversity means broader experience, a wider set of perspectives and a better collective ability to problem-solve. And it means being more representative of customer groups, which supports areas such as product development.

Our culture is one of belonging.
We strive to be transparent and accountable. We believe in equipping our associates with the knowledge and resources they need to be successful. No matter where you’re at in the organization, you’re an integral part of our team and your input, thoughts, and ideas are valued.

Join others who value a workplace for all.
We appreciate and celebrate everything that makes us unique, from personal characteristics to past experiences. Our different perspectives strengthen us as an organization and help us better serve all Rhode Islanders.

We’re dedicated to serving Rhode Islanders.
Our focus extends beyond providing access to high-quality, affordable, and equitable care. To further improve the health and well-being of our fellow Rhode Islanders, we regularly roll up our sleeves and get to work (literally) in communities all across the state—building homes, working in food pantries, revitalizing community centers, and transforming outdoor spaces for children and adults. Because we believe it is our collective responsibility to uplift our fellow Rhode Islanders when and where we can, our associates receive additional paid time to volunteer.

Why this job matters:

Responsible for leading end-to-end technical integration of BCBSRI’s core administrative systems, utilization management platforms, clinical data sources, enterprise data platforms, FHIR services, electronic health record systems, and external healthcare trading partners. Serves as the hands-on technical lead for interoperability and clinical data integration initiatives, ensuring the reliable, secure, and efficient exchange of clinical and administrative data across internal and external systems. Supports compliance with CMS interoperability requirements and the development of broader enterprise clinical data capabilities. Defines and guides integration approaches across APIs, FHIR services, data pipelines, middleware, messaging, batch interfaces, and event-driven solutions. Leads technical enablement of Patient Access, Provider Access, Provider Directory, Payer-to-Payer exchange, and electronic Prior Authorization capabilities, including CRD, DTR, and PAS workflows. Applies advanced healthcare integration expertise across core administration and utilization management systems, EHRs, HIEs, clinical data repositories, enterprise FHIR platforms, cloud data platforms, API gateways, and external health plan and vendor platforms.


What you will do:

  • Lead the design and delivery of secure, scalable integrations across core administration, utilization management, clinical, enterprise data, FHIR, EHR, HIE, and external partner platforms.
  • Define reusable integration patterns for APIs, batch processing, messaging, event-driven solutions, transformation, routing, orchestration, error handling, and reconciliation.
  • Lead FHIR R4 solutions supporting Patient Access, Provider Access, Provider Directory, Payer-to-Payer exchange, and electronic Prior Authorization using applicable Da Vinci, US Core, CARIN, CDS Hooks, and SMART on FHIR standards.
  • Direct the ingestion, transformation, mapping, validation, and reconciliation of clinical data from EHRs, HIEs, laboratories, providers, and vendors, ensuring data quality, provenance, and traceability.
  • Design and optimize cloud-based APIs, integration services, and data pipelines across Azure, Snowflake, Apigee, and related technologies, including CI/CD and secure authentication and credential-management practices.
  • Manage technical integrations with vendors and trading partners, including solution review, connectivity, onboarding, end-to-end testing, production readiness, and resolution of risks and dependencies.
  • Establish testing, monitoring, logging, alerting, and incident-management standards; lead root-cause analysis and remediation of complex integration and data failures.
  • Maintain technical documentation and provide technical direction to engineers, analysts, and vendor resources while coordinating decisions across Product, Engineering, Data, Architecture, Security, Infrastructure, and Operations.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

What you need to succeed:

  • Seven or more years in systems integration, software engineering, data integration, or interoperability engineering, including three to five years focused on healthcare interoperability, clinical data exchange, or HL7/FHIR integration.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, Health Informatics, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and related work experience.·
  • Demonstrated experience implementing FHIR R4 APIs in a payer, provider, healthcare technology, or healthcare services environment, including hands-on integration with health plans, EHR vendors, HIEs, or UM vendors.
  • Strong working knowledge of HL7 FHIR R4, HL7 Da Vinci guides (PDex, CRD, DTR, PAS, Plan-Net), US Core, CARIN Blue Button, CDS Hooks, and SMART on FHIR.
  • Working knowledge of HL7 v2, C-CDA/CCD, REST APIs, JSON/XML, and healthcare messaging, plus integration patterns spanning batch, real-time, asynchronous, event-driven, and publish/subscribe.
  • Strong understanding of payer data domains — member, coverage and eligibility, claims, encounters, provider, clinical, utilization management, and prior authorization — and familiarity with Facets or comparable core administration platforms.
  • Hands-on experience with cloud integration and data technologies (Azure Data Factory, Azure Functions, Snowflake, Azure SQL, ADLS) and API gateway platforms (Apigee, MuleSoft, Azure API Management).
  • Strong SQL skills for profiling, validation, mapping, reconciliation, and troubleshooting; working knowledge of OAuth 2.0, JWT/JWKS, mutual TLS, certificate management, and external API security.
  • Experience with source control, CI/CD, automated deployment, and integration observability including logging, monitoring, alerting, and tracing.
  • Excellent analytical, documentation, and communication skills, with the ability to translate business and regulatory requirements into technical integration designs and to explain complex concepts to business stakeholders.
  • Demonstrated stakeholder and vendor management skills, comfort in Agile, Waterfall, and hybrid delivery models, and a strong ownership mindset for production reliability and data quality.

The extras:

  • Experience with a health plan, provider organization, or healthcare interoperability technology company.
  • Direct experience supporting CMS interoperability initiatives and implementing ePA workflows involving CRD, DTR, PAS, CDS Hooks, and UM platforms.
  • Experience integrating with major EHR platforms (Epic, Oracle Health/Cerner, athenahealth, eClinicalWorks) and with HIEs, ADT feeds, laboratory feeds, C-CDA documents, and clinical APIs.
  • Familiarity with X12 healthcare transactions such as 270/271 and 278.
  • Relevant certifications such as HL7 FHIR, Azure Solutions Architect or Developer, AWS, MuleSoft, or Apigee.
  • Experience with operational dashboards and monitoring (Grafana, Azure Monitor/Application Insights, Power BI) and incident management platforms such as ServiceNow

Location:
BCBSRI is headquartered in downtown Providence, conveniently located near the train station and bus terminal. We actively support associate well-being and work/life balance and offer the following schedules, based on role:

  • In-office: onsite 5 days per week
  • Hybrid: onsite 2-4 days per week
  • Remote: onsite 0-1 days per week. Permitted to reside in the following states, pending approval from the Human Resources Department: Arizona, Connecticut, Florida, Georgia, Louisiana, Massachusetts, North Carolina, Oklahoma, Rhode Island, South Carolina, Texas, Virginia

Our culture of belonging at Blue Cross & Blue Shield of Rhode Island (BCBSRI) is at the core of all we do, and it strengthens our ability to meet the challenges of today’s healthcare industry. BCBSRI is an equal opportunity employer.

jobs.excerpt: About North-Star CareNorthStar Care (NSC) is a startup founded in 2020 focused on providing comprehensive, next generation, virtual treatment to patients suffering from Alcohol Use Disorder (AUD).
jobs.description:
About North-Star Care

NorthStar Care (NSC) is a startup founded in 2020 focused on providing comprehensive, next generation, virtual treatment to patients suffering from Alcohol Use Disorder (AUD). The company uses cutting edge genetic and diagnostic testing to create personalized treatment plan for every patient. All patient appointments are performed via telehealth and care coordination is orchestrated seamlessly using North-Star Care’s mobile app. Peer support sessions are performed from the comfort of the patient’s home using virtual reality for a 100% anonymous experience.

NSC is a US-based, 100% remote company that welcomes and encourages diversity of all kinds. NSC is committed to recruiting; training and supporting staff who identify as Black, Indigenous and People of Color; bicultural/bilingual Spanish. As a company, we are committed to undoing systems of oppression and the harms they have caused. We actively work toward building an anti-racist environment and a sense of belonging.

To learn more about North-Star, visit

Job Overview

The Peer Guide serves as a compassionate, patient-centered support specialist within NorthStar’s multidisciplinary Care Team. Drawing on personal lived experience with Alcohol Use Disorder (AUD) and Substance Use Disorder (SUD), the Peer Guide walks alongside patients as they navigate their own path of healing and transformation. This role embodies NorthStar’s core belief that healing happens in relationship, and that every individual is the expert of their own recovery journey.

The Peer Guide provides both individual and group support through NorthStar’s virtual engagement platforms, including telehealth and virtual reality (VR), ensuring a trauma-informed, harm reduction-oriented presence throughout every interaction.

Organizational Context

NorthStar is a 100% remote behavioral health organization founded in 2020, providing next-generation virtual treatment to adults with Alcohol Use Disorder and Substance Use Disorder and co-occurring conditions. NSC integrates pharmacogenomic testing, remote biometric monitoring, virtual reality therapy, and AI-assisted care coordination to deliver personalized, evidence-informed treatment at scale.

NorthStar is deeply committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion, and actively recruits, supports, and develops staff who identify as Black, Indigenous, and People of Color, and/or who are bicultural or bilingual in Spanish. We are an anti-racist organization dedicated to dismantling systems of oppression in behavioral health care.

Essential Responsibilities

The following responsibilities reflect the core functions of the Peer Guide role. Additional duties may be assigned consistent with organizational needs for peer support services.

Direct Peer Support Services

  • Engage patients in a strengths-based, trauma-informed manner, affirming each person as the expert of their own healing and recovery goals.
  • Provide individual peer support via telephone, video conferencing, and Virtual Reality (VR) platforms, connecting with patients at least weekly during initial treatment phases.
  • Facilitate and co-facilitate virtual peer support groups and recovery-focused educational sessions, including VR-based group programming.
  • Share personal lived experience with AUD and SUD authentically and appropriately to motivate, encourage, and reduce stigma for patients.
  • Support patients in identifying and pursuing personal recovery goals, building on individual strengths and resiliency.
  • Assist patients with community networking, resource navigation, and bridging to community supports and services.
  • Advocate with and on behalf of patients to ensure their voices are heard and their rights are upheld throughout the course of care.

Care Team Collaboration

  • Function as an active member of NorthStar’s four-person interdisciplinary Care Team, participating in care coordination, team huddles, and collaborative treatment planning.
  • Communicate patient needs, observations, and concerns to the clinical team in a timely, professional manner, maintaining appropriate boundaries and confidentiality.
  • Align all peer support activities with the patient’s identified treatment plan, as developed and updated by the clinical team.
  • Contribute to the organization’s quality improvement efforts by providing input on peer support service design, delivery, and outcomes.

Organizational Engagement

  • Use your lived experience voice to inform NS’s ongoing efforts to improve care quality and reduce systemic harm in behavioral health treatment.
  • Participate in mandatory orientation and ongoing training programs, including training on peer support principles, HIPAA and 42 CFR Part 2 confidentiality, trauma-informed care, harm reduction, and NorthStar’s clinical technology platforms.
  • Attend and contribute to organizational meetings, staff development activities, and peer workforce engagement initiatives.
  • Maintain a flexible schedule including availability for evening, weekend, and holiday coverage as operationally required.

Documentation and Compliance

  • Complete timely and accurate documentation of peer support contacts, group sessions, and patient interactions in accordance with NorthStar’s Clinical Documentation Policy.
  • Maintain strict confidentiality of patient information in compliance with HIPAA, 42 CFR Part 2 (SUD-specific confidentiality protections), and applicable state laws.
  • Adhere to NorthStar’s Code of Conduct, Ethics and Corporate Compliance Policy, and peer-specific ethical boundaries as outlined in organizational policy.
  • Report concerns related to patient safety, critical incidents, or compliance issues through established reporting channels.

Requirements

    • Lived Experience: Personal lived experience with Alcohol Use Disorder (AUD) and/or Substance Use Disorder diagnosis and/or treatment. This is a non-negotiable foundational requirement of the Peer Guide role.
    • Commitment to Harm Reduction: Demonstrated support for a harm reduction philosophy, including an all-paths-to-recovery approach, and respect for patient autonomy and self-determination.
    • Communication Skills: Strong verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to engage empathetically and effectively in a remote environment.
    • Technology Proficiency: Demonstrated comfort with or strong interest in virtual engagement tools, including video conferencing platforms, mobile applications, and virtual reality technologies.
    • Reliability and Flexibility: Ability to maintain a flexible schedule, including evenings, weekends, and holidays, and to respond consistently to patient engagement expectations.

Preferred

    • Certification as a Peer Specialist, Recovery Coach, or equivalent credential recognized at the state or national level (e.g., Certified Peer Specialist, CCAR Recovery Coach).
    • Formal training or coursework in peer support principles including mutuality, self-determination, healing in relationship, and recovery-oriented systems of care
    • Lived experience as a Veteran, or experience providing peer support to Veterans or military-affiliated individuals.
    • Bilingual proficiency in Spanish and English.
    • Experience in a remote, telehealth, or technology-forward healthcare setting.

Background Check

  • All offers of employment are contingent upon successful completion of a background check in accordance with NorthStar’s Staff Background Checks and Exclusion Checks Policy and applicable state requirements. A criminal record (CORI) does not automatically disqualify candidates from consideration for this role. NS evaluates criminal history on an individualized, job-related basis.
  • Working Conditions
    • Environment: 100% remote; employees must maintain a private, professional workspace suitable for confidential patient interaction via telehealth and virtual reality platforms.
    • Schedule: Full-time (40 hours/week). Schedules include evening and weekend hours. Specific schedules are determined in coordination with the CSO.
    • Technology Requirements: Reliable high-speed internet connection, webcam-equipped computer, and ability to operate VR hardware (training provided). NS provides relevant software access.
    • Physical Demands: Primarily sedentary work performed at a computer workstation. May involve extended periods of screen use.

Benefits

  • Paid Time Off (Vacation, Sick Leave, and Public Holidays)
  • Training and Professional Development
  • Work From Home
  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP) — see HR for current program details
  • Additional benefits as outlined in the NorthStar Care Employee Handbook

Overview

Lumicera Health Services is seeking a Supply Chain Contracting Manager to join our team!

The Supply Chain Contracting Manager develops, negotiates, and manages contracting strategies that reduce the total cost of goods and services for Clarventa and its GPO member pharmacies. This role focuses on high-impact pharmacy supply chain categories, including logistics and last-mile delivery, cold-chain and packaging, pharmacy technology, and credentialing. By aggregating member volume, the Manager secures preferred pricing, favorable terms, and sustainable savings that individual pharmacies may not achieve independently.

This is a high-level individual contributor role with significant ownership and influence across contracting strategy, supplier negotiations, and category performance. The Manager owns a portfolio of supplier agreements and category strategies, initially focused on supply chain and cost-of-goods programs, and potential expansion into additional strategic initiatives that support Clarventa’s broader cost, access, and value objectives. This is a supplier-facing negotiation and contracting role, represents Clarventa in the market, leads sourcing and negotiations, manages supplier performance, and ensures negotiated savings are successfully delivered to member pharmacies. Working closely with a small, high-performing team and cross-functional partners, the Manager helps advance Clarventa’s mission of delivering more efficient and transparent contracting solutions.

Is this you? Find out more below!

Responsibilities

How do I make an impact on my team?

  • Represent Clarventa in the market as a supplier-facing contracting leader for supply chain and cost-of-goods categories.
  • Lead end-to-end sourcing and negotiations with vendors and suppliers to secure competitive pricing, favorable terms, and reliable service for GPO member pharmacies.
  • Develop and execute category strategies and action plans that expand savings, strengthen contract structures, and enhance partner value.
  • Build and manage a portfolio of vendor relationships and agreements, converting vendor interest and preferred-pricing opportunities into signed, executed agreements that deliver measurable value.
  • Monitor supplier performance and promote accountability to contract terms, service levels, and expectations.
  • Uphold high contracting standards and ensure the timely, accurate execution of agreements.
  • Ensure negotiated pricing and renewals are reliably extended to eligible members.
  • Identify opportunities to aggregate member volume, standardize terms, and drive continuous improvement in category performance and cost competitiveness.
  • Partner with leadership to assess, plan, and launch new supply chain and cost-of-goods initiatives.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams, including analytics, finance, operations, contract operations, compliance, and legal, to support contracting objectives.
  • Ensure all vendor and supplier agreements align with legal, regulatory, and industry standards, including anti-kickback, transparency, and reporting requirements.
  • Support compliance program objectives, and contribute to people, learning, and culture programs across the function.
  • Willingness to travel up to 10% of the time to support business needs.
  • Other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

What our team expects from you?

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Supply Chain, or a related field, or equivalent work experience, required. MBA or other relevant advanced degree preferred.
  • Professional procurement, contracting, or supply management certification (e.g., CPSM) preferred.
  • 7+ years of experience in procurement, supply chain, vendor contracting, category management, or sourcing required.
  • 3+ years of direct contract negotiation experience with demonstrated, quantifiable savings or value delivered required.
  • Experience building new programs, categories, or functions, with comfort operating under ambiguity, pressure, and tight timelines, strongly preferred.
  • Experience with group purchasing organizations (GPOs) is highly preferred. Candidates should understand the group purchasing organization model, including how aggregated member volume creates negotiating leverage and how value is delivered back to member pharmacies.
  • PBM or specialty pharmacy experience preferred.
  • Strong financial acumen, including cost modeling, total-cost-of-ownership analysis, and interpretation of pricing constructs.
  • Participate in, adhere to, and support compliance program objectives.
  • The ability to consistently interact cooperatively and respectfully with other employees.

What can you expect from Lumicera?

  • Top of the industry benefits for Health, Dental, and Vision insurance
  • 20 days paid time off
  • 4 weeks paid parental leave
  • 9 paid holidays
  • 401K company match of up to 5% - No vesting requirement
  • Adoption Assistance Program
  • Flexible Spending Account
  • Educational Assistance Plan and Professional Membership assistance
  • Referral Bonus Program – up to $750!

About the Role

At Pavago, one of our clients is hiring a Sales Service Representative to support inbound sales inquiries and provide exceptional customer service to individuals exploring debt settlement and debt consolidation solutions.

This is a customer-focused, consultative sales role where you’ll primarily engage with prospective clients who have already expressed interest in the company’s services. You’ll listen to their needs, understand their financial situation, explain available options, and guide them through the next steps with professionalism and empathy.

You’ll also manage ongoing lead follow-up and conduct outbound outreach when needed to ensure prospective clients receive timely support throughout the sales process.

If you enjoy helping people, building trust, and guiding customers through important financial decisions, this role is a strong fit.

What You’ll Own

Inbound Sales & Customer Support

  • Answer incoming calls from prospective clients interested in debt settlement and debt consolidation services
  • Understand each prospective client’s financial situation and needs
  • Provide accurate information about available programs and financial solutions
  • Guide prospective clients through appropriate options
  • Answer questions clearly and professionally
  • Deliver an empathetic, consultative, and customer-focused experience
  • Build trust while handling sensitive financial conversations

Lead Follow-Up & Outreach

  • Maintain consistent communication with prospective clients throughout the sales process
  • Conduct outbound follow-up calls when required

  • Build strong relationships with potential clients

  • Track lead progress through the sales process
  • Ensure follow-ups are completed on time
  • Maintain organized and accurate client information
  • Handle sensitive customer information professionally and confidentially

Team Collaboration

  • Share customer feedback and insights that may improve the sales process
  • Collaborate with team members to improve customer experience and sales effectiveness
  • Stay informed about company offerings and processes
  • Maintain awareness of relevant industry trends and compliance requirements

Requirements

  • Previous experience in sales, customer service, call center, or another client-facing role
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills in both English and Korean
  • Strong interpersonal and relationship-building abilities
  • Professional phone presence and active listening skills
  • Strong organizational and time-management abilities
  • Comfortable handling sensitive financial conversations professionally and confidentially
  • Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with a team
  • Experience using CRM systems or customer management software

  • Ability to work during U.S. business hours

    • Debt consolidation
    • Lending
